The atmosphere is great and the service was great too. The food was lovely as amongst us, have 4 platters, i think, or they had other food ordered too. All taste really good, accompanying fries, salad, sauces. The drinks were refreshing after having the meal. The staff were great and kind to assist. Will hopefully visit again.

places.name: Ottoman
places.formatted_address: 193 Fulham Palace Rd, London W6 8QX, UK
places.editorial_summary: Classic Turkish meze, charcoal-grilled kebabs and fish to eat in a no-frills space or take away.

reviews.text:
This was such a London find!

The service was outstanding: we sat down and immediately got a small salad and bread, a type of attention that is harder and harder to find nowadays. Our waitress was also speedy and friendly.

We got the mixed grill and every piece of meat was cooked to perfection. It was served over a piece of pita that soaked the juices and became a delicious bite.

The grilled eggplant was also very good, fantastic to mix in with yoghurt (also great to mix in with the rice).

Finally, they gave us tea and baklava for free. Going back is certain.

The doner made here is not Turkish. The taste and quality is mediocre at best.
Service and setting is good. Definitely a big gap if anyone thinks this I a Turkish doner. It was not worth me making the effort to come here.

This is hands down the best Turkish restaurant in Fulham! The food was absolutely delicious — everything was fresh, flavorful, and cooked to perfection. The atmosphere was warm and welcoming, making it a perfect spot for both casual meals and special occasions. What made the experience even more memorable was the outstanding service. Moh, in particular, was incredibly kind and attentive. His friendliness and genuine care for the guests truly made us feel at home. I highly recommend this place — you won’t regret it!

Easily one of the best doner shops I’ve been to. The meat was perfectly seasoned, fresh, and juicy, and the portion sizes were generous. The salad and sauces complemented the wrap beautifully without overpowering the flavor. Staff were friendly, service was quick, and everything was clean. Great value for money — definitely my go-to spot for a proper döner.”

I came for lunch, plenty of tables available and seated right away. Service from the stuff was excellent, very friendly and helpful recommending stuff. Bread, salad and dips were brought to the table as a complimentary starters which is always nice. The main meal came out fairly quick, we ordered few dishes like the lamb kofte, chicken and lamb doner (not the usual style roll) all the food was delicious and tasted fresh. Everything else from the chips and drinks (not fresh juice but from a box) were also good.

The quality of the food was fantastic. Some restaurants I've eaten claim to use lamb but often can be mutton, but not this one. These guys use very good quality ingredients. My Yogürtlu Shish was fantastic. The lamb was incredibly tender and juicy. I'll be coming back just for this alone. The service was reasonably good. I think they could be a little more attentive and check everything is ok. They did however offer cup of Turkish tea on the house which was really helpful after such a hearty meal, a nice added touch at the end.
A job well done!

First time eating here and I was truly impressed by the size and the taste of the food. Super delicious, fresh, generous. A must try in the area 100%

And thanks to Mohamed and all his team!

Absolutely loved this place! The Turkish food was delicious and came in really big portions—great value for money. The staff were super friendly and made us feel right at home. The atmosphere was cozy yet vibrant, perfect for a relaxed meal with friends or family. Fun experience overall, and we’ll definitely be back to try more dishes!

Extremely Disappointing Experience – Would Strongly Recommend Avoiding This Restaurant

I rarely leave negative reviews, but our recent visit to this small Turkish restaurant was so shockingly poor that I feel compelled to share our experience in full detail, hoping it might help others avoid the same mistake.

From the moment my partner and I walked in, it was clear that something was off. The atmosphere was unwelcoming and the service — or rather, the complete lack of it — was one of the worst I have experienced in any restaurant in London, or anywhere else for that matter.

Let me begin with the staff attitude, which was simply appalling. The person who approached our table to take our order didn’t even bother to greet us. No “hello,” no “good evening,” nothing. Just a blank stare, followed by silence as if we were an inconvenience rather than customers. This wasn’t a case of someone being shy or overworked — it was plain rudeness. When we said thank you after giving our order or when receiving something at the table, the waiter didn’t respond at all. No smile, no nod, not even eye contact in most cases — just an indifferent, cold look.

In my culture — and in Turkish hospitality too — mutual respect and warmth are the foundation of good service. Turkish restaurants are usually known for their welcoming atmosphere, generosity with bread, and attentive service. This place, however, seems to have entirely missed that memo. I don’t expect over-the-top pampering, but basic human courtesy is the minimum anyone should expect from hospitality staff.

Speaking of bread, let’s talk about the extra charge for additional bread — something I have never seen in a Turkish restaurant before. Bread is often complimentary in Middle Eastern and Turkish dining, especially when the meals are served with dips or grilled meats. Here, not only were we charged extra for a small basket of bread, but there was also no mention of this when we asked for it. It was only when the bill arrived that we noticed the charge. While it’s not about the money, it’s the principle: being transparent with customers and not exploiting basic expectations like bread with a meal.

Now, about the food quality. At best, it was average. Nothing particularly bad, but certainly nothing special or memorable either. The meat was a bit dry, the salads lacked freshness, and the seasoning was inconsistent. I’ve had far better meals in takeaway kebab shops than what we were served here. For the price we paid, the value was seriously lacking.

And yes — the pricing. For a small, casual restaurant with mediocre food and poor service, the bill was surprisingly high. The dishes are priced as if you’re dining in a high-quality, fully-staffed Turkish restaurant with excellent ambiance and a pleasant experience — when in fact, the experience was more like eating in a disinterested diner that just happens to serve Turkish food.

To be clear, the real issue wasn’t just one specific thing, but the overall experience:
•	The unwelcoming attitude from the staff
•	The absence of any basic manners
•	The surprise charge for something that should be complimentary
•	The underwhelming food
•	The high price tag for what we received

All of this combined made for an experience that left a bad taste in our mouths — both literally and figuratively.

Unfortunately, this restaurant seems to lack even the most basic understanding of customer service.

To anyone considering visiting this place, my honest advice is: don’t waste your time or money. There are plenty of wonderful Turkish restaurants across London where the food is authentic, the prices are fair, and — most importantly — the staff genuinely care about your experience.

This was one of those rare meals where we left not just unsatisfied, but genuinely frustrated. A dinner that should have been an enjoyable evening out for me and my partner turned into a disappointing memory that we won’t soon forget — not because of the food, but because of how we were treated.

Absolutely not recommended.

Great food - we shared the Adana kebab and chicken wings and they were both delicious. You get bread and side salad complimentary and the salad is a plate each so no need to share! Chilli and garlic sauce also complimentary and were very nice. Prices are good, £15 for the Adana kebab which is very reasonable for quality and portion.

places.name: Selale Restaurant
places.formatted_address: 1-2-3, Salisbury Promenade, Green Lanes, Harringay Ladder, London N8 0RX, UK
places.vicinity: 1-2-3, Salisbury Promenade, The Coliseum, Green Lanes, London
places.editorial_summary: Bright, simple dining room with tiled floors, for traditional menu of Turkish kebabs and meze.

reviews.text:
Door-to-door kindness and service, just like being hosted by a Turkish family.

The warm and competent service started right at the entrance, and there was never a “no” to any of my requests.

I ordered the Turkish breakfast, which is world-famous and often rated as the best breakfast in the world.
I truly enjoyed the traditional spread with sucuk, olives, different kinds of cheese, börek, and more — and of course, unlimited Turkish tea.

I can highly recommend this place to anyone who wants to experience genuine Turkish hospitality and delicious food.

Great job, guys 👌

Upon entering till leaving Selale the customer service has just been exceptional, the servers are friendly, warm and welcoming.

The Selale special platter was delicious and enjoyable.

The only thing I found strange was the price of the chips and soft drinks, very high in price for something that was not exclusive nor special. However that would not stop me from coming back haha.

At the end of our dinner me and my family were served Turkish tea and baklava on the house and the baklava was just delectable! Absolutely tasty it was.

I would recommend this place, family friendly, kid friendly and a relaxing atmosphere.

Thank you for your exceptional service Selale.

Excellent food and beautiful restaurant. The mix meze and fresh orange juice were unreal.  Our meal was topped off with the amazing service we received from Ahmet. We only needed to lift our heads away from our plates and he was there making sure we was happy. The complimentary Turkish tea and baklava at the end was the cherry on top. Can’t wait to go back!

Wonderful Turkish dining experience!  Soooo much food was served we had to take home as it was so delicious.  Staff were very attentive and quick.  Lamb chops and moussakka were probably the best weve ever had.  Had lots of laughs as we tried Raki liqueur after dinner.  Definitely will return!
The food was simply amazing! We got both of the large platters and it served 12 people (kids and adults). The flavors were delicious. 10 out of 10 recommend!

places.name: Midpoint Restaurant
places.formatted_address: 3, Anchor Iron Wharf, Ballast Quay, London SE10 9GL, UK
places.vicinity: 3, Anchor Iron Wharf, Ballast Quay, London
places.editorial_summary: A menu featuring classic Turkish cuisine & drinks in modern, rustic setting with hanging plants.

reviews.text:
We visited a Turkish restaurant by the Thames in Greenwich. The food was very tasty, and the portion sizes were just right. The presentation was nice, and everything was fresh and well-cooked. The staff were friendly and gave great service.

We had our meal in the garden. It was beautiful and peaceful. There are special flowers in every season, and everything is very well cared for. We asked the owner, and he said his father takes care of the garden as a hobby. It was a lovely experience.

The restaurant has a nice view on the river as you approach it, the staff is friendly, quick and helpful. They have great portion sizes. I ordered the mixed kebab and sigama boregi which where all very lush, I like that the borek came with some chilli jam and the salad that came w the kebab had pomegranata which was refreshing. Cocktails are great too here, not too strong but also not a faint taste. Honestly, no complaints and I'd 100% return here.

This place is set in a lovely location by the river. The decor is appealing and the seating is well planned. All staff are immaculately dressed. Went with some friends and we ordered the Turkish breakfast. The waiter took time to listen to our orders and requirements. The food didn’t take too long to come and was presented beautifully. The only thing that I would say could be improved were the eggs. I asked for runny yolks, not snotty, but they came overcooked. That’s the only thing I would say needed improvement. Nice low level of music in the background so you don’t have to talk loudly at all. Overall, a lovely experience.

Really happy with our experience today! We went for a late lunch (3pm) and the staff were really friendly, food was amazing and it was a great atmosphere. We ordered sharing platters of mezes and mixed grill and it was was delicious. The chicken shish was amazing. Cocktails were great too. Can't fault it; eager to go back. Thanks Team Midpoint!

Lovely Turkish brunch...

Great restaurant with lots of seating and can accommodate large groups.

Breakfast / brunch menu was amazing. The Turkish breakfast for 2 had more than enough food, could easily feed 3.

Plus, the menu has something for everyone.

Highly recommend.

places.name: Zahter
places.formatted_address: 30, 32 Foubert's Pl, Carnaby, London W1F 7PS, UK

reviews.text:
Yummyyy! Loved the Ali Nazak (ground beef and lamb with aubergine). The pastry with spinach was good too. The garlic labneh and the bread was such a good starter.

Slightly on the higher price side.

Nice restaurant in a good location in London.
The food was all tasty, but a little overpriced for the quantity. It would have definitely been nice to have more bread or the waitress to explain that we should have ordered two of them.
The waiting staff generally were very inattentive. We were never asked if we wanted more drinks, and we had to go inside to pay because no one was around.
Overall, the food is delicious but the price is too high for the level of service and portions.

The overall quality was good enough, though I noticed the food portions have become smaller compared to last year. For a Middle Eastern/Turkish restaurant, where bread is usually an essential part of the dining experience, it felt strange (and a bit disappointing) that no bread was offered with the meal. When we asked, the staff weren’t very accommodating, so we ended up buying toast from a nearby shop just to feel satisfied.

The flavours are still enjoyable and the atmosphere is nice, but small details like this make a big difference, especially in a place that should feel warm and generous by nature of its cuisine.

All the food was more than expected! In particular, baklava with kaymak was the best I experienced. The fish and shrimp dish was really nice. It is on the pricy side, but worth trying! The staff there was also very kind and polite.

Zahter is a total gem in the heart of Soho. Unique flavors you don’t come across often.  The service was warm and on point from start to finish, and for the quality, it felt like real value. Booked through The Fork!

For mains, the wood-fired prawns were a standout: succulent, garlicky, with a subtle kick from Aleppo chili and a rich lemon butter sauce. The beef fillet skewers were tender and juicy, complemented by a smoky paprika butter. The sea bream was beautifully cooked, flaky, and paired wonderfully with chimichurri. Highly recommend!

places.name: Riviera
places.formatted_address: 23 St James's St, London SW1A 1HA, UK

reviews.text: Celebrated my birthday at Riviera on Saturday. It was absolutely amazing! Our waitress Gayu was so lovely and her attention to detail was impeccable. She made the most amazing martini and she also made me feel really special. My seabass was delicious and myself and my guest loved this restaurant. Also to mention the decor is stunning!!! I highly recommend riviera!

I celebrated my birthday at Riviera and couldn’t have asked for a better experience. The food was absolutely delicious, beautifully presented, and full of flavor. A special thank you to Omar, who went above and beyond with his impeccable service. He was professional, attentive, and made the evening feel extra special. Truly a memorable experience, highly recommend Riviera!

An absolutely exceptional fine dining experience from start to finish. Every detail, from the ambiance to the presentation of each dish, was flawless.

A special thanks goes to Omar, who elevated the evening even further with his outstanding service. He was attentive without being intrusive, knowledgeable and ensured every moment of our dining experience felt special. His warm professionalism made us feel truly valued as guests.

Without a doubt, one of the finest dining experiences I’ve had in London— highly recommended for anyone seeking excellence in both cuisine and service.

Absolutely fantastic experience! The food was delicious, beautifully presented, and full of flavor. The service and hospitality were outstanding -  warm, attentive, and made us feel truly welcome. The restaurant is thoughtfully designed, creating a wonderful atmosphere that elevated the whole evening. A special mention to Riad, who went above and beyond to ensure everything was perfect. Overall, it was brilliant from start to finish. Highly recommend to anyone looking for an exceptional dining experience!

Everything from the food to the service was bang on. We ordered the lobster pasta and pesto pasta and the lobster pasta stole the show. It was DIVINE. Paxci and Omar took such good care of us and were lovely. Can’t wait to come back!

places.name: Brasserie Zedel
places.vicinity: Twenty Air Street, 20 Sherwood St, London
places.editorial_summary: Grand French art deco restaurant with classic brasserie dishes and choucroutes in 1930s building.

reviews.text:
After being swept away by the glitz and glamour of Moulin Rouge the musical, we had a dinner booking at the Brasserie Zédel, a perfect match to the show. While waiting for our reservation, we had drinks in their bar, Bar Americain, which was an experience in itself, moody lighting, classic cocktails, and a vibe that whispered old-school elegance. It was the ideal spot to decompress and relive our favorite moments from the show.

Once seated in the brasserie, the atmosphere shifted into full Parisian charm. The grand Art Deco dining room is stunning, like stepping into 1930s Paris. The menu was classic French fare, with comforting favourites. Everything we ordered was delicious and beautifully plated, and the service was warm and friendly.

Brasserie Zédel isn’t just a meal, it really is an experience. Whether you’re coming from the theatre or just looking for a slice of timeless sophistication in the heart of London, it’s a place that delivers on ambiance, flavor, and charm.

We came here for dinner, and had a great time.

Although reservations are not necessary, I would really recommend doing so at least 1 hour in advance.
The food tasted fantastic, and there was a large selection of individual dishes and set menus.
The service was also very good. The staff members were really friendly and helpful at all stages, and even provided us with slightly modified dishes without an allergen.
The atmosphere is also great. Although the entrance is in a medium-sized cafe, the restaurant itself is located in a massive basement.

Overall, the place was pricey, but a very nice experience.

A really great dining experience. I chose the starter, main, and dessert preset menu. Everything I had was amazing but I really enjoyed the pea and mint soup. The staff was professional and hospitable. If you have the opportunity to experience a meal here do not pass it up. I went for lunch and there was a really nice band to provide entertainment. The band wasn’t too loud and you were able to have an easy conversation at the table as well.

Good food & perfect ambiance for a romantic evening. Good to go. The music can be continued till the 10 pm though. I added the reservation note that we are going to celebrate some special updates of business. They gave a special sweet, ıt was so cool! Thanks again for an amazing dinner

Service impeccable, friendly yet professional. Prices very decent for the area.

The attention to detail is vast and deep, no expense spared, it’s not a few details here and there it’s an immersive experience.

Came for a cabaret show and was not disappointed! Drinks high quality, performance high quality, over all a brilliant place bringing real energy.

places.name: Bouchon Racine
places.formatted_address: Upstairs, 66 Cowcross St, London EC1M 6BP, UK

reviews.text: Beautiful setting. Staff couldn’t be more helpful. We thought the mustard in our ham and celeriac starter & the rabbit was just too overpowering. The terrine and steak were excellent though. Great wine recommendations from the staff paired perfectly with our food and the dessert she recommended was our favourite dish of the night.

Came here for a birthday dinner with my partner, and the experience was truly exceptional!

The food was absolutely delicious, where the calf brain stood out as an especially memorable dish. The snails, lamb, and pheasant were all super delicious.

On top of that, the serving was absolutely excellent, where the waiter was incredibly helpful, friendly, and nice.

It was such an enjoyable experience that we booked in our next visit for my birthday dinner before we left.

Very highly recommend place, and I would argue it is the best place to eat in the area!

Had a wonderful experience at this restaurant!
Everything was delicious — each dish was prepared with great care and full of flavour.
The atmosphere was top-notch — cozy, stylish, and very welcoming.
Service was excellent — friendly and attentive staff.
I really enjoyed it! 💫

We ate delicious food. The servers deserve full marks for their knowledge of the products, their sincere and friendly service. My only criticism is that the steak tartare was a bit pale. The crème caramel was truly wonderful. All the dishes had a balanced flavor; the anchovy tomato salad, pâté, and deviled eggs were all delicious.

Love it, love it! Amazing food, impeccable service, great prices and lovely atmosphere. Though I live a little far away from their location, I will certainly frequent it and endure the longer-than-usual car ride.
Though I paid over £100 per person, I ordered a large amount of food so that I try the tastefully curated menu.  Dave, the co-owner was most hospitable and made the night speciall

places.name: 64 Goodge Street
places.vicinity: 64 Goodge Street, Greater, 64 Goodge St, London

reviews.text: Well presented and delicious food at a price. I had the pleasure of watching the chefs working from my seat which added to my experience. The waiters are quick and efficient and they serve half bottles of wine in carafes which is a bonus.

I’m surprised this place has a Michelin star. The set menu was hit or miss. First course (duck and quail) was better than main course (pork and venison). The appetizers (snail and frog lollipop) and side dishes (pomme something) were extra costs, as tiny as the bouche amusee, not flavorful at all, and very greasy. The desserts were regular size and actually quite good. Drinks were okay…my sparkling wine had a tiny serving as well. Overall, would not recommend…for this price, you can get much better food elsewhere.

I recently celebrated my mum's birthday at this wonderful restaurant, and it was an experience to remember! From the moment we arrived, we were greeted warmly and shown to a our table.

The food was absolutely delicious. Each dish was bursting with flavour, and you could really tell that everything was made with care and quality ingredients. We enjoyed a variety of appetizers, mains, and desserts, and each course was better than the last. We have tried the snail bon bons, frog's leg lollipops, petite gougeres, smoked eel, quail forestiere, saddle of rabbit and the veal. For dessert we had the Rhubarb vacherin and Paris Brest. Everything was 10/10!

The service was impeccable. The staff were attentive, friendly, and really went out of their way to make sure we had everything we needed. It was clear they were genuinely focused on providing an exceptional experience.

What’s even more amazing is that I’ve been to this restaurant before, back in 2023 when they first opened, and even then, the food was absolutely amazing. It’s incredible to see how they’ve maintained such high standards and consistently delivered a fantastic dining experience. They definitely deserve their michelin star!

All in all, it was a fantastic experience, and I couldn’t have asked for a better setting to celebrate my mum's special day. Highly recommend this place to anyone looking for spectacular food and top-notch service!

It was a great dining experience at 64 Goodge Street in terms of atmosphere, attentive service, and overall quality. However, I found the food to be average, not quite above my expectations. We had the lobster and steak as our main dishes; both were decent, but there was no surprise in terms of flavour. The starters were similar, not bad, but lacking in harmony and depth, and nothing particularly memorable. The courgettes we had were way too salty, to the point of being unpleasant.

At this price point, I was hoping for something either novel or a truly exceptional take on a classic. While it was a lovely evening overall, the food didn’t quite match what I’d expect from a Michelin-starred restaurant.

The desserts were the highlight of the meal. I particularly enjoyed the crème brûlée with prune, which was simple but well done. The strawberry mille crêpe was also delicious and nicely balanced.

I probably wouldn’t return, but would still recommend it to someone looking for a stylish, intimate place to celebrate, especially if food innovation isn’t a top priority.

This place never disappoints, the food is amazing every time ♥
We’ve been four times now (and counting!) and have loved every visit. The only struggle is deciding what to order because everything is genuinely delicious (especially the quail for starters is just ♡!)
I brought my parents and brother today to celebrate their birthdays, and the team prepared three cards and three candles for us, such a thoughtful touch.
The service is always friendly and the vibe is cosy. For the price point in London, it’s 10/10. Can’t get enough of this place.
Sharing some of the photos from my past 4 visits!

places.name: La Palombe Kensington
places.formatted_address: 267 Kensington High St, London W8 6NA, UK
places.vicinity: Leonard Court, 267 Kensington High St, London

reviews.text: Don't have enough good things to say about this place, the food, the team, the atmosphere.  I had my birthday here and I can't imagine going anywhere else where literally everyone (with a lot of foodies) couldn't stop having about the food, combined with being so very well looked after by James and his outstanding team.  Every dish was perfection, great wines, outstanding service and wonderful people.  Thank you for making my birthday so special Palombe.  I hope I've helped send a few more loyal customers your way :).  I was having too much fun to take pictures of the delicious food on my birthday, but have plenty from our anniversary we also chose to celebrate here!

I absolutely love this restaurant. I’m sure this isn’t my first review, and it certainly won’t be my last. They update the menu quite often, but every dish I’ve tried has been excellent. It’s become my favourite restaurant in London. The prices feel very reasonable, especially given the quality of both the service and the food — well deserved.

We went here to celebrate our anniversary and had an amazing experience. The staff were friendly and welcoming, and the cocktails were amazing.

The venison croquettes were delicious. We had the octopus and duck leg for entrées, then venison and pork belly for mains – all were exceptional and full of flavour. Even the side of fries was the best we have ever had.

The chef even surprised us with a special treat at the end. Highly recommend – incredible food, excellent drinks, and wonderful service!

This is my second time having dinner here and never failed me. The whole atmosphere from start to finish was perfect. The food was amazing as before.  Will visit again for sure!

Just to say that I had beef tartare last night and I am perfectly fine. It was delicious!

Amazing French food in a lovely brasserie setting! We’ve probably eaten here 5-6 times since discovering La Palombe a year ago and the food has always been beautifully prepared every time. The venison croquettes and octopus are favourites, as are the venison and chicken ballotine. Warm and friendly service as well!

places.name: Le Relais de Venise L'Entrecote | Marylebone
places.editorial_summary: French restaurant, part of petite chain, serving set menu of salad, steak and fries plus dessert.

reviews.text: Enjoyed my first time experience at this popular restaurant. Waited for one hour for an early dinner. Arrived at 5.40pm before opening - there was already a large queue however it went fairly quickly considering. Security on hand to ensure everything ran smoothly. Guests were buying drinks at the restaurant bar next door which was nice (if that’s your thing whilst waiting). We were served by some lovely ladies who were organised - food came out quickly and we didn’t feel rushed. Nice authentic French brassiere feel. Loud but you can still hear each other. Chose medium for the meat which was nicely pink. Enjoyed the desserts too, not too sweet. If you’d like to get in early for dinner I’d say arrive at 5-5.15pm

I’ve been here many times, and I keep coming back — and will continue to do so. For starters, there’s a salad with mustard and walnut served with slices of baguette. The main course, of course, is the steak and fries it’s truly delicious. As for desserts, the profiterole and the tower-shaped version of it are great; the classic one tastes better, but the tower is perfect for sharing.

The service is excellent — the staff are very elegant, kind, and genuinely beautiful in the way they present themselves, and they always look so polished and well-put-together, which adds to the restaurant’s charm. Everything is clean,beautiful and well-organized.

The only downside is that it can get crowded and there can be a queue in the evenings and on weekends, and the tables are a bit small, but that’s understandable since it’s always busy inside. Definitely a place worth visiting not just once, but many times.

Wanted to visit this French steak house for a long time and eventually came with three friends.  It was Sunday after 1pm, we queued and waited for half an hour for a table, which was not too bad.  There only one set menu that covers bread, salad, steak and fries.  They offer one refill of steak and fries.  The food was good but not great.  The seat setting was very close to each others.  We had two bottles of house red at £27 a bottle, that was reasonable.  Unfortunately we didn't check the bill when we pay until two hours later when I looked at the photo of the receipt and found that they had charged us three bottles of red.

I actually like this place. Nothing to complain about. You get a starter, which is a salad with walnuts, two rounds of your steak and fries, good selection of wine, dessert for about £100 (for two people). Yes, you're crammed into the restaurant but you have to expect it when there is a queue going into the place most of the time. The service is fast, the food is delicious. If you don't make it in the first round of people, you'll end up waiting between 30-45 mins for a table.

First of all, I'd like to say that this is a restaurant in London that will definitely satisfy your hunger. Even though we arrived during dinner service, we waited in line for about 30-45 minutes. The restaurant was very elegant and crowded. All the wait staff we saw were women of various ages. The modest salad, a small bowl of lettuce, walnuts, and mustard, was wonderfully flavorful and filling. They told us they only cooked the meat medium or rare. They served half of the meat with plenty of fries and sauce. Then they served the rest of the meat and plenty of home-style potatoes. The wine they recommended and all the desserts were excellent.

places.name: L'Escargot Restaurant
places.editorial_summary: London's oldest French restaurant offering fine-dining classics in a grand Georgian townhouse.

reviews.text:
L’Escargot – London

We chose L’Escargot for dinner after learning it was one of Princess Diana’s favorite restaurants, and my wife insisted we try it. Our group of five had a 7 pm reservation.

Service: The staff was warm and friendly. Even though the restaurant wasn’t very busy that evening, service was on the slower side—something to keep in mind if you’re used to the faster pace of American dining.

Food:
•	Appetizers: The French onion soup was one of the best we’ve ever had—rich, flavorful, and perfectly comforting. The seafood lobster soup was creamy and indulgent. And of course, the escargot was excellent—the butter and green pesto sauce made it a standout.
•	Mains: The smoked haddock was not our favorite—it came in a heavy cheese-based preparation that wasn’t clearly described on the menu. On the other hand, the lamb was tender, flavorful, and highly recommended.
•	Dessert: If you plan to order a soufflé, do it early—it takes at least 30 minutes to prepare, but it’s worth the wait.

Extra Tip: Don’t miss the charming live piano bar upstairs—just follow the staircase after dinner for a lovely way to end the evening.

Overall, L’Escargot offers a classic French dining experience with standout starters and a touch of royal history. Perfect for a special night out in London.

This restaurant is always keeping in my pocket and go to enjoy the authentic French cuisine when I visit London. Although they not provide big variety of food, that’s enough for me. Great value on the meal set and the menu will be changed time by time. Price is reasonable in city centre and the service is attentive and professional. Remember to enjoy other glass of drinks with friends on their bar on top of the same building.
P.S. booking through open table which will have special steak+ champagne set offer.

We had the 3 course set menu for £28 each, which was fantastic value. The quality of the French onion soup, the fresh bread and the lemon tart were outstanding. The additional champagne offer of a whole bottle for £48 made it incredible value.

This is the oldest French restaurant in London and while the food may not be groundbreaking it was completely delicious. The early prix fixe is a great value. Breads are divine and you must try the cheese straws. The chocolate mousse dessert was a great finish to a really nice meal. This place will never be innovative and that's just fine.

What a fantastic restaurant! We had the most delicious lunch today, the service was impressive from front of house and throughout our visit we were so well looked after.
The venue is exactly what I like, quirky and stylish, and the atmosphere very relaxed. We spent 2 hours and could have stayed longer if we didn’t have flights to catch. Thank you so much!

places.name: Galvin La Chapelle
places.editorial_summary: Galvin La Chapelle's little sister, next-door to the gourmet spot, with a French/Italian cafe menu.

reviews.text:
I came here for dinner by myself.

Overall, this place has a Bailie, unique and magical ambience. The interior of an old chapel is one of the more unique and charming Settings for a restaurant that I have ever seen.

I will say that my expectations were very high, as a place has Michelin  star. Overall, the Service was very good, but not extraordinary. The food was excellent, but again – I was not as impressed with the food as I would have expected – I feel the food that I got at sketch. Two nights ago was much more, outstanding, and culinary. Perfect and unique.

Overall, I would be unlikely to return at the Price point, but it is a quality restaurant, and I do feel that it is deserving of it status.

Loved my experience here for a romantic date. The place itself is truly a vibe, I was mesmerised by the sheer size of the architecture. Our server was amazing and so attentive. We went for the tasting menu and it was so decadent and perde for the start of autumn. We loved everything but the desserts, they weren’t particularly outstanding.

We had dinner at Galvin La Chapelle and it was excellent. For a Michelin Star, the price for the summer special was very affordable. The dishes were all excellent. If you are starving, it might not have been quite enough food but it was all very tasty for a great price.

The service was also excellent here - warm and inviting.

I had the 7 course + 1 tasting menu with the wine pairings.  I have gone to many restaurants in my time and I would have to rate this one among the best.  The vegetarian tasting menu was inventive and decadent.  I thoroughly enjoyed every single thing.  The service level was world class.  Absolutely breathtaking building.  Go there now.

We had a birthday Sunday lunch here. The appetizer was exceptional, and we especially enjoyed the seabass. The sourdough with lemon and pepper butter was also delicious.

However, the main dishes were just fair. They were tasty, but we expected more from a Michelin restaurant. We were pleasantly surprised when the restaurant offered us a birthday dessert. Lovely!

places.name: Chez Bruce
places.editorial_summary: High-end Modern French dining, fine wines and an extensive cheese board in a simply decorated space.

reviews.text: Very impressed with the place. We tried a few dishes, and they were all very well executed. Special mention to the sea bass, which came with a beautifully balanced buttery and acidic sauce — very, very nice. The bread and focaccia were excellent as well. Everything was good, including the desserts. The restaurant's reputation is well deserved. I’d also add that, for what it is, lunch offers decent value. You could spend around £80–£100 per head, and I’d say that’s definitely fair for the level of food.

Incredible lunch! Not only the food was insanely delicious, but also the service was impeccable. Everyone is so nice, genuine and welcoming. Not wondering why the restaurant is there since a long time! The care of the team in every single detail is second to none. Favourite restaurant ever!

I was looking forward to try this place! As is a classic in the area, however I was bit disappointed. Yes the food is good, but I have tried better food in places that has no Michelin star, I was pretty shocked. I was expecting better quality of food, prettier platting and just tastier, that is what you would expect in a place with 1 star. I wouldn't recommend it at all!

Chez Bruce, a modern high-end French dining with one Michelin star. Although the offering is French cuisine but it comes with a twist of Asian flavours which add an exotic flavour to some of the dishes. The desserts were the highlight of the evening.
The ambiance is elegant but relaxed.
Service was professional and friendly.
Absolutely beautiful dining experience. The food was exquisite (the tuna sashimi was my favourite) and the service couldn’t have been better. A wonderful birthday treat from my friends!

places.name: Maison François
places.formatted_address: 34 Duke Street St James's, London SW1Y 6DF, UK
places.editorial_summary: Upmarket bistro offering classic French cuisine in a chic setting, plus a basement wine bar.

reviews.text:
For full transparency, I have dined here many times for lunch and dinner and also had a birthday party in the private dining room too.
Today was my first experience of their afternoon tea at the bargain price of £25 during August 2025. I have tried pretty much every place in London for afternoon tea so would say I know what I like and what's good value.

The staff as always were knowledgable, friendly and attentive.

In August, this is a great value for a new offering especially if you're new to trying out afternoon tea and don't want to fork out £100+ per person in London.

Limited range of teas, which isn't a bad thing, sometimes having a long menu can be somewhat perplexing. They had the usual stars, Earl Grey, English Breakfast and Darjeeling etc. The only one that was missing for me was Assam.

The servings are generous - 5 finger sandwiches. The best one was the vadouvan chicken, the worst one was the rilletes de thon (tuna sandwich), which in my opinion has no place in afternoon tea!
Of the patisserie the chocolate and peanut slice was the champion in this category, think a luxourious snickers. I could have easily eaten three of these.

Now what really differentiates MF's afternoon tea from others is that instead of scones (my least favourite part) is that they serve two warm babkas which are superb. Soft like a cloud and served with homemade strawberry jam, hazelnut spread and clotted cream.

Harry asked for my thoughts on the offering which I gave willingly.  I suggested they add their cabbage with achoiade in a petit pan instead of some of the finger sandwiches or a shot of the french onion soup.

Definitely worth a visit.

A bit overpriced but as expected given its superior  location. Quality of food was good overall, not the most extraordinary but still we enjoyed everything especially the onion soup! Added onion soup to my “to cook” list right afterwards. Staff is not rude for sure but I don’t remember feeling particularly welcomed so a solid 4 instead of 5.

Absolutely beautiful experience from start to finish. Great service particularly from the manageress going above and beyond. The food was outstanding — the steak tartare and gougères are must-tries, and the oysters were fresh and top quality. Venue itself is stunning too. Highly recommend.

What a delightful dining experience the place is! I am always pleasantly surprised to be reminded of what proper hospitality can achieve.

The space is vast and high, but is really well planned out, so manages to feel intimate and private. Service was almost impeccable, especially from the younger staff members, who were all effortlessly and genuinely charming.

Had the pate en croute, and was very pleased to be offered a little pot of mustard (that kept returning, refreshed as needed), a flatbread and then steak and cabbage. Prices vary, and I’m sure can rack up quite a bill, but there’s real value in there too. Had a cute mini martini and a couple of very pleasant glasses of wine.

It’s certainly one of the better meals I’ve had for a while, and whilst all the food was excellent it was really more the indefinable qualities of atmosphere and service that stood out the most. A proper, complete restaurant, and a total joy

We visited on an early Thursday evening. It was relatively quiet but it had filled up by the time we left.
I had a seasonal Bellini to start and I shared the chateaubriand with chips and green salad. It was very good and excellent value at £90 for the quality.
We didn’t need the sides but I really wanted the pommes purée. I definitely over-ordered. Ha!
The leeks were worth it. I’d return for the steak and order less next time. Recommended.

places.name: Casse-Croûte
places.editorial_summary: Intimate operation presenting a menu of traditional French offering & fine wines.

reviews.text:
I had a thoroughly enjoyable experience overall and would recommend this establishment to others. The service was consistently attentive throughout our visit—staff members were prompt with drinks, checked on us regularly, and were quick to address any needs we had. However, I did notice that while they were professional and efficient, there wasn’t much warmth or personality in the interactions. The service felt somewhat mechanical, lacking the friendly banter or genuine connection that can elevate a dining experience from good to memorable. It wasn’t poor service by any means, just a bit formal and distant.
That said, the food—which is undeniably the star of the show here—absolutely delivered on every level. Each dish was thoughtfully prepared and beautifully presented, showcasing quality ingredients and skilled execution. The flavors were well-balanced and sophisticated, demonstrating real culinary expertise in the kitchen. From the appetizers through to dessert, everything we ordered met or exceeded our expectations. The portion sizes were generous without being excessive, and the timing between courses was well-paced.
While the slightly impersonal service was a minor drawback, it certainly didn’t overshadow the exceptional quality of the food. When you’re dining at a place that prides itself on its cuisine, that’s ultimately what matters most, and this restaurant succeeds admirably in that regard

The atmosphere at this restaurant really is so beautiful. It’s low lit and intimate so it is perfect for couples or groups up to 4. The menu changes regularly and is entirely in French so the servers will translate for you if needed (which I certainly did). We ordered a veal salad, a duck main, and chocolate fondant. The veal salad was nice and light with a sour dressing. The duck confit was soft with mash and spinach. The chocolate fondant had a vanilla ice cream and a little caramel on top.

We came for Saturday lunch and enjoyed the cosy bistro atmosphere and the food was very good with good portion sizes. I like that the menu changes daily. Between the two of us, we shared the quail salad (very fresh and tasty), the steak with beans and peppercorn sauce with green beans and potatoes on the side (meat cooked perfectly medium rare and the peppercorn sauce was delicious) and the cabillaud with ratatouille (nice piece of fish and the ratatouille balanced it out well). The service was polite and friendly.

This bistro in the vicinity of London Bridge offers a compact menu but their dishes are all very good. This evening the three of us have the chance to try all their three starters and three main courses. Among the starters, I love the herring salad most, yet the asparagus and smoked duck breast with gizzard are not bad either. As for the main dish, the wellington beef, the cod and rabbit are all at our satisfaction. The ingredients are fresh enough and nicely cooked. The staff is helpful enough despite they are very busy.

It was my first time here and I wish I could go everyday! The atmosphere, the food and the friendly staff were simply incredible. I never go to places twice but I planning on visiting this gem again next week! It is not overdone, very authentic and INCREDIBLE food. As a French person living in London it was like they took the best parts of Paris and made it into this lovely place.

places.name: Clos Maggiore
places.editorial_summary: Modern French restaurant with notable wine list, flower-filled conservatory and log fire.

reviews.text: We had the set menu pre theatre menu and it was out of this world and excellent value for money. The interiors, and service was impeccable and the ambience was lovely. Most diners were doing the set menu at the time and we felt very relaxed and not rushed. Between the three of us I think we had one of everything off the menu and it was all divine - you won’t be disappointed

From start to finish, the experience was excellent. The starters, mains, and desserts were all beautifully presented and full of flavour. The décor and atmosphere are truly stunning, making the setting feel very special. Service was attentive and professional, complementing the high quality of the food. Overall, a memorable dining experience that I would highly recommend to anyone.

We celebrated a mix of birthdays and new jobs at Clos Maggiore, and it was absolutely perfect. The restaurant has a beautiful, romantic atmosphere, with the stunning floral décor making it feel really special for an occasion. The service was attentive and professional without being intrusive, and the food was excellent – every dish beautifully presented and full of flavour. It made for a memorable evening and felt like a real treat. Highly recommend for anyone looking for a place to celebrate something special in London.

We had a lovely dinner. The restaurant looked amazing with flowers beautifully decorating the entire ceiling. We enjoyed a three course meal each dish was delicately flavored and perfectly balanced. The service was attentive and efficient. The lunch set offers great value for money. I would definitely come back again.

Very nice place to eat, in terms of decoration it was really a 10. We are a fan of fine dining so we did the tasting menu (vegetarian and regular option) + wine parring. The food was good but not every dish was fantastic. For example: the steak tartare was very good, but the dish with lobster was not very special en it was one little bite off lobster.

Overall we had a good evening, but we expected more.

My experience at Pavyllon was truly exceptional. From the moment we walked in, we were greeted with warmth and professionalism. The cocktails were expertly crafted, setting the tone for an evening of culinary delights. The starters were a work of art, each dish bursting with flavor and beautifully presented. The mains were cooked to perfection, with each bite a symphony of taste and texture. And the chocolate souffle for dessert was simply heavenly.

But what truly stood out to me was the impeccable service provided by Rob and the rest of the wait staff. Rob's attention to detail and his warm personality made our dining experience even more memorable. He took the time to explain each dish and made sure that we were comfortable and satisfied throughout the evening.

Overall, I cannot recommend Pavyllon enough. From the delicious food to the top-notch service, this Michelin rated restaurant truly exceeded all of my expectations. It is a must-visit for anyone looking for an unforgettable dining experience in London.

Every single dish was a piece of art – beautifully plated, perfectly balanced, and full of flavour. From the delicate textures to the creative presentations, everything felt meticulously crafted.

Special thanks to sommelier Ricardo, who made the wine pairing truly memorable. His knowledge, warmth, and attentiveness elevated the entire evening.

The service was outstanding, the atmosphere elegant yet welcoming, and the attention to detail – flawless. A must-visit for anyone who appreciates refined, modern French cuisine in the heart of London.

We’ll definitely be back! ⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️

We stopped in for lunch at Pavyllon London and had an amazing time at the chefs counter! Chef Benjamin took time to explain dishes to us which really made the experience. The food was outstanding and I would like to go back for dinner service.

Some of the servers weren't the warmest would be my only critique.

The restaurant wasn't overly concerned with a dress code which was nice.

Overall a great experience!

An amazing Taste Of Pavyllon set lunch in such a spacious luxurious space. Sitting at the dining counter you see how the chefs prepare food at the large open kitchen and learn how the dishes are put together. One of the best chefs dining counter we've had.

Lots of natural light and a focus on comfort we began with an amuse bouche while we choose our starters of Soft Egg, Bluefin Tuna Tartare with a Ginger mayo and a Steamed Comté Cheese Soufflé with Watercress and smoked eel butter. Both delicious dishes.

Mains included a perfectly cooked Cornish Lamb Cutlet Cooked Over Fire with a trio of sauces and the exquisite Brown Butter And Lemon Confit Cod served with Cockle, peas and a herbal emulsion.

And what a divine mashed potato side dish with nutmeg!

For desserts we had the “Not So Classic” Tiramisu with a Cardamom and Mascarpone ice cream and a coffee sauce while my partner had the  Salted Chocolate Ganache with Yellow wine iced cream, mushroom extraction and honey. Both perfect.

What made this such a memorable visit is the fantastic food and the great interaction with all the team led by Head Chef Benjamin creating  a delightful Michelin-starred culinary journey.

The food was good, but I've had better steak and eggs in Dubai, which is why I'm giving it 4 stars. The ambiance was elegant, and the service was good. Although my steak was overcooked initially, the staff was accommodating and promptly replaced it. The apple juice was also a nice. I visited for breakfast, but I'd like to try it for lunch or dinner in the future.

places.name: La Trompette
places.formatted_address: 3-7 Devonshire Rd, Chiswick, London W4 2EU, UK
places.editorial_summary: High-end Modern French food with charcuterie and foie gras dishes in stylish contemporary space.

reviews.text:
We had such a fantastic experience here! For starters, we ordered the scallop lobster bisque ravioli and the foie gras chicken liver pâté, and both were exceptional. The ravioli had a generous amount of lobster, and the bisque was perfect – rich and flavourful without that bitter aftertaste you sometimes get. The pâté was unbelievably soft and smooth, one of the best we’ve had. (No photos of these dishes as we absolutely devoured them 😂)

For mains, we chose the beef and the pork cheek. Again, both dishes were outstanding - the pork was succulent, and the beef was tender and full of flavour. I especially loved the sweetcorn with the beef; it was such a lovely touch.

For dessert, we had the chocolate salted caramel délice and the banana soufflé. My husband is a big salted caramel fan, so he was in heaven with the délice, while I much preferred the banana soufflé. It was light, not too eggy, and beautifully done - I especially loved the crispy bits in the soufflé. It came with a very sharp passionfruit sorbet, which at first felt a little mismatched, but it ended up being oddly addictive and I ended up enjoying them separately.

Excuse my bad photos, which were a bit of an afterthought – I promise everything looked even better in real life!

Food was nice. Service was basic; serving each course without much description, but the menu had captured the key ingredients (I usually took pictures of the menu so that I could refer back to). I was expecting something more exciting from a Michellin star restaurant at this price tag for 3 courses. Rather low value for money in a very competitive F&B scene in London in general. Dessert was too sweet and tasted artificial for my liking.

the experience was great overall, it is located in a very quiet neighbourhood in west London. When we were there, the majority of the customers inside were people who were above 50 yrs old. But the food was good. Standard high end restaurant quality.
Fantastic one star neighbourhood gem, not the most obvious location but easy to get to from central London, both indoor and outdoor seating. Seasonal dishes, great wine selection and fab staff.
Always do great food, I love coming here. The white peach Bellini is a great start before your meal.

places.name: Mon Plaisir
places.editorial_summary: Busy bistro serving French classics in intimate dining spaces, with 50+ years of history.

reviews.text: Absolutely fantastic! I’d always wanted to visit this cozy French spot in Covent Garden and it truly exceeded my expectations. The slow-cooked beef cheek was one of the best I’ve ever had melt-in-your-mouth perfection. The waiter was so friendly and gave great recommendations for both food and drinks, which made the experience even more special. The decoration made me feel like I was in France, adding to the charm. Such a lovely evening overall, and the prices are very reasonable for the quality. Can’t wait to go back!

Although the food was good, we received such a poor welcome and service..  This French restaurant had a fantastic reputation back in the days and we were excited to have a nice quick meal while shopping in the area. Prices are mad...over £100 for 2 (one main course each and a glass of wine!!), service was so poor to a point the manager in charge did not speak to us once...until she took our payment..."have a great day" !! The waitress seemed to be the only one really working that day. The food was good, tasty and well presented...but not exceptional. There were spelling.mistakes in the menu. This was a disappointment....

Fantastic evening and great service from all staff. The food tasted exceptional and definitely worth the visit.
Mussels to share along with a prawn cocktail. The bread and French butter to soak up the sauce. The butter was 10/10! As was all foods.
Atmosphere was lovely, staff were attentive, decoration on point.

Great wine choice.
I was enjoying myself soo much i forgot to take pics of the mains.
Authentic French dishes, fresh ingredients and tasty flavours. Very good ambience and easy to have conversations over meals. Would come back.

December 2024

I had been here several times in the past and came back after many years and the food was still pretty good. However the portions appeared to have shrunk which was a shame. The beef tartare was good although it was a little too creamy for me. The duck main course was fairly nice and the crème brûlée was your standard crème brûlée. The only real issue was that I couldn’t believe how small my spinach side dish was considering I paid atleast £5 for it. There was probably no more than 3 mouthfuls in the bowl.

places.name: Sabor
places.editorial_summary: Lively, 2-story Spanish eatery offering tapas plates plus bar & countertop dining in casual digs.

reviews.text: The food was excellent—on the pricier side, but definitely worth it. Service was outstanding from the bar staff through to management. A special mention to Karolina at the front desk: even though we didn’t have a booking, she kindly found us seats at the bar and later welcomed us warmly to a table as soon as one became available. The premium beer and margarita were both fantastic. I’d give this place 5 stars and will definitely be returning.

The food is indeed fantastic and the Counter experience is recommended. Went there in June. Arrived 15 minutes before the 17 o'clock opening on weekday and all the people in the queue plus whoever arrived within 20 or so minutes got a spot at the Counter. Your next best chance is around 18:30 to 19:00 when the first people with happy tummies start leaving.

Either ask for recommendations or choose what you fancy. Pan Tomate was absolutely delicious, and so was the Mackerel. The Cuttlefish pappardelle were lovely too. Well, everything was good. Cremoso de Chocolate at the end was a fantastic finish.

I really wanted to love this place and had been looking forward to this visit for a celebratory occasion. We were sat at the counter and ordered similar dishes as the group of 3 next to us. Yet from the time stamps on our photos, we were only served 2 lukewarm (albeit tasty) croquetas in the 45min from placing our order. We didn’t want to complain but eventually when one of the staff asked if everything was ok we replied honestly that we were hungry. The group next to us had received 4 dishes in that time including the tortilla and octopus which we had also ordered. He then told us that these dishes take time as they are made on the spot - no apology or I’ll check with the chef but the implication that we were impatient - this seemed not in keeping with any good customer service much less Michelin starred. The second dish (arroz negros) eventually came in nearly an hour from when we ordered, which understandably is a dish that might longer to cook but we had also ordered a gem lettuce side and tortilla etc that could have staved off our hunger in the meantime. The food was delicious although a tad salty and all chefs were working hard if inefficiently. They seemed to make one dish at a time despite multiple orders of the same being made and then the dish will go on a little journey up the counter to be garnished then down the counter to be dressed then around again as they looked whose dish it was for - which probably explained why some dishes ended up being lukewarm. I really loved the dishes but feel underwhelmed by the service for the price and how delays were handled. Eventually when he realised we hadn’t received our tortilla after more than an hour our wait staff apologised. We didn’t feel appreciated as customers and probably won’t go back as we’ve had better service with same level of food at Barrafina.

Loved everything we ordered. The prawn croquetas were so morish, the show-stopper suckling pig was crispy on the outside, soft perfectly cooked on the inside. Patatas mojo rojo and seafood rice so tasty.

Another amazing dining experience for my husband’s 50th.
We ordered the entire menu pretty much. I cannot tell you which dish was my favourite as they were all incredible! But that pig is so juicy and the crackling is perfection. Our server Ilaria was extremely helpful and made my husband’s birthday that more memorable.
I want to return and explore more of the seafood options.

places.name: Copita
places.editorial_summary: Informal tapas bar with stools at wooden counters, wines, sherries and leche y leche coffee.

reviews.text:
2025/06
Delicious Spanish tapas with rich, authentic flavors! Everything we tried tasted great and was beautifully presented. It is on the expensive side, but the quality of the food makes it worth it. Overall, a very good experience!

Visited for birthday celebration. The drinks and food are great! Especially the gin tonic with basil & rosemary, also the pork! We ordered a cheesecake and the staff smartly deliver it with a candle. Enjoyed a nice time there!

I've been here twice, and every time I come, it's delicious and the service is also very good.
Especially recommend the octopus, ox cheek, prawns, buns
Last time I had apple pear & ice cream for dessert, miss it so much
The food was amazing, the best olives I’ve ever had and the goats cheese was dreamy. The team were so friendly, they really made a fuss of me for my 30th birthday. I would definitely recommend!

We were really disappointed with our experience here. The portions were shockingly small for the price — the ox cheek was literally about the size of a fist, gone in just a couple of bites, and the aubergine dish was barely half an aubergine. For two people we spent nearly £100 and left still feeling hungry. The quality of the dishes simply doesn’t justify the cost.

places.name: El Pirata Of Mayfair - Tapas Bar Español
places.editorial_summary: Informal tapas bar with authentic menu, Iberian wines and informal, dark-wood decor.

reviews.text:
We had such a wonderful experience here! The atmosphere is lively and authentic, perfect for a night out with friends. The seafood paella was absolutely delicious – rich in flavour, with perfectly cooked rice and generous portions of fresh prawns, squid, and mussels.

The tapas were also spot on – the garlic prawns were juicy and fragrant, the patatas bravas had the perfect crisp, and the pan con tomate tasted just like in Spain. Everything paired so well with the sangria, which was refreshing and fruity without being too sweet.

Service was friendly and attentive even though the restaurant was busy, and we never felt rushed. Definitely a place I’d love to come back to when craving proper Spanish food in London!

I chose the appetizer~
🥖Toasted Bread with Tomatoes: A truly authentic appetizer! The bread is super crispy! The freshly cut tomatoes with a little sea salt and olive oil are absolutely delicious!
🐟Grilled Cod Skewers: So fresh and tender! The meat is so tender, it looks like it's right on the cheek!
🍗Seared Chicken: This dish is so delicious! The skin is fried to a crispy crisp, and the chicken is fried just right, so soft and tender! I can't wait to order another plate of bread to finish all the sauce!
🦐Grilled Prawns in Garlic Sauce: A must-order for almost every table! Sizzling and sizzling, eat it while it's hot! The seasoning and olive oil complement the prawns so well!

🥘Seafood Paella: A Spanish must-try! The portion is huge and it's easy to slice! The side dishes included mussels, prawns, fish, and squid, perfect for two people!

🍮For dessert, we tried the caramel pudding: it was beautiful! The caramel layer was super crispy! You could literally take a chunk of caramel right off! The pudding had a rich, eggy aroma! It was the perfect ending. ~ My friend ordered the traditional Spanish cake with ice cream: it felt a bit like a nutty sponge cake, and it was delicious with the ice cream!

Amazing Spanish food! The seafood paella was full of flavour, the grilled octopus was perfectly cooked, and the sangria was fresh and fruity. Great atmosphere, friendly service – can’t wait to come back!

We spent the evening sipping on sangria and soaking up the cosy, vibrant atmosphere. The food was delicious — everything was well-prepared and full of flavour. The service was warm and genuinely welcoming, which made the whole experience even more enjoyable. Already looking forward to my next visit — highly recommend!

A friend invited me here for group dining and wow l was seriously impressed!

They have the 5J Iberico ham and also tried the cod cheeks, which I’d never had before…super tender!  We ended up ordering a bunch of tapas to share and loved every bite.

They’ve got a downstairs area with semi private dining space; Service was friendly and fast. Not overly formal, just chill and professional.

Definitely coming back,really solid food and proper Spanish hospitality

places.name: Copita Fitzrovia Tapas Bar
places.editorial_summary: Airy tapas bar with dark wood tables and a tiled floor, for small plates, Spanish wine and sherries.

reviews.text: We rarely had tapas like this outside of Spain! Everything was great and beautifully prepared. The staff were incredibly friendly and welcoming, which made the whole experience even better. The ceviche was our favourite, but everything was great. We will definitely come back.

All the dishes are cooked to perfection! I highly recommend the artichoke dish!! Martha was super friendly! We had sangria, mushroom croquettes, artichoke, tortillas, ox cheek, beef onglet, octopus and miso basque cheesecake😋😋

Wonderful meal!
Delicious tapas, nice desserts and a bottle of good wine.

Loved this place! Authentic Spanish food, would definitely recommend las croquetas de jamón and the cheesecake was the best i’ve ever tried. David was fantastic, very attentive. If you’re looking for friendly,  professional service and delicious quality food, Copita is a must!
Great quality food, service, good prices. Would recommend, great for sharing with friends. 👌

places.name: Barrafina Dean Street
places.editorial_summary: Cosy, diner-style tapas bar with stools for Spanish small plates, served with sherry, cava and more.

reviews.text: Absolutely loved all the food! Our favourite was the tortillas. This is so far the best tapas place we have been in London. We would definitely be back & will try the other dishes. Waiting time wasn’t too bad for a Saturday dinner time, but it’s worth the wait!

A delightful surprise! We stumbled upon this tapas restaurant and were absolutely blown away – it's hands down the best tapas experience we've ever had. Every dish was a flavor explosion, and we would highly recommend the squid and chicken thigh!

A huge thank you to our server, Kelvin, whose recommendations and attentive service truly elevated our meal. We can't wait to return next time when we are in town again!

We were lucky have a table for 4 , when we visited,  despite the restaurant was almost full, yet the chef or manager still took the time to explain almost all the dishes to us.
Such lovely people and happy staff!
The freshness of the food is clearly the key to this great tapas place. Thank you for the wonderful experience.

Barrafina is, without a doubt, the best Spanish food in London. I’ve been here around 10 times, and it never disappoints. Every visit feels like a little escape to Spain — the flavors are authentic, fresh, and perfectly balanced. From the classic tapas to the chef’s specials, everything is consistently outstanding. The atmosphere is lively and welcoming, and the service is amazing — Ryan and Kevin made our experience even better with their attention and friendliness. Barrafina has truly become my must-go spot whenever I’m in London. Highly recommend!

If you want great tapas, this is the place to be. Love the bar seating where you can watch your food being cooked. Each dish we ordered was well executed. Wish I had more stomach space to try more dishes!!

places.name: Dehesa
places.formatted_address: 25 Ganton St, Carnaby, London W1F 9BP, UK
places.editorial_summary: Spanish & Italian small plates & wine served in a chic, warmly decorated dining spot.

reviews.text: Very good Tapas place. Usual short menu of small plates. We had two starters, two mains and two puddings. Food was very good. Not too expensive at about £70. Sadly, we spent more on the wine, which was also very good. Recommended.

Dehesa has a nice lively atmosphere and friendly service, but overall felt overpriced for what it was. The olives were especially disappointing - £5.50 for what tasted like Tesco-brand in a tiny cup. We had calamari, bravas, tortilla, jamón and a few other dishes, which were decent but nothing standout. A 330ml bottle of standard beer at £7.20 also stung, though it’s probably expected given the area. Good for the buzz, but not great value.
My friend and I decided to try their tasting menu sets and it turned out to be super good value. Loads dishes included, decent portions, nice service. Their cocktail is lovely too.

MEDITERRANEAN TAPAS HEAVEN
📍 Soho, London
⭐️ 5/5
💸 ££
🍴 As a Barcelona girl, I have high standards when it comes to #tapas, and @dehesasoho totally delivered! Hidden in the heart of #Soho, this cosy, stylish spot (part of the @saltyardrestaurants) blends #Spanish and #Italian flavours with serious finesse. The vibe is intimate and modern, perfect for date night or a relaxed dinner with friends 💜
We went for the Head Chef’s Tasting #Menu and were impressed by every single bite. Highlights for me:
🖤 Valencian #arroz negro with Cornish cod and wild garlic aioli – intense, comforting and full of flavour
🌶️ Classic blistered #padrón peppers – simple and perfect
🍅 Creamy Puglian #burrata with beef tomato and sundried tomato pesto – light but indulgent
🍋 And for dessert: #Pistachio & white chocolate buñuelos with whipped lemon ricotta = a dreamy finish.
Also, shoutout to the amazing service! Our three waiters were super sweet and even gave us takeaway bags so we didn’t waste a single bite. Dehesa felt like a little taste of home, I’ll definitely be coming back to.

A really beautiful evening!! Came in for a birthday and Zuzanna was our waitress and she was amazing, very sweet and very knowledgeable about the menu and the drinks. Really good food and good energy, we really enjoyed ourselves so much!

places.name: La Gamba - Spanish Tapas Bar & Restaurant
places.formatted_address: Unit 3, Royal Festival Hall, Southbank Centre, London SE1 8XX, UK
places.vicinity: Unit 3, Royal Festival Hall, Southbank Centre, Waterloo Campus, London

reviews.text: Came here with my boyfriend for our anniversary. Miguel welcomed us in like we were his family. He was super attentive and friendly! He gave us two glasses of bubbles to celebrate our anniversary which was a lovely touch. Food was absolutely amazing from start to finish! From the tasty jamón,pulpo scallops everything we enjoyed.We were so full but managed to squeeze in desserts!  Definitely would recommend and we will be back soon! Thank you !

Nice restaurant, we went for the bottomless sangria brunch. The food is pretty good, very generous portions with three tapas per person, we couldn’t even finish it all. The sangria is not the best I have ever had, but you can drink it quite easily! We also had a bottle of Cava (included in the bottomless) so can’t really complain. Service needs some improvement, generally very slow, which  is not really what you want during a 90 minutes brunch; we also had one waiter with a bit of an attitude…so when we found a £33 discretionary service charge it was quite the surprise. We paid anyway as in the end the food was good.

Trendy and upbeat meets family owned and operated at this River front restaurant on the Thames. It is a must go to when visiting London for a modern take on true tapas recipes straight from Spain. The aubergine is a must when visiting here. The staff is attentive and inclusive to all nationalities, treating each table like you are a part of their own family when dining here.

Bit of a mixed experience today. Some highlights but a couple of lows too. Overall though a fairly decent meal. First positives initially had a warm welcome and service was quick and food came quickly too. Jamon croquettes, aubergine, and asparagus where great, patatas brava was average and mussels tasted really good , but some were very gritty. Lows included overcooked cod cheeks , although caper sauce was nice, and chicken thighs a bit dry and just nothing, cooked better myself last weekend. Would probably give it another go as may have been unlucky. Service at times was a bit perfunctory. Desert was glorious, torrija, sorry didn't get a photo of that one , meaning we left on a high.

Beautiful small plates of food, set next to the River Thames. Outdoor seating if the weather is right.
Perfect place for a get together to enjoy shared plates for lunch or dinner.

places.name: Donostia Restaurant
places.editorial_summary: Gourmet tapas in an elongated room with tables and stools at marble-topped bar, and an open kitchen.

reviews.text:
We've dined here many times over the years an never fail to be impressed and have a great meal.

The staff are great and extremely knowledgeable. The food is always amazing.

You must always order the tortilla because it's the best one you can have anywhere in London.

The Spanish tapas here are absolutely delicious!
The cheesecake was so good it completely destroyed my “keep fit” plan—I couldn’t stop myself from devouring it. Every single dish was full of flavor and brought me right back to my time in Spain.

The only downside? The basement vibe isn’t the coziest and the chairs weren’t very comfortable. Also, the server accidentally tried to charge us twice—but honestly, the food was so good I almost didn’t care! Plus, the staff are actually Spanish, which made the experience feel even more authentic.

Strongly recommend! Just… next time, pretty please let me sit at one of the nice ground floor tables. Gracias!

My friend and I had an amazing meal in Donostia yesterday. The service was great and the food was so fresh and tasty. Definitely the best tapas I’ve ever had in London. I went for my usual go to dishes: croquetas de jamón, pan con tomate, tortilla española, and all were great! The basque cheesecake to finish was incredible. I left very full and content.

Sat at the bar solo .. Chef Kevin and chef marc and manager Eneko were wonderful and made my experience different!!!

Tried a little of the Basque cheese cake and it is is to die for (I’ve had many and this one is truly unique with the texture that is creamy and  ice cream like). Food I had the pork and the octopus, which were delicious.

This restaurant gets very busy at around 830/ 9 pm in summer on a Saturday and has very good ambience with a buzz.  Love the top floor and the bar.. def will be back to try the other dishes .. as I sat at the bar was salivating over the croquettes, tomato bread and the beef.. will be back with my reviews of that!

We walked past this restaurant 6 weeks ago and ate here that night because the food sounded so good, and it was!

6 weeks later we are back in London for a night and we had no hesitation in eating here again and it was superb. The burrata and fig salad, the Galatian octopus, grilled peppers and the lamb ribs were all superb. Enjoyed with a really lovely Albariño and topped off with great service from Gabriel - all in all this was a great dining experience. Do yourself a favour and eat here - you won’t regret it!!!

places.name: Aqua Nueva
places.editorial_summary: A bull guards the entrance to a modern northern Spanish restaurant and roof terrace with city views.

reviews.text: Great atmosphere with a glamorous vibe. The waiters were excellent and very attentive. Spanish food tasted authentic esp the paella! I’d highly recommend turron, it was one of the best desserts I’ve tried!

The food is very good. The portion is as you could imagine for tapas. Though, nothing particularly stands out as memorable. The paella was the only one I could remember the taste of.

Service is good, very professional and proper. The food is slightly salty for mr but maybe depending on individual's taste.

We got a little too much and couldn't finish our meals so we asked to doggy bag it home as they asked us to sign a waiver.

5 stars no notes. Our host, Ray, who doubled as a sommelier was knowledgeable and personable. I recommend visiting in the evening in the week as we had the place to ourselves. Perfect for a romantic date night. The food was delicious I highly recommend the black seafood croquettes, octopus and the pork tenderloin. The wine was delicious, served well and the staff aka Ray was friendly and attentive. The food came out quickly (as we were the only people there) however it tasted fresh and was served hot. Order at least 8 plates for 2 people as the portions are small - however executed very well.

I booked this place for me and my friends. It was 4 of us. And I can definitely recommend this place as it’s amazing. It’s has many great options of drinks and food. Amazing rooftop and nice music. Food was so delicious 🤤 we will definitely come back 😉
Lovely place with both a courtyard and indoor seating. The waiter was friendly and funny, the food was well-presented, and with the lunch discount it was great value.

places.name: La Parra Tapas
places.formatted_address: 158 Fulham Palace Rd, London W6 9ER, UK

reviews.text:
Cosy restaurant with incredibly tasty food. Our personal favourites were the croquetas of the day and ibérico. Will definitely be returning to sample the rest.

Also very impressed by the quantities of vegetarian options on the menu.

Great food and services with fantastic value for money. Not often these days in London seeing lots of options under £10/tapa that’s not overly salty. Would recommend especially if in the area

Would recommend order sangria by glass instead of jug - the 1L option is quite difficult to pour

Drinks / dessert / service all in £50 per head
Amazing cozy restaurant with good food. Chorizo is so so good and also the peppers. Great wine and a free liquor when we left. Tomorrow we are going back for the paella

Unbelievable place, great little find. Service was fantastic,  recommended things which were spot on. The courses we ordered were all so tasty. The quality of the ingredients used were really top notch. Atmosphere was brilliant,  we were sat in the front of house but did see the dining area set back. Seriously when we are back in the area we will revisit. Thank you for a great meal! Wine choice with meal was fantastic.  Menu options were varied and plenty of choices for anyone.

My favourite small piece of Spain in London! The food have amazing taste! I have tried different dishes and all of them get the five stars. It is tradicional cooking, but you can taste the fusions of new flavours. And really good value! The iberico secret! Yummy yummy!
Any corner have a good details to take a picture.
