Alabama was warm in her attentions. She Always advises good recommendations and explaining all dishes with details; even, she explained me the history of the place. She is a sweet girl with a lot of arte! Even she takes care about the temperature of the salon.
The attention and the food come quick.
Really recommend with my heart!

places.name: Lobos
places.editorial_summary: Warm tapas bar with wood furnishings & a laid-back vibe offering steaks & Iberico pork.

reviews.text:
Had a very enjoyable dinner with friends at this tapas restaurant.
The dishes were superb (the lamb cutlets, steak and octopus were my favourites) and it was a nice touch for the chef to send us a complimentary octopus which was delicious - thank you.
The restaurant has a fun vibe, a downstairs bar with some interesting wolf-themed quotes. The staff were super friendly and attentive. Special mention to Jasmine who looked after us - she was superb! All in all - a gem of a restaurant in Soho - I recommend it!

I love that  they location is very central,  food portions on tapas are big.  Like 3 to 4 tapas can be shared for 2. Cheesecake is fantastic.  Lambchop is a must. Strawberry daiquiri and sangria are exquisite.

I honestly have to say everything was exceptional! I'm so glad I chose to celebrate my birthday here 🎈it was the perfect decision. The food was absolutely delicious, every dish better than the last. The staff were incredibly kind and welcoming, which made the evening even more special. I truly appreciate the lovely birthday cake. Thank you for making it such a memorable night!❤️🌹
Delicious food, favorite foie gras steak and octopus leg, others were also tasty, great service, the waiters were friendly

Visited with five friends on a quiet Monday evening.  We were led to the 1/F dining area with view of the half open kitchen.  Ordered loads of tapas, a couple of Iberico pork dishes and three bottles of wine to share.  Price was quite reasonable.

places.name: Salt Yard
places.editorial_summary: Spanish & Italian small plates & wine served in a chic, warmly decorated dining spot.

reviews.text: Lovely atmosphere, great food and drinks. We especially enjoyed the octopus and the tuna! The cocktails were also delicious. One downside was the drinks took too long to come out, but was not an issue in the end. Will definitely be coming back!

Delicious Spanish food and lovely atmosphere. The vibe is order a bunch of dishes to share between yourselves. Highly recommend trying the octopus and the courgette flower - very tasty. The lamb is also very good. Great value for money

Every dish was amazing. Especially the croquetas, courgette flower, lamb, Patatas bravas and churros. The wine was great, they had a really good selection with descriptions on the menu. The staff were all lovely and attentive. The decor was nice as was the music and general atmosphere. I’d recommend booking as they did turn people away when we were there as they were fully booked. We ate pre theatre which was great because it’s a lot quieter area then closer to the theatres and it’s only a 16minute walk away.

Lovely lunch.
The quality of the food is never disappointing.
Chrissie looked well after us.

It can feel like roulette picking a place to eat in the west end - but as we stepped inside this unassuming place on Goodge Street we were immediately enthused by the relaxed vibe. A mid afternoon slot meant the place was quiet but far from dead - with some decent tunes in the background and a couple of other sets of dinners for company. The staff were welcoming and friendly. Our cocktails were on point and slipped down quickly. All dishes were very tasty and well executed. The house white was fresh and nice and chilled. For me, a highlight was the Basque cake desert. Overall we ate and drank well for under £150 including service - which isn’t too bad in the centre of town. A really safe option in an ocean of choice.

places.name: Luna Llena
places.formatted_address: 119 Stroud Green Rd, Finsbury Park, London N4 3PX, UK

reviews.text: Great Spanish flavours, great wine, with decent portions. Everything tasted nice. The paella, the artichoke salad, and bread with salsa dips were fantastic. Stylish and fun decor, with a relaxing atmosphere. I love the red chairs and the writing wall. I came here for brunch with friends during the Easter weekend. It was the only restaurant open in the area, as the others closed at 3pm. So it's a great place to go at any time, with no time restrictions. I would love to come back for the flamenco dancing night.
5***** food and service. The food was outstanding. Everything was freshly cooked and tasted wonderful. The service was very attentive without being over the top. We will definitely be returning.

I was not too sure at first because I know tapas is normally small portions and to be honest I was quite hungry. But to my surprise the portions we decent, food was fresh and if great quality. Wonderful selection of wines and fantastic desserts. Wonderful ambience and great service. I will definitely be coming back 👏👏👏

"A Taste of Spain Like No Other!"
From the moment I walked into  I knew I was in for something special. The warm, inviting atmosphere transported me straight to the heart of Spain, with its rustic decor, soft lighting, and lively yet intimate ambiance.
But the real star of the night? The food. Without a doubt, I had the best paella I’ve ever tasted—perfectly cooked rice, rich saffron flavors, and the freshest seafood and meats, all coming together in a dish that was nothing short of perfection. Every bite was an explosion of authentic Spanish flavors, and it was clear that the chefs take pride in their craft.
The service was just as impeccable, with friendly and knowledgeable staff who made the experience even more enjoyable. Whether you're a fan of Spanish cuisine or simply looking for an unforgettable dining experience, Luna Llena is a must-visit.
Can’t wait to go back! Already booked next Flamenco day on the 04/04 👠💃

I am so lucky to have just walked into this place.  They have amazing food.  The grilled salmon tapas might well be one of the best salmon dishes I have ever ordered. It was crunchy yet soft on the outside and pink and juicy on the inside. The courgette flowers take you back to the Mediterranean.  The staff member is amazingly lovely and welcoming, too.  I especially thank Ece, who was very hospitable and attentive. She also has a huge smile, which is great to see at the end of a tiresome day.

places.name: Little Taperia
places.formatted_address: 143 Tooting High St, London SW17 0RU, UK
places.vicinity: Bonnies Pets & Flowers, 143 Tooting High St, London
places.editorial_summary: Narrow, rustic-modern hub with a marble bar and upbeat vibe for cocktails and Spanish small plates.

reviews.text:
A lovely little place right on tooting high street offering traditional tapas style small dishes but in a restaurant/bar setting.

Service as friendly and efficient.

Location was quiet at lunchtime on a Friday.

Food was delicious and the service was good and relatively fast. Unfortunately we had a table in a pathway in the back part of the restaurant which was not a particularly nice place to sit. The front of the restaurant would probably be a more pleasant experience.

Went for a lovely dinner to celebrate my fiancé’s birthday, and I’m so glad we chose this place — such a gem! The food was exceptional; the cheese board, tortilla, and patatas bravas are a must. Igor gave us amazing service, attentive and perfectly timed. To top it off, they surprised my fiancé with a candle on top of the desert, and a little birthday serenade with instruments. Highly recommend for any occasion!

My partner and I had a super delicious meal here last night. The atmosphere is friendly and intimate. The portions are very good for a tapas restaurant and the quality of the food was excellent. We sat right in front of the kitchen and got to watch them work their magic— would definitely recommend!
I literally have never had a bad meal here. A local gem. Get the set menu, such good value for money. Oh and the cocktails are incredible too! Service a touch slow when it’s busy but it’s worth it.

places.name: El Ganso Cafe
places.editorial_summary: Modern and fusion tapas in a compact, casual Spanish restaurant with simple tables and banquettes.

reviews.text: The staff at El Ganso was so kind and accommodating for my birthday dinner. We were 11 total and had the tasting menu, which was such a great option for us. Because of different dietary needs, they were able to swap out some of options for the folks at our table. The food was tasty, and the portions were generous! We were able to get refills on any of the tapas we wanted.

El Ganso is Head & shoulders above the competition on Broadway Market. Sensational food. Great service. Lovely, relaxed atmosphere. No wonder it’s so busy, they deserve every bit of success. Best brunch in Hackney & gorgeous tapas too.

Great food, service, and staff! I had the best octopus I’ve had in a long time (I preferred it grilled), and the prawns and croquettes — oh my word... Everything was reasonably priced, and there's a nice selection of wines. The staff were incredibly helpful in recommending the best pairings and sharing plates based on our preferences and group size.

Broadway Market on a sunny Saturday just hits different. It honestly couldn’t have been a better day. As tempting as all the amazing street food was, my friend and I are the kind of people who like a comfy seat, a proper table, and a chance to relax before jumping back into the fun. So we picked El Ganso for lunch.

The place was busy and full of energy, but in a good way. Our waitress was lovely and super helpful when it came to choosing what to eat.

My friend went for the Carrillada de Cerdo, which is slow-cooked pork cheeks with mashed potatoes and truffle. She absolutely loved it. I had the Alcachofa Confitada, artichokes with mushrooms, truffle foam, and egg yolk. Honestly, it was so good I could have eaten it twice. We also shared some Gambas al Ajillo, because garlic prawns are always a good idea.

The food was amazing, and we paired it with a refreshing gin and tonic (they have a great selection) and a cold beer.

Everything was spot on, and we’re already looking forward to going back.
Such a great place to celebrate your birthday!! The atmosphere is amazing, the food is great, and the staff were super nice.

places.name: Koko Grill Korean BBQ Restaurant
places.formatted_address: 173 Tower Bridge Rd, London SE1 2AW, UK

reviews.text: Great food! We walked past this restaurant and decided to give it a try — surprisingly, it turned out to be very good!

As my first time having Korean bbq I cannot complain. I really enjoyed the food especially the pancakes and the seaweed rice dumplings but also the bbq was tasty maybe too hot for me but that’s just my personal taste. All the staff were so polite and nice I will definitely go back.
Great Korean BBQ experience... The service was exemplary... Food was great and filling... A bit expensive, but then the portions were big

Really delicious food, great value for money and excellent service. The place itself is very clean and spacious. It does get busy at night so do make reservations especially for BBQ - the staff are really really fast and food comes really fast too so you should be ok walking up for non-BBQ but book for BBQ.

Food is really tasty and good portion size. I would say one of the best around SE1. We ordered 2 mains, 2 rice and kimchi assortment; and we were so full!

We are so happy we have a local Korean restaurant now! Will be back more!
Amazing food! Amazing service even help grill the meet! People are nice the vibe is amazing ! Meat is fresh

places.name: YORI Korean Restaurant (Covent Garden)
places.editorial_summary: Casual outlet providing traditional Korean dishes & drinks, plus tabletop grills & hot pots.

reviews.text: Went there for dinner, had lovely food and the service was great. I had vegan bibimbap with tofu, the scallion pancake, we shared some japchae and drinks. All came to about 40£ per person. Would go again

We had such an amazing evening for my birthday here this evening Hsu and Kia were incredible changing the playlist to suit my favourite songs and constantly wishing me a happy birthday! Food was incredible! Super service will be back!

Disappointed with the quality compared to the other Korean restaurants we tried last week. It might be because it’s a chain, so perhaps expectations shouldn’t be too high. Not terrible, but definitely underwhelming.

It’s pretty good!

The seafood pancake, GalBi Tang and quite good, but the fried chicken batter was a bit too much for my liking, and the egg fried rice was a tad too oily.

Overall it’s still pretty good and service and atmosphere is good.

The kimchi pancake was really good, the rest of the food was okay but I wouldn't say I loved it. Food was very well presented and freshly cooked. We were also sat on quite a small table so we didn't have much space.

We had a great experience dining here! We found the atmosphere to be just like in Korea. Staff were super kind and welcoming! The food was amazing. Fresh and high quality meat, juicy, perfectly seasoned. Exceptional taste that had us ordering more and more. Korean inspired cocktails like the Makpuccino rounded off our evening. Looking forward to return to our new favorite Korean restaurant!

We came here on a Friday evening without a reservation. We had brought drinks with us and were worried we’d have to finish them before going in, but the staff kindly stored them in their fridge for us - which we really appreciated.

The food was absolutely top tier. My sister and I were so caught up enjoying every single dish that we barely spoke throughout the meal. We ordered the seafood pancake, jajangmyeon, and fried chicken - and each one was incredible. As someone who truly loves Korean cuisine, this place completely blew me away

The staff were lovely, and the food came out quickly even though it was a busy Friday evening in a lively area. We were also pleasantly surprised to receive complimentary side dishes - we thought they would be extra, so that was such a nice touch. I’ll definitely be coming back!

we had amazing dinner in this restaurant. place were bit busy considering it was weekend but didn't take long queue and food came quickly. all was absolutely fantastic and staff were super nice, thanks for all taken great care of our table! short rib is THE best!!!

Love the place. Good food, reasonable prices, and great staff.

The soup was pretty hot, and I like my soup HOT, so I appreciated that. Not to mention that this is one of the few places where you get free Banchan (side dishes). + Rice was included in the platter I ordered (platter A).

Will come back again ❤️

This place was recommended to me. Really good food. Really nice staff. I'm not a Korean BBQ expert but this was really nice. I went to an all you can eat Korean nearby and it was good. But this, I immediately tasted the difference in the quality of the meat. It was so nice here. The staff will help you out too if you don't know what to do so do not be put off.

You order through your phone. Each person scans the barcode and sends their order to the chef, the meat and stuff then comes to your table. The barcode let's the chef know what table you are. You pay at the end. Highly Recommended

places.name: Arang Restaurant
places.editorial_summary: Smart modern Korean restaurant with large menu of classic kimchi cabbage and banchan side dishes.

reviews.text:
We recently visited this restaurant and had such an incredible experience from start to finish! The atmosphere was warm, lively, and welcoming, perfect for enjoying a hearty Korean meal. We also had an amazing server SJ, who served the three of us and was attentive the whole time.

Recommendation Dishes:
Jajangmyeon with beef, Kimchi pancakes, tteokbokki with cheese, beef bimbibap.

For any Muslims coming here, there's plenty of halal dishes and you can substitute the pork with alternatives like beef, seafood or chicken.

The food was absolutely delicious. The tteokbokki had just the right amount of spice and sweetness, with chewy rice cakes that were cooked perfectly. The kimchi pancake was crispy on the outside and soft on the inside, packed with flavour and easily one of the best we’ve tried. The jajangmyeon with beef was rich and savoury, with a delicious flavour that paired so well with the noodles. The sides from the kitchen were also fantastic, everything from the kimchi to the pickled radish and other small dishes tasted fresh, well-seasoned, and perfectly complemented the mains. You can really tell that care and attention go into every dish.

We also tried the miso soup, which had a gentle umami flavour and a great palate cleanser between dishes. Personally, I found it a little mild for my taste, but my friends really enjoyed it, describing it as wonderfully soothing and comforting. It's like the kind of warm soup you’d crave when you’re feeling under the weather.

We ordered a few other dishes too, including the japchae, bibimbap, and mandu. The japchae had a good texture, the glass noodles were slightly bouncy but it wasn’t as flavourful as the other dishes we tried, so it felt a little dry and underwhelming in comparison. The bibimbap was enjoyable and nicely presented, though since we ordered quite a variety, it was naturally a bit overshadowed by the stronger flavours of the tteokbokki and jajangmyeon. The mandu was good, though it wasn’t particularly standout compared to the other dishes on the table.

But what truly made the evening special was the outstanding service from SJ. He was friendly, professional, and incredibly attentive throughout our meal. He checked in at just the right moments, made thoughtful recommendations, and went out of his way to make sure we were comfortable and happy. His positive energy and genuine hospitality really stood out and made our dining experience unforgettable.

We’ll definitely be coming back, not only for the amazing food but also because SJ made us feel so welcome. Highly recommend this place to anyone looking for great Korean food and top-tier service!

This restaurant was such a discovery! We ate so well today. The portions are big, the food is super tasty and the girl working was very nice. They play Kpop and the prices are totally ok for the center of London (actually cheaper than many other restaurants we saw).
Food was so good! I had Bulgogi set menu with my friend and could try so many different things. After the meal, they even served fruit! I definitely want to go again :)

Arang has a proper authentic Korean feel, and it’s super easy to get to, just a few minutes’ walk from Piccadilly. The menu’s got loads of choice and the service was really attentive. We went for the BBQ, which came with all the sides (even though that’s not totally clear on the menu), plus a few other dishes. Everything was really tasty.

We had a lovely meal here and were especially impressed by the warm service. The food was cleanly presented and well-prepared across the board.

We ordered samgyeopsal (grilled pork belly), and while the meat was fresh and nicely grilled, do note that you need to order lettuce (sangchu) and green onion salad (pa-jeori) separately if you want the full Korean BBQ experience.

The seolleongtang (ox bone soup) came with plenty of noodles and egg, offering a comforting, mild flavor. The haemul-pajeon (seafood pancake) was crisp and flavorful, packed with seafood. The dolsot-bibimbap (stone pot bibimbap) was deliciously well-balanced, with a perfect mix of textures and flavors.

One particularly touching gesture was when the staff kindly offered roasted seaweed and fruit for the children — a warm and thoughtful touch that made us feel truly welcome.

Highly recommended for anyone craving authentic Korean food with exceptional hospitality.

places.name: Seoul Tokyo
places.formatted_address: 168 Borough High St, London SE1 1LB, UK

reviews.text:
If you’re craving authentic Korean flavors in the heart of London, this place is an absolute must-visit. I ordered 5-6 dishes and there were packed with rich flavors.

One thing I really loved is how they use high-quality ingredients. The portion sizes are great for sharing, so it’s perfect for a casual dinner with friends or a cozy date night.

Prices are reasonable for central London, and honestly, the food is worth every penny. I can’t wait to go back and try more dishes. If you’re looking for an authentic taste of Korea without leaving London, this spot is a gem.

Friendly staff. Clean. Excellent food with just the right amount of salt.

Came here with a friend for lunch. We ordered cabbage kimchi and beans out kimchi as cold starters.

We also got a seafood pancake. It’s fresh, chewy and not too oily.

We each ordered a stew dish. My friend got a spicy ox tail stew with rice. I got a pork and tofu kimchi stew.

Both stews came to us pipping hot. I didn’t find any of the dishes excessively salty or greasy. The rice was a mix of white rice and red rice.

My friend also ordered a Korean soda drink.

We also got 10% off by paying in cash.

The cold dishes, pancake and two stews with rice portion came to a total of £38.50 (including the discount). This is great for value considering the quality of food was also great!

I was able to grab a table for one here yesterday as a walk in just before the rush started. I was expecting smaller portions so I over ordered but it’s fine because I took the rest home.

I ordered a half portion of the Yangnyeom KFC (5 pieces) £7 and the cheese dalggalbi £14. I also ordered regular cabbage kimchi £2.5 and cucumber kimchi £2.5. I finished the dalggalbi and cabbage kimchi because it was lighter and the sourness and spiciness of the kimchi went well with it. I wrapped up most of the KFC to go home.

The staff were really friendly and attentive. I think towards the end they were ready busy between the tables as well as the telephone calls for reservations and takeaway orders. Even though I did ask for a plastic takeaway box for the kimchi which is watery, I was given an aluminium one. It was my second time asking so I couldn’t be bothered to ask again, and yes, it did end up spilling inside the bag despite trying to wrap it up tight inside the plastic bag I was given.

The chicken tasted fresh and the portions were good. I think I’ll definitely come back if I have the chance.

I’ve been to Seoul Tokyo several times, and overall, it’s one of my favorite places for Korean food in central London. This time, my boyfriend and I came for dinner, and as usual, the food didn’t disappoint.

We ordered gamjatang, half & half chicken (ganjang and snow cheese), white jjambbong, yukhwe, and a selection of kimchi. The yukhwe and white jjambbong were by far the best I’ve had among Korean restaurants in central London — truly excellent. The rest of the dishes were also delicious; I have no complaints about the food itself.

However, this visit had a few frustrating moments. The rice that’s supposed to come with gamjatang was brought only at the end of the dinner because, according to staff, it “wasn’t ready” — which really disrupted the dining experience.

What bothered me the most was the mix-up with the chicken order. We clearly ordered half ganjang, half snow cheese chicken (repeating it twice), but were instead served yangnyeom. When we pointed it out, the waitress didn’t apologise — instead, she started arguing with us, insisting we never asked for snow cheese. And rather than replacing the chicken, she just brought a small bowl of cheese powder. That kind of service felt dismissive and unprofessional.

Customer service and communication matter just as much as the food. I also believe a Korean restaurant would benefit from having more Korean staff, both for authenticity and smoother communication with guests.

I’d still be happy to return because the food is genuinely good, but if we get the same waitress again, I’d kindly request another  server for our table.

My absolute favourite Korean place in London! I’ve been so many times and brought both family and friends – everyone was genuinely impressed. The flavours are so authentic and comforting. I especially recommend the spicy oxtail soup, bibimbap, and Korean fried chicken – all absolutely incredible. I still need to come back for the BBQ, but I already know it’s going to be amazing. A must-visit if you’re craving real Korean food! 🤤🥰

places.name: Soju Korean Restaurant
places.formatted_address: 282 Cambridge Heath Rd, London E2 9DA, UK

reviews.text: Awesome food, lovely staff, fast service and terrific atmosphere. Place is clean, service is top class. Highly recommended.

Stumbled across this place whilst searching for Korean restaurants for my daughters birthday. We came here lovely small restaurant everyone of the staff were very friendly and this made us feel very welcome. The food portion sizes were very good. My favourite thing that we had were the amazing honey garlic sticky wings. The crunch, size, taste amazing. This was my first time and not my last thank you team for amazing service.

The restaurant's food is just nice and testy. Service is also awesome.
Wish to be there often .
Really lovely, kind and friendly staff and super tasty food! Would recommend!
"Had a lovely Korean meal with my daughter today in Bethnal Green. Tasty food, kind staff, and cosy vibe. Highly recommend!"

places.name: Jang Restaurant
places.formatted_address: The Mezzanine, First Floor, Royal Exchange, London EC3V 3LQ, UK
places.vicinity: The Mezzanine, First Floor, Royal Exchange, London

reviews.text:
This was an amazing experience with top quality food.
We were served by Rebecca, Neda and Jose who where all very welcoming and helpful.
The restaurant is beautiful and nice and relaxing atmosphere. They even kindly changed the chair for me to fit my preference.
We had the sushi to start which was the best sushi I've ever had. I then had the lobster which was tender and flavorful in a delicious creamy broth with noodles and a side of kimchi which tasted really authentic. One of us had the duck which was cooked medium rare as requested and the broccoli which was seasoned really nicely. And lastly 2 of us had the sharing platter and added wagyu. All the meats where cooked to our preference and seasoned well and it came with lots of sides my favourite was the seaweed salad and loads of sauces to try with the meats as well as some rise.
We also had some lovely cocktails presented very nicely as well as a lovely birthday suprise.
Definitely worth a visit couldn't recommend enough hopefully we'll get to go back soon.

A very wonderful place to take an afternoon tea. This place is preferred to book in advance due to a lot of people. I can describe this place as a romantic quiet place where you can have some of quiescence. The view from up is also another interesting point. The atmosphere with the red colors is giving the impression of an awesome view. Honestly I have enjoyed the experience and I strongly recommend everyone to try and to get some of quiescence. One more thing that staff are so friendly really big thanks to the whole entire involved people for making such great experiences.

We had a truly wonderful afternoon tea experience, thanks to Jaqueline and Rebecca.

Jaqueline warmly welcomed us, personally escorted us to our table, and made sure we were seated by the balcony as requested. Rebecca was absolutely charming and explained the menu with ease. She also kindly accommodated my partner’s dietary preference by adjusting the selection and offering extra salmon sandwiches without mayonnaise.

The presentation was beautiful, and we especially appreciated Rebecca’s attention to detail—she even changed our plates just before we enjoyed the desserts.

Thank you both for making our visit so special. It was a delightful experience, and we would highly recommend it.

I had lunch at Jang today, and it was such a great experience. The food was delicious, well-prepared, and full of flavor. The atmosphere was welcoming, and the service made the meal even more enjoyable. I’ll definitely come back again!

I absolutely loved my experience at Jang! Our server Neda was so friendly and her recommendations all hit the spot!

The Wagyu Korean BBQ was stunning and we loved that it was smoked at the table and had 3 condiments we could pair it with! The sushi was presented beautifully and the Korean fried chicken bites were gorgeous!

Beautiful interior, perfect for an occasion!

places.name: Korean Dinner Party
places.formatted_address: Top Floor, Kingly Ct, Carnaby, London W1B 5PW, UK
places.editorial_summary: Korean fusion, unique cocktails, art & curated tunes in a hopping locale with a popular brunch.

reviews.text: Gorgeous dining experience! 🫶🏽 I came here with 7 friends to celebrate a birthday and we had the loveliest time. The food was excellent and the atmosphere and service were lovely. We were very lucky to be served by Marina, who went above and beyond to take care of our table, and even took some Polaroids of us to take home as a birthday present. So wholesome 🥰 would definitely recommend to a friend!

Note that this review is specifically for the Taco Tuesday bottomless tacos. I thought the quality of the meats was perfectly fine - the beef was tender and fatty, and the chicken was not dry and had a satisfying crunch. However for a Korean fusion restaurant, these tacos severely lacked any Korean influence. The only element that tasted remotely Korean was the small pot of ssamjang sauce served alongside the tacos. They could’ve done much more with the flavouring to really emphasise that this was Korean fusion cuisine.

I did like the slaw though - it was crunchy, slightly bitter, and complemented the tacos well. On the other hand, we were perplexed by the aubergine and mushroom filling. The menu listed fried cauliflower, which would’ve made a bit more sense, since a crunchy fried filling would’ve been a nice contrast to the soft flour taco. This filling however, felt completely out of place and didn’t belong in a taco. It was too soft and saucy, the flavours leaned more Mediterranean than Korean, and it didn’t hold up well in a soft flour tortilla - it would’ve been better served over rice. If not fried cauliflower, fried enoki mushrooms would’ve worked well too?

Service was good, but nothing exceptional. It wasn’t really an issue to ask for more rounds after finishing the tray.

I think with some adjustments, this deal could be worth going for.
Had a lovely lunch - the stone pot veggie and bibimbap special were good! The peppers with cheese as well but the other options felt a bit more exciting and flavorful

Stopped by for dinner before going to the theatre, it's on the third floor of kingly court but there are lifts, we got there at 5pm on a Saturday and got sat straight away but it did get a little busy from 6pm onwards. There was a great choice on the menu, everything was so tasty. The fried chicken was so crispy and delicious. I also really loved the cheesey peppers, it wasn't too spicy and still had loads of flavour, and the wedge salad was (surprisingly) my favourite dish!! Id recommend getting 4-5 dishes between 2, we also got 2 corn dogs and I think that was too much. Reasonable prices for the portion and quality. The staff were also really friendly and helpful, they made a mistake with one of our dishes but we're very quick to rectify it, id definitely recommend a visit here!

Overall, we found the food to be just ok, nothing special. Our experience was tainted by the unexpected service charge.

We did the tasting menu that had a lot of food but most of it tasted mediocre. The best thing was the kimchi stone pot stew and the slaw that comes with the tacos. Everything else - fried chicken, bacon mochi, cheese stuffed peppers, al pastor chicken, ice cream - all tasted pretty mediocre. The amount of mayo on fried chicken overwhelms anything else; the al pastor chicken tastes only of sweetness and it was served cold, not hot; the ice cream was super boring. Flavors were not on point, every dish felt like it was missing something. I wanted to like this restaurant in the name of Korean fusion food but unfortunately it missed the mark completely.

We paid at the end and after paying realized they had added a 12.5% service charge for our table of 2 persons. This was not mentioned when seated or ordering. So, on top of the mediocre food, this unexpected charge soured our experience. I doubt we’ll return.

Stumbled across this restaurant the a few weeks ago and decided to try it out today. Everything we ate was so delicious and of high quality! We ordered the wagyu salad and pork bone broth from the specials and then the grilled black cod. Everything was cooked and seasoned perfectly. The staff were really lovely and attentive and the restaurant is nice and clean. Only con was that the mocktails were too sweet but others may still love it. Defo coming back!

Came a year ago and loved every bite of the Matcha Crème Brûlée. Came back and tasted just as delicious. Has become an all time favourite now. Food and atmosphere is 10/10, super friendly and attentive staff, very warm and welcoming. Thank you, we will be back🤩

Great selection of food and great service. I’ve tried other BBQ spots in New Malden but I much prefer this one.
The spicy pork was full of flavour. I really enjoyed the fried chicken so ordered x2 portions.

This was such a wonderful Korean barbecue. The place is lovely and so are the staff. I would definitely recommend the fried chicken for starters and the dolsot bibimbap was the best I’ve had in a while.

The meats selection is really good and the seasoning is really good. Will definitely be going back soon!

Excellent quality, great flavours and helpful staff! Been there twice and loved what he had both times. Main highlights - fried chicken with the spicy sauce (I requested an upgrade to extra spicy and loved it); aubergine starter was delectable with it’s subtle flavours; we also enjoyed the BBQ a lot - we opted for the selection for 2 which came with pork and beef options. Spicy pork was a big hit at our table. We also tried to cucumber kimchi, which was delicious!

The second time we went there, we took our friends who have lived in Seoul for several years and visit there annually. They too loved it and said the food took them back to Seoul.

Both times we visited, the staff were super helpful and guided us well.
We are fortunate to have this gem in our neighbourhood.

places.name: YORI Piccadilly Circus Korean BBQ
places.editorial_summary: Compact restaurant serving traditional Korean cuisine & BBQ specialties in relaxed surrounds.

reviews.text: Wonderful place for Korean food in London ! We didn’t try the BBQ but standards plates, all delightful ! The tteokbokki and the pajeon were so good, as well as the soy garlic chicken bites. We tried different bibimbap and the tofu and sea food stew, so tasty and not too spicy, which was great for us ! Plates are really affordable in my opinion. And the service is great ! I highly recommend this place !

It was very easy to make reservation on Google Maps. We were craving for some Korean barbecue and we ordered the beef selection.

Some of the smaller pieces come with very nice marble however the quantity wasn’t that much there is a piece of bigger steak, and some other that are marinated.

When we first put the meat on the grill, the grill wasn’t completely heated up so the steak wasn’t the best and no staff told us when the grill  would be ready.

On top of that we ordered a Seaford pancake, mushroom fried glass noodle and a soup with rice.

The rice wine in a bowl is a must to order. It is very delicious and with low alcohol percentage.

We had a very nice time there drinking rice wine and eating. Three of us and we had a full tummy.

It was £120 for 3, not bad for London price, especially we had alcohol.

Took my daughter here for a celebration meal We went for the set barbecue (chicken) we also got beef, 2 rices and some kimchi glass of coke and a big water total £82 lovely atmosphere, great customer service.My only downfall is if 2 people are going the tables aren't big enough apart from that I lovely experience

Popped in for a quick pre-theatre meal without a reservation, and the staff couldn’t have been more accommodating - managed to seat us promptly and made it all feel easy. The service throughout was excellent.

We ordered the bibimbap and doenjang jjigae - both comforting, well-seasoned, and full of flavour. The drinks deserve a mention too: the strawberry and lychee Yori highballs were refreshing and not overly sweet.

Great spot if you’re in the area! Efficient, friendly, and reliably good food. Would definitely come back.

We came here because it was kid friendly. They had a lovely kids meal. It was rice with vegetables and egg on top, and served with a side of dumplings. Our chicken and beef dishes were delicious. We even ordered an extra bowl of kimchi because it was so good. Highly recommend, we will be back.

places.name: Bibimbap Soho
places.editorial_summary: Bright, modern eatery serving multiple varieties of the signature Korean mixed rice dish.

reviews.text:
I had a fantastic time at this restaurant, which offers delicious and authentic Korean cuisine.

We ordered several dishes, including bibimbap, sweet and spicy Korean fried chicken, and the spicy rice cakes tteokbokki, all of which were tasty. My favourite dish was the fried tofu bibimbap, which paired wonderfully with their iced plum tea.

I highly recommend visiting this place!
Minimalism interior eat-in Place in really nice location. Love the atmosphere and here we enjoyed Bibimbap. A rainbow colour of rice and veggie. Will try Bingsu next time.

Tried Bibimbap in Soho for the first time. It’s a small Korean spot with great food and fast service. I had the chicken bibimbap, which is halal and was served in a hot iron bowl—delicious and fresh. I was honestly surprised how quickly it came after ordering. Staff were friendly and polite throughout. Spent £23 for the meal and an apple juice. Worth it. Will definitely go again.
Lovely authentic Korean food. Quick and friendly service. Food made fresh and very tasty for a quick bite before going to the Theatre. Recommend the chilli squid and chilli fried chicken.

Perfectly sized menu with enough options for everyone.
Great warm bowls with rice, veritable and chicken/meat, amazing flavor and satisfying size.
Great Koren beer and amazing dumplings.
Highly recommend for a light dinner.

places.name: Daebak
places.editorial_summary: Korean staples, such as fried chicken, rice dishes and noodles, served in a chill, wood-clad space.

reviews.text:
Really good Korean fried chicken. They're deboned, so the portions are huge. Ordering the half-and-half on my own (especially on top of the seafood pancake) was a mistake. I bagged half of it for take out, ordering that much was definitely enough for 2.5 people. I went for the Yang Nyeum and sweet cheese powder. The former is better, but the latter isn't bad.

Came at an 4pm on a Saturday so there was no queue. They also don't take reservations past 6pm. Really kind service.

Food is pretty good here! My partner liked it a lot, me not that much, hence why I took off 1 star, but I think it's a matter of taste. What I do want to point out is that the pieces of fried chicken are pretty good and satiating so even if you feel tempted to get the big portion, if you're also getting a side dish my advice would be to get the medium one for 2 people. At the end the food felt a bit too greasy for me but again I think it's just my opinion.

Daebak – A Fun Spot for Soju and Korean Bites Near Vauxhall
Daebak is a great little restaurant if you’re near Vauxhall and in the mood for Korean food and soju. The vibe is casual and lively—perfect for sharing dishes and drinks with friends.

Starters
We tried the Spinach Namul and Beansprouts Namul. Both were flavourful and nicely seasoned, though a touch too salty for my taste.

Mains
Pa Dak (Spring Onion Fried Chicken)
The fried chicken was perfectly crispy without feeling too greasy, and the spring onion topping added a refreshing bite. Great texture and balance—especially with a shot of soju on the side!

Bibimbap with Soy Chicken & Egg
This came with a generous portion—definitely enough to share. The soy chicken was well-marinated, and the bibimbap arrived with a side of miso soup. Overall tasty, but again, a bit on the salty side.

Final Thoughts
Daebak is a solid choice if you're looking to drink soju and enjoy some Korean comfort food to go with it. If you're visiting just for the food and not drinking, some dishes might come across a bit salty. But if you’re pairing it with drinks and good company—it hits the spot.
Excellent. Food is tasty & waitress was great, now I know where to feed my KFC addiction.

Loving little place in Vauxhall… went there before night out and had the set menu for £22. Was so much food and great to try a few different things. Will definitely go back and do this again when I have plans in Vauxhall.

We chose Miga to celebrate our anniversary, hoping for a special experience — but unfortunately, we left quite disappointed.

We ordered six dishes: hwe, maeun saeu, yukhwe, galbijjim, oligogi tangsuyuk, and seolleongtang, which was never brought to us despite being ordered.

Service was inconsistent. One waiter (a young man with a European appearance) was genuinely excellent — attentive and kind, and we truly appreciated him. However, the other waiter  called my boyfriend ( who is also Korean) “oppa” in front of me, which I found completely unprofessional and inappropriate, especially given that we were clearly a couple. It made the atmosphere uncomfortable.

Food-wise, it was underwhelming. The galbijjim was the only dish we really enjoyed. The yukhwe was the biggest disappointment — both in taste and presentation. The overall quality simply didn’t match the hype or the pricing.

Honestly, the place feels overrated and overpriced. There are far better, more authentic Korean restaurants in London that offer better food and atmosphere for the same — or even less — money.

Sadly, I don’t think we’ll be returning. And definitely not worth to visit.

Lunch for 2 at Miga, Hackney. Our order: fried chicken thigh, sliced raw fish w/ rice, soy braised beef short ribs w/ rice, a bowl of ox bone broth, tea & a Cass beer. The meat dishes were exceptional (especially the galbi) and customer service was excellent. Our total bill for 2 was about £95. Highly recommended.

Unfortunately this place did not live up to its hype for me. The portions were small, flavours were underwhelming and I’ve definitely tasted better for cheaper at more affordable traditional Korean restaurants in London.

The starters were good - I liked the sashimi paired with the sauce. The tofu was also really good.

Beef ribs were tasty but I found the portions way too small. Did not like the beef stew - lacked depth and flavour with a strange after taste. The beef noodles were also very average.

Overall a very average experience.

Very good Korean restaurant with a very good value. Very attentive staff.

After visiting South Korea and falling in love with its cuisine, we gave a shot at this Michelin’s bib gourmand restaurant and it was a success.

Both, starters and mains were perfect.

Good food, poor service. The guy who served us told us that there was a problem with our order, so we ended up waiting almost an hour for our food. Our reservation was for 1:30 which we were on time for and ordered probably 5/10 minutes later and didn’t get our first dish until 2:15 which is fine but we the next dish came at 2:28 and the one after that came at 2:32. They close at 3 and were rushing us for the bill, I wasn’t able to finish the soup or my meal comfortably. I really wanted to remove the service charge but we were in such a rush that it completely slipped my mind. They were rushing us that I didn’t even have time to go to the toilet.  To expect us to finish two main dishes in less than 30 minutes, and when we spent more time waiting for our food than actually eating is a bit silly. They removed two of our drinks from the bill but I ended up ordering another one since I had drunk most of my first one while waiting.
Very disappointing service to be honest, the server just made it worse. I was turning my head towards the kitchen just to see what was going on as it’s not normal to be waiting so long and our server was just watching me the entire time. I could not comfortably enjoy my food at all, that being said the food is good and if we had a different server or experience I am sure the rating will be at least 4 stars. But to rush us for your mistake is very silly to be honest. Can’t say I want to be back, my friends were also looking forward to visiting since the food looked so good but not sure if I would want to recommend…

places.name: Kimchimama
places.vicinity: Mary Queen of Scots House, 142 Fleet St, London

reviews.text: Very lovely staff and the owners wife was also there to suggest food! There was nothing on the table that didn't taste good. Highly recommend if you want some easy-going Korean food.

My wife, our baby boy and I came here twice for lunch in April 2025.

The food is super fresh and delicious! The staff is very friendly and professional. If you happen to meet the owner he will take the time for a little chat and tells you the beautiful history of the restaurant.

We will definitely be back!

The best Korean restaurant I’ve been to in London! Both the chicken and the stews were amazing. The tteokbokki was sweet and spicy, and the cheese hot dogs are something I definitely want to have again. I feel like every item on the menu would be delicious. On top of that, the staff were incredibly friendly!

I had the kimchi stew, and its spicy, rich flavor really brought out the authentic taste of Korean food. This is my go-to place whenever I crave kimchi stew. They’ve recently started selling Asahi beer—I tried it, and it was crisp and refreshing. Next time, I’d love to enjoy it with some chicken.
We went in to try something new. The place was empty. The food was very good, everything was perfect. I had the Korean fried chicken Cupbap and it was delicious. I highly recommend it.

places.name: Assa
places.editorial_summary: Laid-back eatery serving rice bowls, hot pot & other Korean comfort foods, plus beer, sake & wine.

reviews.text:
I had a great time at Assa! The place felt cozy and welcoming 😊. The food was super tasty 🇰🇷—full of real, bold flavors.

The staff were kind and helpful, and made sure we understood the menu 👍. You can tell they care about their food and guests.

Whether you're trying Korean food for the first time or love it already, this spot is worth visiting. I’ll be back soon! 👏

The food was delicious, I would definitely come back again to try other items on the menu. The restaurant is walk in only, the queue does move fast. The staff are very attentive and the food came out very quick despite being super busy. From the flavours to the portion size, this place did not disappoint and it was halal.

I come here at least once a month because the food is delicious and priced well. My favourites are the beef bulgogi, the scallion pancakes and the boneless chicken in sweet and spicy sauce. Their drinks selection is really impressive as they have a wide range of flavours. I like the lychee soda personally. The service is very quick, I gave the atmosphere 3* as it's quite packed and loud in there but I guess that's what makes it so reasonably priced. Always looking forward to coming here ❤️

not gonna lie, I walked in kinda skeptical… but then I saw actual Koreans eating there and was like 👀 this place is legit. And omg the food?? So good. The prices?? Literally unreal. Like how is it this cheap?? And in London!! Definitely coming back.

-written by a millennial trying to be a Gen z ✨

Assa

Located in Soho, is a favourite for those craving authentic Korean food in central London. Known for its hearty hot pots, flavourful bibimbap, and crisp kimchi pancakes, the restaurant delivers bold, satisfying dishes at prices that feel fair for the area. The casual setting, lively atmosphere, and quick service make it a great choice for groups or anyone after a vibrant dining experience without the polish of fine dining.

On the flip side, Assa’s popularity means it often gets crowded, with tight seating and noise levels that won’t suit all diners  seeking quiet meal or intimate meal. Some dishes can be hit-or-miss, but the highlights more than make up for it, keeping regulars coming back. For authentic flavours served in a bustling, energetic space, Assa remains one of Soho’s most reliable Korean food spots.

Personally , we loved the food and experience.

places.name: Cu4tro Restaurant & Tequila Bar
places.formatted_address: 21 Great Windmill St, London W1D 7LB, UK

reviews.text:
Located just a couple of minutes’ walk from Shaftesbury Avenue and the heart of Theatreland, and about five minutes from Piccadilly Circus, Cu4tro is a relatively new Mexican restaurant that’s been open for around four months.

The interior is spread across two floors — the bar and a few tables occupy the ground level, with additional seating upstairs. We were seated at a table for three on the first floor, which unfortunately hadn’t been properly cleaned — there were crumbs on the surface, and it felt a bit sticky.

We started with margaritas, but both the classic and mango versions were overly sweet and unbalanced, lacking the refreshing tartness you’d expect.

The Nachos con Guac were underwhelming — both the portion size and the flavour were average, with guacamole that didn’t stand out.

For mains, we tried a few dishes:
•	El Pescador (crispy fish, creamy slaw, pico de gallo, coriander, and house mayo served with salsa verde) — the taco arrived lukewarm, and the fish wasn’t particularly crispy.
•	Burrito King of Flavour (Mexican-style rice, cheese, lettuce, creamy slaw, black beans, pulled pork) — the pulled pork was fine, but overall the flavours felt muted.
•	Backstreet Tacos (pulled pork) — again, fairly average, and the fries on the side were limp with an oddly sour sauce.

Churros was also too oily and too much sugar on it with the accompanying chocolate sauce was inedible!

Service on the first floor was patchy — staff only appeared when bringing dishes, and there were noticeable gaps between courses. Payment is taken at the exit, though this wasn’t explained, so we sat waiting at the table for a while before finding out.

Overall, Cu4tro feels like it’s still finding its footing. The atmosphere is fine, but both food and service need polishing. If compared to a fast-casual Mexican benchmark like Wahaca, it would sit below that level in both quality and consistency.

It you're looking for purist Mexican food then this is not the place for you. Good for people keeping an open mind on Mexican cuisine. We had a small misunderstanding about our order but the server was super nice! Food fresh and tasty.

We had a good food here, we ordered many different tacos and quesadillas, most of them were great, however, i think we should had more compared to the price we payed, and two dishes were alright.
The staff are nice and friendly, the place is clean and looks good.

Great food and drinks, the staff are helpful and attentive, and just the right ambiance to have an intimate yet casual chat. After a minor hiccup with the bill, Andre was quick to respond and resolve it with me. Now that is what exceptional service is! Definitely worth coming back to.
This place is the place to go, food was amazing, worth it 100%. Michael was amazing, full of humour and great service. Recommend 100%

places.name: Mestizo Mexican Restaurant & Tequila Bar
places.editorial_summary: Fine Mexican cuisine plus tequila shots and cocktails in smart, scarlet space.

reviews.text: We went to this restaurant to celebrate my mother-in-law’s birthday, and everything was absolutely amazing! The atmosphere was warm and welcoming, and the food was delicious from start to finish. What really made the evening extra special were the two waiters who looked after us. They were attentive, friendly, and went out of their way to make sure we had everything we needed. They even made my mother-in-law feel celebrated, which meant so much to us. Their professionalism and kindness truly elevated the whole experience. Thank you for such wonderful service—we’ll definitely be back! Special thanks to Damian and Hatzy

Tasty Mexican food which changes from your typical London chain and has some proper special dishes like mole etc. We had salsas with totopos for starter and then for main tried the 3 different enchiladas: a mix of verde and rojo, the mole and Cancun. Great service, delicious margaritas (recommend the jalapeño and tamarind!).
The only downside perhaps is that it’s really loud downstairs

Had lunch here today with my husband (who’s Mexican). Food was incredible. We normally have a difficult time finding good Mexican food around Europe. My husband even said the tamales tasted just like his mom’s. Juan Carlos was our waiter and he was super friendly. Will definitely be going back as often as we can

This was my first time coming here from a recommendation from a friend and it did not disappoint. The staff were just delightful from the second we walked in, Hatzy and Richard were so friendly it made the experience worth while even before we had ordered our drinks! I couldn’t recommend this place enough! They even gave us a free shot each to celebrate our anniversary. We will definitely be back!! Oo make sure you order the taco sharing platter!

We had a lovely dinner here on a Saturday night with a couple of friends. All the staff were helpful, diligent and friendly. Our waiters Richard and Roger kindly explained what the best combinations of drinks and food would be and we left with a happy heart and a full belly. A dinner for four cost us £210 (incl service charge). We had the taco tray and the other sharing option, 2 bowls of guac and totopos, a bottle of red and a couple of cocktails. I recommend this place if you love Mexican food and tequila!

FONDA is an upscale, modern Mexican restaurant that specializes in what I would call classics with a twist.

The menu is designed so that each guest should order 3-4 plates and share. It’s a great way to sample many menu items.

We ordered as instructed by the very knowledgeable server and were blown way by the quality and flavor combinations of every dish!

We washed everything down with Fonda Margaritas.

The only drawback is that FONDA is not just expensive it is VERY expensive, socially considering this is Mexican cuisine.

I love Mexican and am willing to pay for great food. (Which I did). I did not expect to walk about paying £428 for 4 people.

Would I go back? Yes, because it was that delicious. I would focus more on the larger mains and less on the small tapas plates that require multiple orders per item to feed the table so they add up quickly!!
Example: £10 for a small plate but then the server advises we order 1 plate per customer so that one “starter” alone was £40.

Second time dining out this week where an automatic 15% gratuity was added to the bill.

This is becoming more and more common here. It’s too bad. There was always something refreshing about the 10-12% gratuity cap. Feeling more like the US these days.

From hearing about this restaurant on the Off Menu podcast I had very high expectations. I can honestly say these expectations were exceeded threefold. The staff were so genuinely passionate about their food and felt so proud to share it - I can see why though it was fantastic. Never did I think I would enjoy a pumpkin seed dip but it was one of the best things I’ve eaten. I can’t wait to go back (hopefully the cheesecake will be back on the menu by then!!!)

We had lunch at Fonda yesterday and were truly impressed by the whole experience. The location itself is beautiful — stylish and welcoming, with a lovely atmosphere that made us feel comfortable and relaxed right away.

The staff were incredibly kind and attentive from the moment we arrived. Their warm hospitality and willingness to help with recommendations really stood out and added a personal touch to our meal.

As for the food — it was simply outstanding. We ordered a variety of dishes to get a good sense of the menu, and every single one exceeded our expectations. Each plate was not only visually appealing but packed with flavor and clearly prepared with high-quality ingredients. It’s clear that the chefs at Fonda take great pride in their work.

Overall, it was a wonderful dining experience. Great location, amazing food, and exceptional service — we couldn’t have asked for more. We’re already looking forward to our next visit!

It’s been a long time since I’ve enjoyed everything about a restaurant. The food was absolutely delicious—the pumpkin seed mole, carnitas, and churros are must-haves. The decor is lovely, and the music creates a pleasant atmosphere without making conversation difficult. Most importantly, the service was perfect. Every staff member we spoke to was friendly and gave great explanations for each dish. The service charge is higher than usual (15%), but it’s well deserved. Fonda, thank you for a wonderful evening—I will definitely be back!

Food, totally delicious!
Service, exquisite!
Decor, visually pleasing much!
Ambiance, delightful.
Would I visit again....Absolutely!
Definitely recommend.
( I didn't take photos of all 6 dishes as I was too busy enjoying the experience.)

places.name: Wahaca Covent Garden
places.editorial_summary: Mexican restaurant with a lively soundtrack for small plates of market-style food & cocktails.

reviews.text:
The menu was expansive and if you're like us and you're not sure what to order, go for the 'Feasting Menu'. It says it's for two but we could share two sets amongst 5 of us, 3 below 15 years old.

The highlight for us were the vegetarian options such as the Sweet Potato & Feta Taquito. The sweet potato was baked and the insides were creamy and sweet. Topped with feta cheese, tomatoes and a mixture of sauces (I have no idea what!) and they just go so well. The Beet Tartare Tostadas was also a splendid surprise. Buttermilk Chicken Tacos and Grilled Brindisa Chorizo Quesadilla were our faves as well.

Just make sure that you make reservations on their website. We were there on a Friday evening and I heard that it was an hour wait if you walk-in.

I can’t recommend Wuhaca in Covent Garden enough. As someone who lives for great vegetarian and vegan food, I found myself returning at least once a day just to try more of their incredible dishes -each one bursting with creativity and flavour.

What makes the experience even better is the team who works there. The staff aren’t just friendly; they’re vibrant, caring, and they clearly enjoy working together, which creates an atmosphere that’s uplifting to be around. By the time you leave, you don’t just feel like a customer- you feel hugged, held, and genuinely cared for.

Wuhaca is more than a restaurant; it’s a place where good food and good people come together in the best way.

We recently celebrated my brother’s birthday at Wahaca, and it was a fantastic experience from start to finish. Even though we arrived without a reservation at 18:30 on August 27th, the hostess greeted us warmly and ensured we were comfortable throughout the evening. The vibrant atmosphere and delicious Mexican cuisine made our meal truly memorable. The staff’s friendly service, especially our hostess, made the occasion special—we hope she knows how much we appreciated her help.

The exterior looks great and makes you definitely want to see inside.
I had the chicken burrito and it was delicious. It had a nice atmosphere but it was very loud yet still easy to talk.
The main complaint was that the waiter was a bit rude and impatient.

Wahaca is truly Mexican hitting the right spice levels making for a satisfying gastronomic experience. Big shout out to Paulina for making this a delicious and memorable meal for us. Thank you 🙏.

The corona was served ice cold. We requested Paulina to suggest vegetarian options and I’m glad we asked her. The summer veggie set menu came with cactus and courgette tacos, black bean quesadilla, beet root tostada, sweet potato taquito, crispy cauliflower, halloumi taco and avocado and cos salad. This is amazing value for money considering the deliciousness of the food and location.

places.name: Santo Remedio - Asador, London Bridge
places.editorial_summary: Modern take on Mexican street food with casual, idiosyncratic vibe and a creative drinks menu.

reviews.text: We came here with friends and had an amazing evening. We had no reservation but were offered a table right away. The food was amazing and the service was great! Olivia was very attentive and even kept up with us constantly switching between Spanish and English :) many thanks, seguramente volveremos pronto!

Delicious food and great service! My friend and I went for the £44pp tasting menu, which was a fantastic way to sample a variety of dishes. Both my friend and I used to say that we aren't Mexican food fans but we were obviously eating rubbish, this food is exceptional.

The tuna tostada was the standout for me absolutely bursting with flavor.  We had the beef short rib and absolutely every single ingredient owns its space on the dish. Who would have thought plantain and feta cheese go well together?!

The hibiscus margarita was amazing too, super refreshing. Love the fresh guacamole, I regularly order it just to enjoy at home.

The space is cute, homely, and not at all pretentious. Highly recommend, and I will be back in the very near future.

Food tasted good, the reason why my review is only 3 stars was because the prices were just too much for the serving. Serving of the seabass ceviche was so cute, looked like it was a lot on the plate but the plate was super flat. Tacos were good but so tiny, the lamb shank was amazing probably the only reason why I added 2 more stars. We were also shocked that there was a service fee on top plus the tip 💀 Felt like we were only paying for the "Michelin" on the front of their entrance nothing else.

Santo Remedio delivers on its promise of fantastic, authentic Mexican flavors—from tacos and tuna tostadas to beautifully plated sharing dishes, the food really stands out. Unfortunately, that culinary high point is somewhat dampened by inconsistent service—several requests went unnoticed. The restaurant’s lively, colorful interior sets a fun mood!! And the churros were absolutely wonderful!! soft, melty, and perfect. All in all, a great spot for a food-focused outing.

I thank everyone for their warm welcome. • "The menu showcases the best of Mexican cuisine, with authentic dishes bursting with flavor."
• "The options are varied, going far beyond the basics, and demonstrate a commitment to representing authentic gastronomy."

We had a most memorable experience and meal, went there for El Pastor and Friends with Elena Reygadas.

The food was absolutely fantastic, especially dessert. Drinks were great. Staff is so kind, welcoming, friendly, and attentive, and goes above and beyond. Special thanks to Juan and Mary.

Music selection was great, and ambiance really takes you back to Mexico City. The place does get noisy, but everything else was so good that we didn’t mind.

The pictures really don’t do the food justice. Everything was spectacular.

El Pastor in Soho is a fantastic spot for authentic Mexican food in London. Their salsas with totopos are a must-try, and the tacos and chicken tostadas were full of flavor. Great atmosphere and delicious food, we’ll definitely be back!

My friend and I went there for a cosy lunch, we booked through The Fork and we had 30% off on the food. It was our first time and I have to say that the service is very efficient and all the staff is very polite. The food is fresh and tasty and we shared few dishes. The drinks are tequila's based with different combinations of fruits and flavours. I would definitely recommend this place.

Great experience all round

It was busy, bustling and tables are tight, but it didn’t feel like a squeeze or too on top at all, just a nice convivial space with a breezy atmosphere, high ceilings but no harsh sounds; it’s a well put together place

Service was superb; everyone that came to our table were affable, knowledgeable and seemed in control of the floor. Really gives you confidence in a meal when everyone seems happy and relaxed whilst being so busy

Mini carafes of interesting mezcals, Mexican beers, great guacamole, some excellent tacos (brisket was a little flat tasting, but the rest were lovely) and all the salsas were ace

Thought the pricing was spot on for what we got

This is officially my favourite El Pastor location. The food was outstanding, we loved everything we ordered and the staff were attentive and helpful. I recommend the Charred Pork Quesadilla, & the Short Rib to share with bottomless tortillas.

We came here for my birthday and was the perfect atmosphere - we were treated with a complimentary dessert as well / staff were very kind.

The star of the show was the beautifully set vibe of the whole restaurant, but the food was equally impressive. The shrimp tacos was my favorite personally and the crab tostadas was my partner’s. We also got a t-bone with a side of potatoes and fresh, warm tortillas which we definitely recommend - meat was very tender, juicy, and seasoned.

Has become my favorite Mexican restaurant in London but is a little bit on the pricier side if you’re looking to get a casual bite.

We had such a lovely Sunday lunch at Ixchel. The restaurant itself is stunning, right on King’s Road, with thoughtful design touches everywhere (even the bathrooms are gorgeous!).

The food was seriously impressive—everything we ordered was so flavourful and beautifully presented. The fish tacos were a real standout and perfectly balanced. You could tell each dish had been prepared with real care and attention to detail. We also noticed a really lovely private dining space downstairs, which looked ideal for a more intimate celebration.

Although the service was a little on the slower side, we honestly didn’t mind. It suited the pace of a long, relaxed lunch, and our servers were genuinely kind and attentive, clearly wanting to make our experience a great one.

We finished with the tres leches cake and it was truly exceptional. Will be thinking about it for a long time!

Ixchel is such a great find—fantastic food, a beautiful atmosphere, and ideal for a slow, indulgent afternoon with good company. We’ll absolutely be back.

Though the space can get lively, the energy adds to the experience. It creates an atmosphere where you can enjoy a fun, social vibe without it ever becoming overwhelming or uncomfortable. Conversations flow easily, and the overall mood is joyful and relaxed.

Whether you’re stopping by for a casual meal, a special occasion, or just looking to try something different, this place delivers on all fronts. With its remarkable food, top-tier service, and inviting ambiance, it leaves a lasting impression. Highly recommended for anyone seeking a truly special dining experience.

Came in for dessert and a drink. We were welcomed by the lovely Jalal who immediately made us feel at home. We ordered the tres leches cake, which was an absolute delight. The restaurant is beautiful and the atmosphere is quite appropriate. We loved it!

Wow, this place is amazing!!! I couldn't recommend it more - definitely one of my new favourite spots in London! The food was exquisite, sooo delicious!! There was something for everyone - lots of vegetarian options too. The salsa was actually super spicy, hard to find these days - so yummm! The wine was incredible too. The staff were super friendly and helpful. I'd have to say the best part is the ambiance - I couldn't get enough of the decor!!!

places.name: Los Mochis London City
places.vicinity: Liverpool Street Station, 100 Liverpool St, London

reviews.text: Took our daughter here for her 18th birthday lunch. And what a lunch it was. We were welcomed right from start and ushered to our table right away. The place is huge and we were surprised at its size. The service was great - attentive, helpful and prompt (without feeling rushed). The cocktails were spot on and we did have quite a few - Tikki Tulum, Tokyo Trailblazer, Tropical Paloma and Pelino Jalapeño Margarita. We were disappointed that a couple of unique cocktails such as the bartender’s competition drink were not available (though they were on the menu). The best part was the food. The starters - asparagus yakiniku, chipotle calamari, truffle guacamole on crispy rice and shiitake, left us smacking our lips and craving for more. The main course was equally good - dynamite prawn and courgette dynamite tacos were yummy. To top off a great afternoon, our daughter was surprised with a complimentary birthday dessert and sake, which made her very happy. We will be back for more.

We visited Los Mochis London City and tried a selection of small plates alongside a couple of cocktails. I did however go with someone who unfortunately doesn't like seafood (so there's a lack of sushi in this review - but luckily Los Mochis caters for all).

For food, the chipotle calamari was good, though I’ve had better elsewhere. The chipotle mayo that came with it was delicious & smokey which made all the difference. The pato on crispy rice (duck) had a tasty batter but was quite heavy, making it tricky to eat with chopsticks but I still thoroughly enjoyed it. The chutoro (medium fatty bluefin tuna) melted on my tongue. Both the shrimp tempura maki rolls and the dynamite prawn tacos were excellent, with the tacos easily my favourite dish of the night: sweet, spicy, and perfectly balanced.

For drinks, the Pepino Jalapeño cocktail was outstanding. Unlike similar versions I’ve had elsewhere, it was refreshing, light, and had just the right gentle kick. It was so good I had to order it again. The margarita was a safe but smooth classic.

Service was polite and attentive throughout. They are strict with table timings, and once our time was up, they kindly moved us over to the bar so we could continue our evening without feeling rushed.

Something I don’t usually review, but worth mentioning: the restrooms. They were impressive - clean, stylish, and with a refreshing yet relaxing ambiance. I love when a restaurant makes a statement with its facilities, and Los Mochis definitely delivered on that.

Overall, Los Mochis offers a great mix of creative Japanese-Mexican dishes, fantastic cocktails, and stylish surroundings. A spot worth visiting, especially for the dynamite prawn tacos, Pepino Jalapeño cocktail, and yes, even the restrooms.

Went with a friend to Los Mochis, we were originally booked for the sushi counter and asked on arrival if there were any standard tables available. They were able to accommodate us straight away and gave us a table next to the window.  We had a selection of dishes as it's small sharing plates paired with a few cocktails. We really enjoyed the food, really good quality and you could taste the different flavours in each dish. Very vibey with a house ambiance on a Friday night. Good for a high end London city date night.
I highly rate the service, they were great at offering recommendations on drinks and dessert and I was able to charge my phone for a bit at the front desk. Also can't not mention a view of St Paul's in the distance.

Amazing 100% gluten free menu. I walked in and sat at the terrace bar because I was by myself but highly recommend a reservation.
The drinks were wonderful. The food was incredible. But they take service to a new level. I would say you pay for the quality, experience and location, but found it fine what’s offered. Will return to try more food because the whole menu looked great.

I came with a friend for her birthday and it was incredible. Our table was for 3pm which we thought wouldn’t be too busy but when we got there we were surprised to see lots of full tables! Despite the restaurant being busy, the team worked incredibly well to keep everything running smoothly and we didn’t have to wait for long to order or for our food to come out.

As soon as we tasted the food we understood why they were busy and for good reason. The food was incredible in both taste and texture and I almost couldn’t believe that it was 100% gluten free! As someone with coeliac it’s such a relief to find restaurants that are totally gluten free, especially when their food is also incredible. To top off the incredible dining experience we had, they brought out a free birthday dessert for my friend. All in all an amazing experience and I can’t wait to come back again.

places.name: Mestizo Chelsea: Mexican Restaurant & Margarita Bar

reviews.text: Had a wonderful dinner here with friends. We all went for the Taco Tuesday offer of unlimited tacos. As a pescatarian there were plenty of veggie options to choose from. The time in between ordering your tacos and getting the next ones was not too long. Our waiter Damian was also great, very knowledgeable and attentive.

First Time at Mestizo – Blown Away!

I’d never been to an authentic Mexican restaurant before, but after hearing my colleagues talk about how amazing Mestizo is, I had to check it out..and I’m so glad I did! The food was seriously delicious and looked just as good as it tasted.

The place itself has a really cool vibe, perfect for a Friday lunch that eased us right into the weekend. Big shoutout to Prasun who looked after us..his service was spot on and really made the experience even better.

If you’re after some proper good Mexican food and a great atmosphere, I’d definitely recommend giving Mestizo a try. I’ll be back for sure!

Had a lovely experience with my family Saturday afternoon, it was my mother in laws pre birthday dinner.
We particularly enjoyed the atmosphere, which was more informal than expected.  Alberto was our main server, he has a really lovely character and made us felt at ease and respected. He spent time talking us through the menu and guided us to what would suit our group, this is reflected in his staff as well, who are incredibly professional and clearly take pride in their work. We enjoyed our meal (amazing volcano hot pot to share) and as it was a surprise birthday meal, we were given good treatment with dessert and a surprise performance that made my mother in law smiling. Highly recommend this place, we would definitely go back, we were all left feeling content with smiles. Alberto was a fantastic host and super attentive.

Had a great experience at Mestizo! The food was delicious and full of authentic flavor, and the atmosphere was lively and welcoming. Our server William provided excellent service — friendly, attentive, and made great recommendations. Overall, a wonderful meal and experience. Will definitely be back!

Loved it here!

Our waiter was lovely and took his time to explain his favourites on the menu and chat to us. We got 2 for 1 frozen Margaritas (can’t complain) and the food was tasty and I didn’t think it was overpriced as you got a decent amount of everything. I will be coming back to try more of the menu.

places.name: El Pastor
places.editorial_summary: Tacos al pastor & other South American–inspired food & drinks served in buzzy, colourful digs.

reviews.text: A fun, casual, and delicious spot in Borough Market serving up tasty tacos, guacamole, ceviche and more. We got the beef brisket tacos which comes with salsa verde, al pastor tacos, and agave prawn tacos which were a special. There’s not a lot of filling in each taco so if you’re hungry, order a couple more. The prawn tacos could use a little more flavour, but get yourself a sauce on the side and you’re good. The service was so nice, prompt, and attentive. Also try the mezcal!

Fantastic Mexican food. Started with nacho’s with a choice of 5 dips, watch the hot one, it’s very hot!  I had soft shell crab tacos and then shredded beef tacos. Both were good, but the crab was the best. If you want quiet this isn’t the place for you, it was noisy and busy but that added to the great atmosphere. The staff were also great.

This was my first Mexican restaurant in London, and it did not disappoint.
I adored the crab tacos, al pastor, and the limited crispy potato. The corn cake was just perfect—nothing to add.
If you can’t handle spicy food, just ask them for recommendations. The staff were really helpful and super nice.
A bit expensive, but worth it.

Incredible tacos in an excellent spot to watch the passing traffic. I would say that that they were quite pricy and definitely added up at the end. Still, the tacos were very juicy and tender. We did have to wait around 5 minutes but I recommend if you are ever visiting the Borough Market.

We love this place and even though it is not the cheapest, it is worth it for the quality of the food.

The crab tostadas and tuna tostadas are superb as are the various tacos.

The roasted pineapple salsa is simply sublime and each of the taco dishes are individually spiced to differentiate between them.

places.name: Loco Mexicano
places.formatted_address: 64-65 Wilton Rd, Pimlico, London SW1V 1DE, UK
places.editorial_summary: Upbeat, party-style Cuban/Mexican-themed bar and salsa club for tequila, tacos and nachos.

reviews.text: Loved the place. Just had the spicy beef nachos and spicy chicken nachos and both were tasty and amazing, well sized portions as well. Excellent service from staff and thoroughly enjoyed the evening. Place was super busy but waited for it to empty a bit to take photos

This restaurant has a fun atmosphere and friendly staff. We appreciated that they were willing to make a special margarita we requested, though my partner had to go up to the bar to place the order. The food was fresh and flavourful — the pulled pork was tasty but a bit too wet for our liking. Overall, a good spot for casual Mexican fare with great drink options.

This place is amazing, absolutely well worth a visit. The food was fantastic and the pitcher of margaritas was pretty good too🤣 the staff was so friendly and provided some sombreros for our entertainment! But behind all the fun the food was truly excellent.

Booked for 7 ppl to celebrate 2 birthdays. Even though the reviews were mixed, as mostly was quite promising we braved ourselves to try out this place.
The Good(s):
Atmosphere is quite Mexican theme, nice and had various art on the wall with good music. They have these Mexican hats which creates quirky fun for the diners.
Food were all decent portions - nachos were great, so was the prawns we had and BBQ ribs and wings.
The food was all edible - everything was nice but not really a wow factor that makes me think, I want to come back here again.
The Bad(s):
We wanted to get Starters sharer platter of 4 and they had beef as part of it but our family do not eat beef. We asked if we could exchange to another meat but the chef didn't allow, not even we offered to pay extra. And due to limitations, its either this platter or vegetarian platter.
