Bubala is giving organic/healthy meets sexy/sultry and I am positively OBSESSED! ❤️‍🔥

• LOCATION:📍Soho (they also have locations in King’s Cross and their OG spot in Spitalfields!)

• DISH OF THE DAY: without a single doubt the baba ganoush - we were salivating over the rich depth of flavour 🤤 Special mention also has to be made for the smacked cucumbers - wow! 🥒

• FLAVOUR: 12/10 - foodie witchcraft. Outstanding flavours! Creative, unique, moreish x1000 🔥

• PRESENTATION: 10/10 - beautiful, and authentic feeling! Perfect for sharing

• VALUE FOR MONEY: the set/tasting menu can feel a little pricey but if there are just 2 of you I think it’s worth it. For £33/pp for 5 of us, including wine, we were stoked (and very full!)

• SERVICE: 8.5/10 - our waitress was very sweet! Food came at the perfect pace

• VIBES: 8.5/10 - it’s moody and earthy which feels so on-brand! Both their Spitalfields and Soho locations do feel a bit cramped but that’s just London buildings for ya!

• GOOGLE RATING: 4.6 - could even see this being higher 👀

• BEST FOR: Middle Eastern food, sharing plates, veggies/vegans, flavour-packed dishes

• WOULD I RECOMMEND IT TO A FOODIE FRIEND? Legit my fave foodie spot in London 🫳 🎤

If you are looking for DAILY videos on the best places to EAT, SEE and VISIT as a foodie then come find me on socials @octavia.overseas! 💁🏼‍♀️🇪🇸💫

🚨 You can also download my Foodie Google Maps Guides totally for FREE from my IG/TikTok bio! 🗺️

Gorgeous gorgeous vegetarian and vegan meal. First time here and I can't fault it. The service was warm, attentive and friendly, nothing was too much. I wish I had made a note of the 3 people who served us, I think one was the manager. They were so helpful about the 'Bubala knows best' set menu and accommodating with a vegan and vegetarian mix for the 3 of us.

The food is incredibly tasty. We all loved it. Each dish tastes different and I couldn't choose a favourite. The mango and chilli drink is delicious.

I can't wait to go back and a cookbook is coming out in October!

We had a really high expectation of this place given the raving reviews and lots of recommendations, especially with the vegan/veg options. We were able to get a seat without booking on a busy weekend which we were grateful. I must start from the service and need to provide the explanation of it first before I go into the food review. We were seated downstairs and there were initially two servers but later became one and sat behind the bar area at the back. The service felt very generic with very little personality and felt as though the person was not very happy or focused. They took the order and we ordered quite a few dishes (which became apparent later on) and there was no indication from the server that we ordered way too much. There was a missing tea which took a quite long time to be rectified. There were a few moments in the service where it was hard to get any attention given they were working facing behind. Later on another table asked for service charge taken out due to lack of service, and they have become quite upset and the rest of the evening felt a little off (and hence atmosphere also felt a little off). The food was great, throughout except for the natural red wine which tasted like a vinegar - really bad option. The sad point is that because of the amount of food we ordered, it became too much to enjoy towards the end and had the server did a better job suggesting the right amount we would have enjoyed the evening more.

I  visited Bubala Soho over a weekend in June, and it was a fantastic dining experience. We chose the restaurant for its strong selection of vegetarian and vegan options, and it definitely delivered.

Although we arrived about 15 minutes before our reservation, we were promptly seated without any issues. The staff were incredibly welcoming and attentive, taking the time to explain the concept and menu, which we really appreciated.

We opted for the vegan set menu, and by the end of the meal, we were more than happy with our choice. Every dish was beautifully presented and full of flavour. Highlights for me were the babaganoush, which was smoky and rich, and the grilled oyster mushrooms, which had an amazing texture and depth of taste.

Overall, a warm and satisfying experience—perfect for anyone looking to enjoy creative, plant-based Middle Eastern dishes in the heart of Soho. Highly recommended!

places.name: Mildreds Soho
places.formatted_address: 45 Lexington St, Carnaby, London W1F 9AN, UK
places.editorial_summary: International-themed vegetarian restaurant which favours organic, seasonal produce and wine.

reviews.text:
We had a truly wonderful experience at Mildreds Soho for my father's 75th birthday dinner. From the moment we arrived, everything was handled with care and warmth. The table was thoughtfully chosen, the food was excellent, and the service throughout was outstanding.
A special mention to Laura, who managed the second floor with calm professionalism and genuine kindness. Her attentiveness made a real difference to our evening.
We were also touched by the thoughtful gestures that made my parents feel celebrated it added a lovely personal touch to the occasion.
Overall, the team created a memorable experience for us, and I’m very grateful for the effort and hospitality shown

I visited Mildreds Soho on a Friday evening – the place was quite busy, but the staff were very attentive and friendly throughout. The restaurant is spread across three floors, with each level split into smaller dining rooms of just a few tables, which gives it a cozy and intimate feel.

The food was tasty and well-prepared, though I found the portions a bit on the small side for the price. It’s a nice spot to hang out with friends and enjoy a relaxed meal, but I wouldn’t say it’s the top vegan food I’ve had in London. Still, worth a visit if you're in the area and looking for a chill vegan-friendly place.

Third time coming here and it never disappoints
My girlfriend is vegetarian and I am not but the menu satisfies us both every time with a huge choice of perfectly cooked food.
The staff are incredibly attentive and the atmosphere is incredibly welcoming with an upbeat relaxing vibe

From the US, was recommended toe by a bartender at St James and it was spot on! Amazing food, even my husband who isn't vegan and generally doesn't like it and wasn't hungry ate a lot of it! Guac, gyoza and kebabs.

We visited for the second time to celebrate our wedding anniversary. Mentioned this on the booking and were greeted with complimentary drink.

We had the set menu for dinner which was just amazing. For a meat eater that is great praise indeed. Food flavours and color amazing.

Will certainly be heading back.

places.name: Tofu Vegan Islington
places.editorial_summary: Unpretentious restaurant fixing up plant-based versions of classic Chinese dishes.

reviews.text: Honestly one of the best vegan restaurants I've ever been. I was there in June this year and I'm still not able to forget this food. The staff was very friendly, everything was clean and pleasant. The dessert was a highlight because I usually don't order them but honestly worth it! This restaurant deserves 5 stars!

We had such a lovely time at Tofu Vegan! The food was brilliant and the service was so friendly and accommodating. Our server Yama was really great, offering us suggestions and overall just really friendly. We had a one year old and everyone made us and him feel really welcomed. Can't wait to come back!

I have been many times now to TV (this branch and some of the others) and it's ALWAYS SUPERB. My non-vegan friends love it too and I always enjoy introducing new people to the magic. My favourite vegan restaurant in London for sure. Love their ethos and above all the super tasty food - so many flavours and different dishes to discover.
I had to leave a review today with a special mention of lovely waitress Yama. She spent lots of time with me and gave generous advice on new dishes for me to try, asking my preferences and taking them properly into consideration, and coming back later to ask what I thought. I could see her going from table to table offering the same thoughtful advice to others. Thanks for your kindness and passion!

Can’t believe one of my favourite Chinese restaurants is vegan!

Fake meat has proven itself already but I had doubt fake fish could do the job. This is the first time I’ve believed fish could be replaced with a vegetarian alternatives.

The fake fish in “Sliced fish in sizzling oil” actually tasted like fish, including texture! Mind blowing.

The fake duck rolls were very impressive as well, and a great alternative to duck rolls for vegans. Just not quite as good as real peking duck rolls, but still the best replacement I’ve seen.

The wonton in house special sauce and green beans were very nice. The sweet-sour ‘chicken’ was good but overshadowed by the rest of the dishes so I likely wont order it again.

Very friendly and attentive staff. I’ll return to this restaurant for sure, and I’ll order the ‘fish’ every time.

The food and service was incredible here! Yama was very attentive, polite and helped us with recommendations for food, and was so wonderful. Definitely coming back here as a place with some of the best vegan food.

places.name: Govinda's Soho Street
places.editorial_summary: Linked to the Radha Krishna Temple, serving vegetarian and vegan Indian thalis, salads and sweets.

reviews.text: What an awesome experience. The food is definitely authentic and delicious. Above all, the staff are genuinely filled with love and greet you so warmly. I travel the globe eating out daily, and this beats any restaurants I've been to in the last 50 years. This is the best gem of London. A big thank you to all the staff showing me that humans are beautiful. Hare Krishna.

I have always thought of Govindas as making and serving good quality, affordable (though not fancy) food with love. This curry was ok, but not the tastiest, and the serving size was small for the price. The service was ok but the staff took their stress out on me when I asked how big the small and large serving sizes were - a very valid question in my opinion. Prices are about the same as other eateries, which have nicer decor and more options. I won’t be coming back unfortunately.

Probably the best and cheapest meal I paid in London since I arrived on Sunday. Located in the heart of Oxford district, right next to Tottenham underground. Very busy and first come first serve, and you will enjoy the food.

Govinda’s has an interesting set-up, reckon, run by devotees with a temple-style, “sewa” vibe. The concept is unique, but the execution leaves a lot to be desired.

Food-wise, it’s fine. Think really simple temple food rather than restaurant-quality Indian cooking. A thali sets you back around £10–15, which is standard London pricing, but what you get is nowhere near the flavour, richness, or polish you’d expect for that price at other Indian/ Gujarati spots. It’s wholesome and filling, but not particularly delicious.

Atmosphere and hospitality are where it really falls short. At this price point, you’d expect more warmth and a bit of care in service. During my visit, I was briefly greeted by Shree, who seemed kind and polite, Thanks Shree. However, most of the staff looked disengaged, just going through the motions and perhaps waiting to clock out. I get that hospitality is a tiring job but here you could see no spark. The server could also be more hygienic; not dirty, but not up to the standard you’d expect in a typical restaurant.

In short: if you’re after a simple, vegan/ vegetarian thali with plenty of variety, Govinda’s will scratch that itch. But don’t expect standout flavours, warm hospitality, or much of a restaurant atmosphere. Management would really benefit from focusing on basic hospitality and creating a more welcoming dining experience. :)

Govinda’s Restaurant in Soho London is truly a hidden gem and one of the most delightful dining experiences we have always had in London. Located just off Oxford Street, it offers a calm, welcoming atmosphere that feels like a retreat from the busy streets outside. The restaurant specializes in wholesome vegetarian and vegan food, and the quality is excellent. The thalis (eg. Govinda / Deluxe / Paneer  etc. at least five different varieties)  are generous, balanced, and full of authentic flavors, while the curries are rich yet light, without being overly oily or heavy. The variety of dishes ensures there is something for everyone, whether you are a long-time vegetarian or just curious to try something different.
What really stands out is the freshness of the food—every dish tastes home-cooked, nourishing, and comforting. The staff  in general are warm, polite, and efficient, creating a friendly environment that makes you feel at ease. Prices are very reasonable for central London, and the portion sizes are excellent, offering fantastic value for money. The casual, canteen-style service also adds to its charm, making it an easy and relaxing place to enjoy a meal. On the flip slide, the lady at the counter could have been more smiling and generous. We ran a bill of almost GBP 19 and she refused to accept a legal tender of GBP 50.  Hmm!

places.name: Unity Diner
places.editorial_summary: Cheery, modern restaurant offering plant-based fare & a non-profit diner & bar ethos.

reviews.text:
I visited Unity Diner for their Sunday Carvery buffet, which is available only on Sundays. For £22 + service charge, you can choose 1–2 mock meats (served only once) and then help yourself to unlimited vegetables and sauces.

The restaurant ambiance is really nice and welcoming, and the staff were very kind. The food tasted alright overall — I felt the mock meats and side vegetables could use a bit more flavour, but it was still a good experience and filling.

I also really appreciate what they stand for and the work they’re doing to promote plant-based dining. Worth checking out if you’re looking for a vegan Sunday roast in London.

Everyone in my family enjoyed the meals.  We were surprised how similar the steak and salmon looked like the real thing.  Flavors were great.  The desserts were excellent too.  Would love to go here again the next time we're in London.

I'm atheist but...OMG!! The Diner served up truly great food..... Oh my! Absolutely delicious. I got home and I was a happy bunny. I was so happy I got distracted by the flavors I forgot the names of the dishes ate. Why on earth would you want to eat animal based version of these beats me. But please admire what I and my mother demolished right down to the crumbs I.e photos. And to add they aloud my very handsome 2 large doggies to join us fantastico. In the words of The Terminator "I'll be back"

Delicious! We went for the Sunday vegan roast and then went back in the week for the regular menu.

Food is very tasty, creative, and nicely presented. My only feedback would be to add some salad or chips to the burger so it looks better value for money.

The tofish and calamari were our favourites. And we really loved the sticky toffee pudding. Yum!

Overall, it’s on the expensive side for what you get. The Mac & Cheese tasted mostly of flour with a bit of salt, though the vegan fish and chips were better. It’s an option if you specifically want vegan alternatives, but the taste was often far off from what you’d expect if you’re used to the meat or cheese versions (we all tried different dishes and felt the same).

Drinks and food are quite pricey considering the portion sizes and taste. On the positive side, the food arrived on time, and everything came out together even though we were a larger group, staff was friendly and welcoming.

Not really a fan, to be honest. It works if you need a vegan option, but I wouldn’t rush back.

Lets start with the food.....thats the important bit.
Between us we ordered nearly all the menu, there was not one dish that disappointed on flavour, texture and presentation.
Each dish had a personality, it fought for its place as a favourite dish!
Stylish restaurant with a lovely look and feel with a good wine and cocktail selection.
Busy with a real buzz from Portobello Market just outside.
Vegan or not, this is a place to eat great food and enjoy flavour!

Incredible vegan food. Every course was delicious. The staff was friendly, warm and helpful. The only issue was the speed. We ordered the chef selection, 8 dishes over 4 courses. The first two came basically at the same time and the rest quickly after. For this price I expected a slow food experience. Too bad because everything else was amazing.

My wife and I had an early dinner here on a Wednesday evening and had a really great experience. Shout out to Gabriel for the engaging and enjoyable service he provided, as that really took it from a very good time to an exceptional one.

Food was ordered after taking our server's recommendations into account, which we highly recommend doing. When we went, we especially loved dishes featuring beetroot & blueberries with pine nuts, roasted leeks with almond romesco, and a cassoulet with cep & smoked tofu, and a dessert featuring an orange & bergamot pudding (pictures included). If still available on the menu, also recommend trying the low-ABV drinks from AMA brewery.

The atmosphere is inviting and lively without being loud. Highly suggest to anyone who has a chance to go!

First I would like to say that the staff was really helpful and kind at all times and most probably their chefs too.

With that said I would like to say that I feel their menu is overpriced and their dishes are dull and without taste.

All dishes that we had were oily and salty, from the bread to the white bean paste to every bite.

As well I understand they want to “grill” the bread but they burnt it and that’s not a good thing.

I tried their pecan tiramisu and it was just like nothing, I left almost half of it because there was no flavour.

There are many things wrong with their menu and I think they should really take a look at it and improve.

It’s not about how many oils you infuse, how many oils you use or the amount of salt or sugar has in it, it should be the simplicity of the flavours and as their name says Holy Carrot, just bring the basic flavours with a twist.

Lunch might be expensive anyways it should be tasty and feel the love with every bite.

As well the restaurant is really tight and they have given priority to their bar, which by the way they had a really nice Spanish speaking person who was really helpful and with a smile at all times.

The entrance is so tight you can’t move and everyone working there or guests have to juggle their way through it.

In my opinion they should rethink the layout to improve service and make it less hectic.

I hope with this review they improve and one day come back to see them do better.

I give it 2 stars because of the service they provided.

Had a great vegan dinner here - great variety of healthy veggies and hearty dishes. Also, the server told us everything on the menu has some level of fermentation, so we felt great afterward. Delightful cocktails and great selection of wine, including natural wine.

places.name: KIN Cafe & Restaurant
places.editorial_summary: Quaint eatery specialising in vegan breakfast staples, sandwiches & sweets, plus coffee & smoothies.

reviews.text:
This food was absolutely delicious. The dishes were some of the best vegetable focused (rather than imitation meat) dishes I’ve had and is probably one of my favourite vegan restaurants I’ve been to in London.

The staff were incredibly friendly and the interior was nice. Their chai latte was also great which is hard to find in London.

Would highly recommend.

I must admit that when I saw how quiet KIN was compared to the other restaurants nearby, I regretted my reservation. However I definitely should not have. My starter (house style aubergine) was one of the best things I’ve ever eaten at a restaurant, and the others in my group also thoroughly enjoyed theirs (croquettes and corn soup). The service was extremely understanding and helpful when I told them about my nut allergy and brought me a different menu. For my main I chose the truffle rosso pasta due to my allergy. The sauce was quite nice - my complaint would be that the pasta was slightly too soft and was falling apart which was likely due to its being gluten free so I understand that was probably unavoidable. The portions were huge so unfortunately I had no space for dessert, but my companions said the black forest tart was fantastic. Highly recommend KIN; favourite dishes were the aubergine and corn soup small plates.

Food was intentionally cooked delicious and not greasy at ALL! I had the KIN Brunch special (make it vegan) and it was DIVINE!
Excellently decorated but the Café is quite cramped.

Popped in for brunch and already cannot wait for my next visit. The tofu was delicious, and the breakfast burrito was delicious - we were able to swap it to vegetarian rather than vegan. Coffees were good and the service was lovely! Would also love to try their restaurant next door.

An Absolute Gem: Ken Cafe & Restaurant!
We recently had the pleasure of dining at Ken Cafe and Restaurant, and it was a truly fantastic experience from start to finish. This place is an absolute gem, and it's easy to see why it has such a loyal following.
From the moment we walked in, we were greeted with a warm and welcoming atmosphere. The staff were incredibly friendly, attentive, and genuinely enthusiastic, making us feel right at home. The decor is charming and cozy, creating the perfect setting for a relaxed and enjoyable meal.
But the real star of the show is, of course, the food. The menu offers a wonderful variety, with something to satisfy every craving. We were particularly impressed with the fresh ingredients and the obvious care that goes into every dish. Each plate was a work of art, beautifully presented and bursting with flavor. The portion sizes were generous, and the quality was top-notch—a perfect combination of comfort food and culinary excellence.
Whether you're looking for a quick coffee and a delicious pastry, a hearty lunch, or a celebratory dinner, Ken Cafe delivers on all fronts. We left feeling completely satisfied and already talking about our next visit. If you're in the area and looking for a fantastic meal with great service and a lovely ambiance, do yourself a favor and visit Ken Cafe. You won't be disappointed!

places.name: Meat The Vegans - Multicuisine
places.formatted_address: Unit 729, Meat the Vegans, Camden Stables Market, 731 Camden Lock Pl, Chalk Farm Rd, Chalk Farm, London NW1 8AH, UK
places.vicinity: Unit 729, Meat the Vegans, Camden Stables Market, 731 Camden Lock Pl, Chalk Farm Rd, London

reviews.text:
If you're anywhere near this restaurant, you really must try it. It's in a great, easy to find location in Camden Market and offers both inside and outside seating. It has a menu to suit all tastes and although everything is vegan, (thank you) the food is so tasty, any non vegan could have a really good meal here without any concerns over lack of choice. The service is excellent, the staff are friendly, helpful and knowledgeable about all of the dishes. I had the Jamaican jerk chik'n which was exactly the right level of spicy and came with rice and peas, while my husband had a burrito with peri peri chips.
It was great value for money as the food is excellent and really good sized portions. My only complaint, I don't live closer!

Such a great place that caters for vegans and everyone else with a range of multicultural food. Fantastic tasting and value vegan food in the heart of Camden Market area. I'm not sure how the chefs do it, but they work magic into their food. We've tried most of the menu and always loved everything, but the wings are a real wow! If you can tolerate heat go for the Siracha and you won't be disappointed. Also love the jewelled rice, the butter chick*n, and the pad Thai. Milkshakes are good too.

This place was delicious! I ordered the vegan curry goat and it was so good. The waitress helped me decide what to get when I couldn’t choose between two options. As someone who has eaten a lot of vegetarian and vegan food, I really really enjoyed this dish. It was so flavorful and so filling. All pieces of the dish were tasty, from the rice and beans, the goat curry, the green beans, and the plantains. The plantains even had a nice little crisp to them on the edges! I would definitely come back here the next time I’m in Camden Town. Outside seating is great as well. Perfect for people watching, which I enjoy as well. Highly recommend!

It's always good to see a fully vegan restaurant with plenty of options. I got a pad thai, which was nice enough, but a bit greasy, and my hubby got the hotdog, which had way too much sauce on it and a hard bun, which had clearly been microwaved, it was hard as a rock at the ends.

Although the restaurant wasn't very busy, the service was minimal, we weren't checked during our meal, and the drinks came after the food - definitely would not have left a 12.5% tip if I had been asked.

When I went to pay, the card machine gave service charge options, and the server quickly clicked 12.5% (so quickly I didnt even see, and I was paying). My husband told me after we left, so I didn't go back. This really shouldn't happen in the UK, where tipping is completely optional, especially when the service wasn't even friendly. That left a bad impression overall as it was very dishonest.

A great 100% vegan restaurant with different styles of food: Indian, Mexican, American and Asian. Colorful, beautiful meals with different kinds of protein, full of vegetables!
Tasty and amazing!

The best Thai food experience ever.

I have been to many Thai restaurants everywhere in the world (including in Thailand) but none of them came even closer to this one.

Each plate is infused with so much flavors and taste; fresh ingredients from Thailand; using natural and wholesome foods; they are crafted with much attention, detail, care, love… Every bite was a trip back to Thailand! It was so good to be able to enjoy healthy Thai food without worrying about the use of msg/ chemical additives used in other places.

The owners are so welcoming and kind; I was in London for three days and kept going back for every dinner. I highly recommend the wing bean salad and the banana curry; it was so delicious!!

So looking forward to coming back again on my next trip. Kapunka!!

A cosy vegan Thai restaurant closed to London Bridge, offering noodles, curries and stir fry dishes. We tried the beetroot broth noodles and the konjac noodle tofu and broccoli scrambled. Both dishes were cooked well and full of flavour, especially the broth. Service was friendly and welcoming. Overall a great lunch experience.

Incredible vegan food. One of the dishes I’ve missed the most since going vegan 10+ years ago is the Hainanese Chicken Rice. I had accepted that I would never be able to eat it again. So you have made me very happy. Very kind staff as well! Highly recommended.

I really enjoyed the food here! Even though I didn’t have a reservation, they kindly found a table for us. Considering it’s in central London, that was a pleasant surprise.

The food combinations are unique and intriguing, with rich blends of spices and condiments that make the aroma alone worth the visit - truly mouthwatering.

The staff are incredibly kind and attentive, always ready to help as soon as you need them. Overall, a fantastic experience!

Next time I’m in London, I’ll definitely be coming back! 🌱💛

Love this fantastic restaurant with such great food. Everything is delicious. I had the jasmine ginger beer which was not too sweet and perfect for hot weather! We tried the coconut Thai rice chips which was super tasty. My main was vegan Plant you cashew nut Chick'n with Jasmine rice. ....so good I loved it. My friend had Yen Ta fo street noodles which she loved.  Staff were friendly and ambience is welcoming here.

📍 Cream Dream, Ukrainian Women-Run Café & Vegan Delights 💕🩷

Cream Dream is an absolute gem and a must-visit for anyone who loves vegan, gluten-free, and wholesome café food. This incredible Ukrainian women-led business is not only inspiring in their mission to support Ukraine, they sell bracelets to raise funds and even collect vape batteries to send back home, but also in the way they serve delicious, thoughtful food that delights every sense.

The açai bowl was a burst of fresh, vibrant fruit, perfectly paired with rich, crunchy chocolate granola 🍌🫐. The avocado toast with smoked salmon was an explosion of flavour, creamy, savoury, and unforgettable 🥑. Every dish we tried was 100% vegan and gluten-free, making this café ideal for anyone with dietary preferences or just looking for healthy, tasty café options.

We couldn’t resist the sweet treats either. The Yana Coffee Caramel melted in my mouth, it’s officially my favourite! Amy and Hannah loved the Not Ur Oxy Honey Honey Cherry. For drinks, I had the pink matcha, which was light, fruity, and perfectly refreshing after a long walk. Hannah’s almond milk flat white was equally enjoyed, smooth, rich, and expertly made.

Beyond the incredible vegan and gluten-free menu, Cream Dream shines because of the passion, dedication, and positivity of the women running it. Supporting this café means enjoying flavourful, Instagram-worthy dishes while contributing to an impactful, socially conscious business.

If you’re looking for healthy brunch spots, vegan cafés, gluten-free treats, or simply a feel-good place to enjoy amazing food and drinks, Cream Dream should be at the top of your list. We are so grateful to experience this unique café and support such an empowering women-led business.

Literally my favourite place in London. As a gluten free vegan, getting to have their beautiful sweet treats (AMAZING pastries) makes my
whole life. Also as a gluten free vegan polish girl, getting to have their varenyky’s reminds me so much of my perogies from my grandma ❤️ The cafe itself is beautiful and all the girlies running it are so amazing. Amazing food supporting ukrainian refugees 🇺🇦

The menu is rather interesting, there are lunch options with some Ukrainian dishes, but you can only find the full menu via QR code. The desserts are amazing, but pricey.
Having gluten and sugar free options is very important for me.
Why I didn't give it 5 stars? The service was  slow,  so there was quite a queue. We wanted to order more, but didn't have much time to wait, so we had to get our desserts elsewhere.

Absolutely fantastic food and smooth coffee.

The cakes are delicious and not too sweet, which is a boon as they are huge! The USB-C ports on the table lamps is a useful touch.

Cream Dream is an absolute gem!
From the moment I walked in, I felt like I had stepped into a little slice of heaven. The atmosphere is warm and welcoming, but what truly sets this place apart is the incredible kindness of the staff. Every single person I interacted with was genuinely friendly, attentive, and passionate about what they do. It’s rare to feel so cared for in a café setting, but Cream Dream nails it.
Now let’s talk about the food and drinks — wow. Every bite and sip is a celebration of flavor. As a fully vegan café, Cream Dream doesn’t just meet expectations, it shatters them. The dishes are beautifully presented, thoughtfully crafted, and bursting with taste. Whether you're plant-based or not, you’ll be blown away by how flavorful and satisfying everything is. Their drinks? Absolute perfection. From creamy lattes to refreshing smoothies, each one is a masterpiece.
You can feel the love and creativity in every detail — from the food, to the service, to the cozy, aesthetic interior. Cream Dream is more than just a café, it’s an experience, and one I will keep coming back to again and again.
Highly, highly recommend. ♥️

places.name: Love Shack
places.formatted_address: Arch 298, 299 Cambridge Heath Rd, Cambridge Heath, London E2 9HA, UK
places.editorial_summary: Cozy, colorful fixture with outdoor seats offering inventive vegan dishes, plus music & events.

reviews.text: Flat white for £4 at love shack. I really loved the service they were very nice and chatty and really brightened my day within the five minute interaction they were so sweet !! The flat white was not bitter at all and steamed to perfection with a great micro foam but still smooth and the right temperature. I wouldn’t definitely recommend and love the atmosphere there too !!

Such a lovely vegan spot! The atmosphere is cozy and inviting, with colorful décor. The staff were so friendly and accommodating — they made me feel right at home. The food tasted amazing, full of flavor and cooked to perfection. Everyone was so thoughtful and well-mannered, and they even sang happy birthday to a near-by table... hands down, as a customer, you’re treated like family, and the vibe just makes you want to kick back and relax. The shack has it all. look no further — eat here, this is the spot!

My husband and I ate here a couple of times whilst we were staying in the area. As a vegan, I am always on the lookout for places to eat and the menu looked intriguing! The first time I had the tofu karaage and miso eggplant while my husband had the vegan  cheeseburger and chips. All the meals were absolutely delicious which is why we decided to return on our last night in London. This time my omnivore brother came with us and he ordered the cheeseburger and loved it. I ordered the tofu karaage again as it was so good, plus the vegan peking duck (no sin peking duck), which was also delicious. I love how all the dishes come with something pickled. They also have a range of pickled cocktails, which look amazing. I really wanted to try one of the desserts, but was too full! The caramel pavlova looked especially yummy.
As well as the food, the service is amazing. All the employees are super friendly and helpful and really make the place a joy to dine at. We all also loved the music selection, ranging from blues to 60s, 70s, 80s rock.
I would definitely eat here again and recommend to anyone wanting a delicious meal in a great atmosphere.

Cannot even describe how good this place was. Instantly welcomed in by the staff and the owner. We ordered the most incredible vegan chicken burger with buffalo sauce, and beyond meat burger and were stuffed. So chill, friendly and has such a community feel about it. Would come back in a flash.

I would give more points for the ambience in this restaurant, if I could. Felt like a mellow dream, in the coziest corner of Nightcity. And that's not the mushrooms talking. The venue is just superb, the food was great (the ramen were spicy enough to be called spicy - loved it). And there's a secret hidden here. :D

This was one of the best plant-based meals I have had! The food was full of flavor with plenty of variety. I especially enjoyed the croquettes and the navratan korma. Varsha was fantastic, recommending lovely dishes and a perfect wine pairing. For dessert, the pistachio tres leches was a real treat and definitely worth trying. Highly recommended!

We went to Mallow for breakfast and had a mixed experience. The interior of the restaurant is amazing, the colour and their detailed decorations are very contemporary. Service was not ready yet even though the restaurant had opened well before we arrived. We waited a while to be seated, and food came only after a wait of about 40 minutes. As a courtesy, our coffee/tea were on the restaurant, which we appreciated very much. However, there was also a corporate meeting on the upper floor, holding a presentation and showing a corporate video we could all, unfortunately, participate in on the lower floor as well. Food was good.

For a vegan meal this is one of the best I have ever eaten. Even for a non vegan/ vegetarian you will not miss the meat. The flavours of the food are outstanding. The staff are attentive and friendly - and if you ask will make perfect recommendations for your meal. The fixed menu will not let you down. Be adventurous and treat your self to ans experience. Definitely worth giving it a shot. You will not regret it.

Mallow in Canary Wharf is a beautiful spot, stylish, modern, and full of charm. The service was great and the atmosphere really lovely. We probably didn’t order the best dishes this time, as the flavors didn’t quite wow us. I’ve been to their Borough Market location before and honestly found the food there a bit more impressive. Still, it’s a wonderful place with a creative, fully plant based menu and definitely worth visiting. I’d love to come back and try other dishes, I feel like there’s more to discover here

The food is delicious. My oyster mushroom and hispi skewer was tender and juicy. The port gravy that came with it added some stronger taste on top of the light oil and garlic that it came with, which gives options to whoever is eating it.
The cocktails are sweet and juicy, the apricot negroni barely tasted of alcohol.
Our server, Divyang, was very attentive and professional. Divyang is knowledgeable about the menu and patient when waiting for us to decide.

However, I do wish that they would not perfume the area near the door. Although it smells good, it interferes with your taste buds when you are about to eat.

I'm not vegan and this is probably the only vegan place I've encountered so far that I would frequent more often. Top quality and preparation of meals! Had them pack one of the pancakes because I couldn't finish it, and it was like fresh even 5 hours later! Staff is great, friendly, and attentive. While I'm not a fan of adding tip automatically to the bill (really the only downside of this place), I was ok with paying it since they clearly deserved it. ⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐

In a cozy spot, where flavors entwine, 🌱✨
A vegetarian haven, simply divine. 🌍🥗
Not just for veggies, but all will adore, 🍽️❤️
Dishes that dance, leaving you wanting more. 🎉

With hints of India and Korean delight, 🇮🇳🇰🇷
Middle Eastern spices that take flight. 🌶️🍛
Beautifully plated, a feast for the eyes, 👀🍽️
Each bite a treasure, a flavorful surprise. 🎊

On a quiet street, where peace does reside, 🌳🕊️
Just a short stroll from Kings Cross Station, your guide. 🚶‍♂️📍
The decor whispers comfort, inviting and warm, 🕯️🪴
A perfect retreat, away from the storm. ☁️

The staff are attentive, so kind and sincere, 🤗💬
Encouraging takeaways, spreading the cheer. 🎁✨
AJ’s wise tip, a suggestion to share:
“Highlight your bestsellers!”—a thoughtful affair. 🌟💡

I booked a table yesterday before heading back to France, and it was one of the best meals I've ever had at a restaurant.
I highly recommend trying the pistachio cheesecake!
As a vegetarian, I was glad I could enjoy everything on the menu, and the staff was friendly and helpful.

I will definitely be returning the next time I'm in London.

The staff were incredibly helpful and genuinely lovely, such a warm welcome. Honestly, the food was one of the best meals I’ve ever had. The Caesar salad was fresh and full of flavor, and the white chocolate tiramisu was absolutely divine! I’m already looking forward to coming back to London and working my way through the rest of the menu.

I really enjoyed stopping in for a quick and delicious lunch at Mildred’s! The artichoke caesar salad with plant-based chick’n was fantastic. The dressing is especially tasty. Service was professional and friendly and my food arrived quickly. I look forward to coming back!

We found this restaurant on the Happy Cow app. The food was so fresh and delicious, we all enjoyed our meals. I would like to come back again if l had time while staying in London. The taxi driver told me the burgers are great here, glad l listened to him and tried it!

Incredible food, amazing atmosphere on the second floor, and amazing food as well! Highly recommend if you are vegan and want some delicious food!

The staff are also very friendly and polite!

We visited last month and I just remembered I forgot to post this review but: Great staff, great variety of vegan food options (all VG menu) and dog friendly! Need I say more?

I never got the name of the man who greeted us but this place is a hidden gem. We walked in (as a vegan and a vegetarian) to ask if they were dog friendly and before we could ask he was obsessed with our dog and said hi to her. He brought her a bowl as well! Good vegan food can be hard to find now as it’s all the same options everywhere. But this place really hit the spot. We shared a couple dishes and it was delicious. Loved the vibe of the place and the staff checked in lots even though we ordered on the QR code which was so nice.
Honestly would go back for the lovely man who greeted us as his energy was 10000/10.

Found this restaurant shortly after visiting Madame Tussaud’s. Always nice to visit a vegan/vegetarian restaurant as it’s rare we can order anything on the menu!

Food was good, very tasty. I liked that you could order via the web (or at desk if you prefer). Wasn’t too busy, there were plenty of tables, and very comfy. Bathroom facilities were very clean and tidy.

Would visit again if I was in the area.
One of the best vegan breakfasts I've had in London. I really liked it, everything was spot on and just goes to show that vegan food can be every bit as good as the traditional stuff.

places.name: Mildreds Camden
places.vicinity: The Glass Bldg, 9 Jamestown Rd, London

reviews.text:
Mildreds Camden is an absolute must-visit for any foodie, vegan or not. The menu is a vibrant and imaginative celebration of plant-based cuisine, proving that vegan food can be full of depth and excitement. It’s no wonder we found ourselves returning for a second day in a row.

Each dish was a journey, and together they made for a dining experience that is, without a doubt, among the top vegan restaurants globally.

Camden branch—first time there and was…
Camden branch—first time there and was really looking forward to the whole experience of a vegan restaurant. My partner wanted to treat me to a meal.

The starter was disappointing: corn ribs that were basically just slices of corn on the cob dumped in a bland sauce. Quite poor. My partner had the dumplings, which were nice—I wish I’d ordered those instead.

The main was better: a Korean chick+n burger that tasted surprisingly like real chicken. The fries were nothing special. My partner had the curry, which was okay but not earth-shattering.

For dessert, my partner had the cheesecake, which was nothing to shout about. At that point, I didn’t want anything else.

But what really ruined the experience was the service—it was awful, to the point of being non-existent.

Most customers had to get up to ask for the bill or order extra drinks during their meal. It took ages for plates to be cleared between courses or for drinks to arrive.

They weren’t short-staffed, but the team—including the manager—seemed completely oblivious to the fact they had customers. They stood around chatting and walked past people clearly trying to get their attention to order, get drinks, or pay.

If this is how the chain is run, then this particular branch is definitely the weak link.

I even them leave a take on the counter getting for 10minutes before the courier turned to take it. So you know that gonna cold.

I cannot see me and my partner returning.

And it was overpriced.
Date of experience: 10 August 2025

Absolutely delicious food, one of the best roasts I've had in a while. The cocktail menu is creative and the chamomile peach old fashioned was delicious, refreshing and not too sweet. Staff were really friendly and attentive and the atmosphere was very chilled (aside from one screaming child but that's not the restaurants fault). The restaurant itself is clean and open and very easy to locate. Id definitely recommend and can't wait to visit again!

I loved it. It was honestly one of the best vegan pancakes I've ever had. And I enjoyed it every last bite.

We were served by a very kind and patient girl, super sweet and friendly. The experience was absolutely incredible. I will return to try the different dishes they offer.

Food was good but not the best vegan I have had, some of the dishes needed a bit of flavor. We took the menu to taste the dishes, the portions were good, but we were only impressed by the romesco. It was good but not outstanding. The tiramisu had no coffee, the sponge cake was supposed to be wet with coffee but it was dry. It was basically just sponge cake with cream.

The food was honestly amazing! I have a lot of fish allergies, so coming here and being able to try it and (being told by the people I was with) it tastes exactly the same was just a nice experience. The menu is very large and a great deal of things to try and honestly I want to come back and try it all.
The staff are so sweet too. They really helped with what to order and are very honest (as we all have different taste palates and wanted to make sure we get what we’d like). Very happy and smiley. Overall just a great restaurant and will DEFINITELY be returning to try more foods!

Thank you so much.

Visited this restaurant before attending a gig at the nearby Black Heart. I had booked but it was quiet enough so that I could’ve just walked in. The food I ordered was very good quality and reasonably priced for London. I was alone on this occasion but would like to return in a group as the menu lends itself toward ordering a number of dishes
Exceptional all-vegan Chinese spot! Bold flavours, attentive staff, and lightning-fast service. The vegan fried fish and mapo tofu were standouts — so good we came back the next day. A must-try!

AMAZING Vegan food. Every dish had the perfect punch of ingredients. We ordered chili oil in addition to the already spicy dishes that was so delicious!

I’m definitely 100% coming back. So worth it!

This restaurant is utterly unbelievable. The food we ordered was quick, beautiful and delicious. The plant based chicken, beef, and prawns were absolutely fabulous. The iced red tea was delightful. The prices are quite expensive, but we believe its quality/price comparison is understandable and definitely deserved. The only downside to me personally is the dessert: I have had better vegan cheesecakes, and the one the restaurant served us is acceptable, but not a high standard like the previous food we received. Besides this, the restaurant is 5 stars anyway for the service, the food and the atmosphere. Will definitely come back again! Our compliments to the team and the chefs!

places.name: The Ledbury
places.editorial_summary: Chef Brett Graham's innovative cooking, paired with fine wines in a smart, modern setting.

reviews.text: One of the best dinners I’ve ever have. Amazing service with a perfect balance between fancy and relaxed and friendly. The wine paring was amazing, some great labels paring perfectly with the food. And. The food was amazing, technically perfect, great flavours and a lot of truffle. I. My opinion a perfect place for a celebration or an important event.

Amongst fine dining restaurant it is a very decent one.

That said I have to admit that service was subpar. We came first to restaurant, but we were not serviced in order. Also chef picked their favourite table to serve and chit chat, but that wasn't a privilege bestowed upon every guest.

lovely restaurant in a very nice area. i went there for my birthday. we felt welcomed from the beginning. super friendly staff with a lot knowledge. food was amazing. plating on point and super interesting flavors and techniques. i loves that they have their own farms with animals and are very close to their suppliers. i could taste the amazing quality. my wife has a bell pepper intolerance and she got a great substitute dish. the owner is super friendly and comes to the table to present some dishes. great guy. hopefully i will manage to come back one day.. i would totally recommend this restaurant and wish all the staff all the best.

This place had been on my list for a while and it mostly lived up to expectations. We came for Friday night dinner and enjoyed the relaxed and inviting atmosphere which struck a perfect balance without feeling too formal. The food was largely excellent, though the dessert unfortunately wasn't to my taste which was a shame. My favourites from the tasting menu were the tuna, scallop, duck and the pre dessert. The service was polished, friendly and helpful.

the best service of all the Michelin restaurants we have ever been to. Very friendly and positive staff. Excellent wine list. The food is generally really tasty and creative. It a couple of portions, in my opinion, the perfect combination of flavors was sacrificed to showiness and populism (like the dish with black caviar, which completely negated the flavor range of the other, really interesting ingredients.
Overall a really cool restaurant with a good atmosphere, service, thoughtful details of dishes and interior and decent food.

places.name: Ekstedt at The Yard
places.formatted_address: 3-5 Great Scotland Yard, London SW1A 2HN, UK

reviews.text:
It would be a shame to give this place just 4 stars — I’m not even talking about 3 or 2.

Absolutely everything was perfect, from the service to the food, and how we were treated.

They even invited us into the kitchen, which was a very special experience. Each dish was better than the one before — truly impressive.

I always choose restaurants very carefully, and I can proudly say that this one is going straight to the top of my list.

The atmosphere was also really pleasant.
Definitely coming back.

Amazing experience in this unique restaurant.

We tried the Scandinavian journey experience+ the volcanic wines pairing.

We particularly loved the lobster and the fir potatoes dishes. Insanely delicious sauce and smokey flavours.

The step that involved seeing the oyster being cooked in the kitchen was particularly fun and unexpected.

The wine pairings were in general very good. We normally don't like white wines that much but these ones particularly well chosen and not too acidic / sour for our taste.

The only thing we found a bit off was how long it took us to be served from the moment we arrived (about half an hour).

Overall the dinner was fantastic, bold flavours, lots of theatrics and creative food combinations. It was lovely to celebrate my birthday here.

Thanks

Embark on a culinary voyage to Scandinavia at Ekstedt at The Yard, a London masterpiece from the visionary Michelin-starred chef, Niklas Ekstedt. Nestled within the grandeur of the Great Scotland Yard Hotel, this restaurant redefines luxury dining with its masterful approach to wood-fired cooking. The ultimate indulgence awaits with the “Journey to Scandinavia,” a seven-course tasting menu paired with an exclusive volcanic wine selection. Så kul att vara tillbaka på denna ikoniska nordiska restaurang 🇸🇪

Amazing dinner experience. Located in the Scotland Yard hotel. The food is really fabulous and the wine pairing was fantastic. Wine I didn't like by itself but with the food was fabulous. So cool how it actually changes with the food.

Journey to Scandinavia with the volcanic wine tasting.
Felt really welcomed here, they took good care of me both in entertaining and food wise, food was extraordinary and will definitely try to get there again. pictures speak for themselves.

places.name: Dinner by Heston Blumenthal
places.editorial_summary: Elegant, contemporary dining room in opulent hotel, for a menu inspired by British culinary history.

reviews.text:
⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️

Dinner by Heston Blumenthal is more than a meal — it’s a journey through history on a plate. Each dish is inspired by centuries-old recipes, reimagined with modern flair. The Plum Meat Fruit (a playful twist on chicken liver parfait disguised as a plum) was the star — surprising, rich, and delightful. The Seabass with Green Sauce was roasted to tender perfection, the seabass paired beautifully with a herbaceous green sauce made of parsley, basil, garlic, and lemon. Bright, zesty, and refreshing — my best main course of the night., while the Hereford Beef with mushroom ketchup showcased perfect cooking and deep umami, paired with unforgettable triple-cooked fries.

Don’t miss the legendary Tipsy Cake (1858, J.H. Walsh): The restaurant’s other viral and absolutely unmissable dish! A freshly rolled brioche baked for an hour, soaked every 15–20 minutes with vanilla, dessert wine, and brandy until it jiggles when it comes out of the oven. Served with pineapple roasted for 4–5 hours and glazed in apple caramel — smoky, caramelized, and delicious. I expected stronger alcohol notes, but it was more subtle — still a showstopper dessert that everyone seemed to order!

Complimentary Christmas Minced Chocolate Pies: A festive surprise! Instead of meat, finely chopped chocolate mimicked minced filling — sweet, rich, and perfectly seasonal.

Service was attentive and knowledgeable, with staff explaining the history behind each dish in a warm, approachable way. The ambience is elegant yet comfortable, making the whole experience feel like both a dinner and a journey through time.

Dinner by Heston isn’t just a restaurant, it’s a historical adventure brought to life on the plate. A must-visit in London for an extraordinary dining experience! A memorable birthday dinner for my mom!

We came here expecting a world-class dining experience from given the 2-star Michelin restaurant, and instead left wondering how on earth this establishment still holds even one star.

First, the food: it was good, but far from spectacular. Certainly not the kind of culinary artistry you’d expect at this level. Honestly, the flavors merited a Bib Gourmand at best, not a coveted Michelin star.

But the real downfall of the evening was the service, which was appalling from start to finish. The restaurant itself feels like it’s tucked into a strip mall—hardly the atmosphere you’d expect for such a highly touted establishment. We were celebrating a birthday, which we noted both when booking and upon arrival. We were assured they would do something special. After over two hours of dining, the check came, and nothing had been done nor was the birthday even acknowledge by the service staff. Only when we mentioned it again did the staff scramble to throw something together—by which point we were ready to leave. That lack of care and detail is inexcusable and genuinely upsetting.

The sommelier was equally disappointing, offering little guidance and the wines were quite overpriced. Worse, the pours were essentially half pours if that—utterly unacceptable at this level of dining and price point. The manager later addressed this when it was brought to her attention and comped the wine, which was appreciated, but by then the damage had been done.

As for the rest of the service, it was shockingly poor for a Michelin-starred restaurant. Servers were dismissive, inattentive, and completely devoid of the polish expected at this level. The only thing they had going for them were they were dressed well. At a true 2 Michelin Star establishment, you expect staff to anticipate needs, escort you when leaving the table, and discreetly refolding napkins. None of this happened. Instead, when we politely asked our server how she was doing at the beginning of the meal, she replied, “Well, I’m working on a Sunday so not great.” That’s a response better suited to a casual diner, not a restaurant that claims two Michelin stars.

We’ve dined at multiple 1, 2, and 3-star restaurants, and this was by far the worst. It’s shocking and frankly appalling that Michelin continues to recognize this restaurant at such a high level.

The manager’s apologies aside, the evening was ruined. What should have been a memorable birthday dinner to cap off a great trip to London turned into an exercise in disappointment. We will not be returning nor going to any of Heston Blumenthal’s restaurants in the future.

In short: the food was fine, the service was unforgivable, and the entire experience left us questioning how this establishment could be considered fine dining. A true disappointment in every sense.

Our experience at Dinner by Heston Blumenthal was nothing short of excellent. We went for the tasting menu during dinner service and could scarcely have asked for anything better.
The dining room was stylish without being stuffy and had a great ambience. One of the very few less-than-stellar aspects was the bathroom location. With the restaurant being in Mandarin Oriental Hotel, the bathroom was quite a walk so much so that staff had to lead you to it the first time. Other than that however, the location and style were excellent.
The food, as to be expected from a 2 Michelin Star restaurant by Heston Blumenthal no less, was exceptional. Everything from the first bites to the last surprise(s) was fantastic. The standouts in my view were the lobster, chicken liver pate, and beef. But then again it seems maybe unfair to choose a favorite. Towards the end of the meal there was a long break where we thought we were waiting for the bill, but instead a cart was brought out to make liquid nitrogen ice cream (yeah, I know). It made for a delightful semi-end to a wonderful meal.
Lastly, the little bits of history and historical inspiration truly make this restaurant unique among others.
Final verdict: treat yourself; you won’t forget nor regret it.

We love delicious food and high customer service standards, and Heston Blumenthal’s restaurant exceeded all expectations.

The superb team (Andrew, Alberto, Maria and one other whose name I don’t know) worked together seamlessly, making our dining experience highly memorable. The presentation of the food was amazing, and the knowledge of all the staff involved was very interesting, making us feel very looked after.

The entire meal was out of this world. We enjoyed lunch for our double celebration: my special birthday and my son’s master’s degree graduation. Every detail was perfectly executed, and the attention to detail was truly impressive.

The food was absolutely delicious, and the ambience was lovely and relaxed. We highly recommend this restaurant.

We VERY highly recommend you book to enjoy this for yourself. Easily the BEST restaurant we’ve ever been to in the UK
Thank you

Big space, cool vibe, and you can even peek right into the open kitchen. They’ve got this fun card system so you decide if you want the dish explained, the history, or nothing at all—love that touch. Food-wise, Tipsy Cake and the rib were spot on, but the Meat Fruit… wow. Clever, fun, and insanely tasty. Totally worth trying!

places.name: Restaurant St. Barts
places.vicinity: Queen Elizabeth II Wing, 63 Bartholomew Cl, London

reviews.text: Simply wonderful restaurant and evening. We went as a very special birthday treat and it was amazing. The food and wine were incredibly tasty and original - all British ingredients. The most lovely thing though was the staff who clearly loved the food, wine and the job. They took time to explain the dishes, show our son the kitchen and make we had a wonderful time.

Beautiful setting for a classy, refined tasting experience focused on British seasonal produce with superbly curated wine pairings. The dining room is beautiful and the service is 10/10 from the moment you enter til when you leave. We adored all the courses - 10/10 for all the fish, sweetcorn, and the puds - just the duck wasn’t great, skin was chewy and it lacked flavour and was a bit dry. Can’t say enough for the wine pairings, some of the most expertly matched to the dishes I’ve seen. Loved it and will be back.

St Bart’s Restaurant sits beside the historic St Bartholomew the Great, the oldest surviving church in London, a location as atmospheric as it is iconic. With floor to ceiling windows framing the church’s ancient stonework, the dining room is beautifully curated with striking artworks, bespoke cutlery, and a warm, understated welcome that sets the tone for an extraordinary experience.

In a playful touch, the menu arrives closed, left to the guest’s discretion to open, offering the option of preserving an element of surprise. This sense of discovery is mirrored in the food itself.

Every ingredient is sourced from within the British Isles, but the culinary influences reach far beyond, weaving flavours from across Europe and Asia. Standout dishes like the squid noodles, the signature Hobnob, and even the opening sip of house made kombucha showcase remarkable depth, precision, and flair. Each bite was bold, layered, and thought provoking.

We opted for the wine pairing, which proved to be an inspired decision. Spanning vineyards across Europe and as far as Lebanon, each pour was thoughtfully chosen to complement and elevate the flavours on the plate.

Service was exceptional throughout, attentive without being intrusive. A heartfelt thank you to Oren and his team for making the experience feel both intimate and seamless.

It is clear why St Bart’s is the only restaurant in the UK to hold both a Michelin Star and a Green Michelin Star. It is not just a meal, it is a journey. One that lingers long after the final course. An unmissable destination for anyone serious about food.

Fantastic tasting menu with wonderful service with real attention to detail and personal food requirements. Excellent flavours and ingredients with delightful presentation. The lunch time shorter menu is excellent value.

I hosted a private dinner for 18 people at Restaurant St. Bart’s and it was an unforgettable experience. The space is absolutely beautiful with a warm, Scandinavian vibe that felt both elevated and inviting. The food was out of this world. Every course was so thoughtfully prepared and full of flavour. I completely forgot to take photos because I was too busy enjoying it all. The highlight of the night was hands down the dessert. It was the perfect ending to a flawless evening.

places.name: Evelyn's Table
places.editorial_summary: Tiny former beer cellar of an 18th Century pub for Modern European dishes and lesser known wines.

reviews.text: It deserves all the good reviews I have read and more. Intimate 12 cover fine dining restaurant. You get to sit literally around the kitchen and admire the magic as it happens. 5 course tasting menu with the option of drink pairing. You can choose which kind of pairing you want. We opted for half with and half no alcohol. It was a great choice because while the wine was delicious the non alcoholic drinks stole the show. I have never tasted fish courses highlighting the flavour of the fish so respectfully. Everything was perfect. Unforgettable!

Excellent! Fantastic service with great wine pairings by Isabel (Isobel?) and her colleague whose name I didn’t manage to catch. I was really impressed with their vegan offering - I didn’t feel like I was served a half-done dish much like many other restaurants’ vegan offerings - I was really satisfied with what I was served and the pairings weren’t adapted but still went brilliantly which shows how robust they were. Lovely touch of the chefs coming to chat with you at the end of the meal to see how everything was. Overall excellent and I look forward to returning.

My wife and I came here for our anniversary.

The food was exquisite and I would highly recommend both the non alcoholic and premium wine/beverage pairings. We were really lucky to have Isabelle guide us through our wines.

It was also lovely to find out we had extra courses but those should be a surprise (although the bread may have been the best bread course I’ve ever had). Would recommend without reservation.

Unique dining experience in a basement in Soho. The chefs and staff are friendly and the food is full of complicated favours and layers.  We did not order the drink package and order glasses / bottles from the menu direct is an alternative option.

It’s truly a miracle for 3 capable chefs to deliver so much in a small kitchen set up . It’s perhaps one of the best if not the best ways Michelin starred restaurants in London I dined in so far. The chefs told us that they change menu from time to time and I will visit again

Absolutely phenomenal! Wonderful staff, very professional kitchen. Very cosy atmosphere. They have set up the space well. Great to see the plating up with such precision and artistry. Every mouth full of food and sip of a drink was delicious leaving me wanting more!

places.name: Kitchen Table
places.editorial_summary: 19-seat U-shaped table around a cooking station, with a multi-course menu of small European dishes.

reviews.text:
My 4th visit and for the first time I went for pescatarian menu, honestly I was disappointed. While my fellow diners were enjoying the normal menu, I felt like a vegetarian. I was expecting the kitchen to replace the beef and duck with seafoods instead of pure vegetables. I wouldn’t have gone for the menu if I knew that was the case, huge anticipation ended in disappointment. I was later advised and the veggie replacements were advertised but wasn’t obvious to me, maybe they shouldn’t call this a pescatarian menu.

More seriously, I don’t know how a professional kitchen really functions, but seeing chefs putting spoons in their mouth for tasting, then put it to a communal pot, nothing wrong with that.  But, then other utensils were taken from the same pot to stir the dishes before plating?! I was quite shocked/disgusted to see that, raised to the waiters but was told the chefs didn’t put the spoon in their mouth. By then I observed two incidents! A small discussion was going on in the kitchen then the communal pot was removed in front of me to the other end of the kitchen. It didn’t address the problem at all, did it? If it wasn’t for my friend’s celebration, I would simply walk out. I don’t know how 2 stars were granted if hygiene was one big factor.

Though some of the dishes had interesting flavours, but the hygiene experience totally ruined my evening.

Amazing experience! It's a great set up for fine dining, the social aspect and connection with the chefs, service and other dinners is great. The food was beautiful, different and delicious. This is the 4th tasting menu I've tried, Wales, Houston, Tasmania and now Kitchen Table and they all bring something new, interesting, varied, exciting and again delicious.

Sensational service thanks mainly to Daniel and Alex.

Expected a lot, food really missed the mark. For a two star level especially.
Oyster w granita nice opener, but playing it v safe.
Crab pleasant but not memorable and lacked texture.
Tomato - absolutely top notch 2 star dish. Has everything. That’s where the meal peaked for me.
Scallop caviar supplement dish, again leveraging amazing ingredients, was good but not memorable. AbiT one note the way cucumber notes interact with the scallop.

Trout - one slice of trout sashimi size was completely tasteless as was the hollandaise. Really really missed the mark. Whole dish lacked flavour and texture.

Bread course which was a brioche was totally average, sub par for 2* imo. Especially when a chain in London like Aux Merveilleux de Fred casually sells a way better one.

The curry like noodles dish that followed has tons of interesting flavour, but that’s all it was - it felt like scraping the bottom of a curry plate with some interesting candied notes. The noodles themselves were a mushy and lacked any taste.

The agnolotti with goats curd and onion consommé. Were pleasant, safe flavour combo seen it done many places - also imo the onion doesn’t really match the rest of the dish.

“Main” slice of pork with tiny sauce portions on side. Pork lacked any flavour, dish lacked texture.

The tiniest quantity of food for a main course I had anywhere in recent memory.

Both deserts were super solid. Fig - memorable and perfectly balanced.
The lemon cake - texture wise was spot on, flavour wise ok but unmemorable.

Petty fours super solid.

I’m a very experienced diner would say whole experience taking 4 hours is unduly taking up diners time. I’d wait 20min for plates if they were absolutely knocking it out of the park flavour wise however on this occasion most of them were ordinary and nothing more.

As an experienced diner at multi star places have to comment on quantity of food. It’s inexcusably too little, we had the 10 course menu. Left hungry.

Daniel gave us 11 star service on a 10 star scale and made our night memorable.

Maybe caught the resto on a night off but have to say whole menu feels like quickly put together lacking the depth of concept typically expected of the high standards and reputation set by Kitchen Table itself in the London dining scene. Happy to reconsider on another visit.

Where to begin! This is hands down our favourite restaurant in all of London, and we love Michelin-starred spots and would like to think of ourselves as proper foodies. The attention to detail from the moment you step inside is just incredible. You’re greeted by none other than Sandia Chang herself, and welcomed into the bar area with a lovely drink and some amuse-bouche to start the experience. It already feels special by then.

You get the chance to chat with some of the team, get a glimpse of the menu, and start soaking in the atmosphere. I love that they’ve recently tweaked their offering a bit. There’s now a shorter and a longer menu, which is great as it opens the door for more people to try it, even if they’re not going for the full tasting experience.

After around 20 to 30 minutes, you’re moved into the main dining area, the kitchen itself, surrounded by a counter table where the real magic happens. It’s like watching a symphony of chefs, all working together to serve you the most memorable dinner. You get to interact with them if you feel like it. They're incredibly warm, happy to chat and answer your questions, but also never pushy. It’s really up to you how involved you want to be, which I really appreciate.

Seeing James Knappett in action alongside his brilliant team is amazing. The level of passion for food and hospitality is so obvious, it’s infectious. Both times we’ve been, our favourite dish has been the lobster, but honestly, there are so many wonderful surprises along the way. The wine pairings are fantastic, perfectly chosen by Sandia, and we even ended with a beautifully paired cider, which was such a delightful surprise.

We’ve had dinner here twice now, in different seasons and years, and we still can’t stop thinking about it. Just an unforgettable place. Thank you so, so much to the whole team, we’re definitely coming back!

PS: I had to pick a few photos as I had too many and don't want to ruin the surprise.

Unbelievable food & service. The staff were incredible, kudos to Alex, the 3 Sam’s & Daniel especially! Food was exceptional, meticulously prepared and presented, and the passion was infectious from the staff and Chefs. We had 14 courses and each one was unique and memorable.
Highly recommend if you fancy the ultimate fine dining experience!

places.name: Restaurant Story
places.editorial_summary: Chef Tom Sellers' novel approach to British classics. Choose from 6 or 10-course set menus.

reviews.text: Restaurant Story offers a beautifully curated fine dining experience with exceptional service from start to finish. The staff are warm, attentive and highly knowledgeable, making every guest feel welcome and well cared for. One of the standout touches is the bespoke printed menu tailored to your name and date, which adds a deeply personal element to the meal. The presentation is elegant, the storytelling thoughtful, and the atmosphere quietly luxurious without being stiff. A truly memorable evening. Pop to the terrace after lunch or dinner, a bustling vantage point. I’ll be back!

I had the privilege of working here nine years ago, and it’s remarkable to see how the dishes have evolved – even more refined, precise, and full of character. The storytelling woven into the meal and the way each course is guided and orchestrated make it an unforgettable experience. Flavours are masterfully balanced, the presentation is art, and the attention to detail is second to none. Next time we are in England, we will most certainly return – this place continues to set the standard for what a Michelin-starred restaurant should be.

We celebrated a birthday here. The cost for three people was £1650, but they didn’t even offer a slice of cake to say “happy birthday." The food was mediocre—nothing like the quality we experienced at other Michelin-starred restaurants in London, yet they charged more. Interestingly, they didn't enforce the dress code, as some guests arrived in T-shirts and casual dresses. We expected high-quality food and service given the price, but we were disappointed and wouldn't recommend it. If your budget is around £500 per person, it's better to explore other options in central London, where many good restaurants are available.

We tried to be harsh critiques , as we were paying a lot and it was Michelin. Some of the food was 10/10. They said the brioche bread was one of their classics , however we found it dry and lacking flavour in general.

The course is very filling we left the restaurant with our tummy stuffed. The whole experience will take 3 hours.

The reason I can’t give it more than 4 stars is because of the service charge . It was 13 percent! Making you pay more than 100 pounds in total. It was a bit exorbitant.

Absolutely superb wedding anniversary dinner. The service and personalisation were perfect. Food is at an exquisite level with a complexity and detail that surprises with every step on the tasting menu
Absolutely recommend as one of the best places we’ve been to.

Without doubt one of the best dining experiences I have had. If this doesn't get another Michelin star this year I will eat my hat.

We've followed chefs Jason and Spencer for many years, particularly enjoying Spencer Metzger's journey on Great British Menu a few years ago and when I heard of this collaboration with Jason Atherton this flew to the top of my list.

My wonderful wife was able to secure a reservation for my birthday this year and my word what a great experience this proved to be.

As soon as you enter you are made to feel as though you are the only people in the restaurant, the space is elegant and intimate, as we entered it was incredible to see Spencer and the rest of the chefs right there preparing the meals in front of you. The choreography and elegance of the service was second to none. I thought we were just lucky to see Spencer for a short time but throughout the meal he was a presence overseeing the service and coming over to explain the dishes along with his personable and equally talented staff.

Every single course was sensational, not a single curio or slight miss. While we were excited to experience each course as it came we were almost wistful that the previous course had finished... Now time to find an excuse to return as soon as possible!

Row on 5 is one of the most anticipated restaurant openings in London recently, and expectations were understandably high given chef Jason Atherton’s success with Row on 45 in Dubai. We visited for a special Valentine’s Day dinner and had an overall memorable but mixed experience.

The evening begins with a tour of the venue – including the wine cellar, kitchen, and champagne room – before you're seated downstairs for the opening courses. The introduction is impressive and clearly influenced by Frantzén, which unfortunately becomes a recurring theme throughout the evening. Some dishes felt a little too inspired, bordering on imitation.

Standout dishes included the langoustine claw, beautifully presented with engraved chopsticks (which we got to take home), and the main of sika deer, which was perfectly cooked and paired with thoughtful, sweet sauces. The seafood courses were strong and well-executed overall. That said, not all courses lived up to the same level — the use of tarts became repetitive, and a few bites (like the brioche and stilton tart) felt underwhelming being listed as an individual course, or oddly placed in the lineup.

Service was polished and professional, with personal touches that really elevated the evening — from engraved chopsticks to a personalised menu sealed with wax. It felt special. However, pacing was an issue. We waited too long between courses towards the end, with little communication from staff, and that disrupted the flow of the meal.

The wine list is massive — physically and in scale. While there’s a by-the-glass option available, the wine pairings felt overpriced, with “upgrades” on the cheaper pairings that came across as cheeky rather than premium. Charging £220 extra for a single dessert wine on a £145 pairing felt excessive.

Desserts were good but again lacked consistency. The petit fours were fun to try, but too many tarts and sweets made the end of the meal feel repetitive and overly sweet.

Row on 5 has all the elements of a top-tier fine dining experience — talented kitchen, high production value, polished service, and luxury touches — but it hasn’t fully found its identity yet. The team clearly has ambitions beyond their current 1 Michelin star, and with refinement, they could very well get there. For now, it’s a strong one-star experience with flashes of brilliance.

Would I return? Possibly, in a year or two. They're still finding their voice. I have to mention that the £250 price tag is one of the most expensive dinners in London, and is of questionable value in my experience.

What a lovely evening!  It’s rare that I’ve loved every course on a tasting menu, and especially so  with 17!    All delivered by craftsman who are clearly passionate, not only about the dishes they’ve created but also about the experience you’re having.  Elegant but not stuffy; intimate but not familiar; every last detail considered…from start to finish, they dazzled!  Anytime I’m in London, they are my first booking.

It took like 4 hours and a half to finish our dinner!🩷 but everything was worth it. Our first time here and we really enjoyed it. Food, absolutely amazing and perfect. Drinks, I had the nonalcoholic pairing one, went very well with the food, Amazing sommelier!! Good vibes, good atmosphere and good service.😆. We really had a good time. ☺️

Simply overrated. The tasting menu was advertised for 15 courses, 5 of which were the sweets/dessert. It felt more like 1 snack (4 bites portion size served separately), 5 seafood/meat dishes, one-bite cheese, pre-dessert, dessert and petit four (multiple little gadgets). They raised my expectations too high, but the actual experience was what it really meant.

Meat portion was tiny. Lamb dish was so small like scraps (tasted ok, just too tiny tiny to enjoy properly).  There was more sauce than the actual substance to eat. It is also noted that no textually identifiable vegetables were used in the tasting menu.

I also felt culinary skills were rather limited for £250 tasting menu price point (price excluded drinks and service charges). But the presentation could easily hide the limitations.

For one course, it was presented by a server with a serious bad breath, likely caused by smoking or something else. It spoiled the dish from anticipation and the rest of the dinner. Sine then, I was hoping someone else came to present the remaining dishes.

The open kitchen was good for a show, but the restaurant flow had to be flawless, expecting every detail to be visible to the diners. Chefs were all very busy even the open kitchen was only serving 1/3 of the available dining area seating.
