The pesto was so good that my friend even got one to take away. I haven’t tried any of their desserts yet, but I’ll definitely be back to give them a go!

Side note: They only accept cash so don't forget to bring some cash with you!

First time coming here. The environment, staff and service was incredible. Such a warm, friendly and cosy environment with speedy service despite it being crazy busy. We were fortunate enough to meet the siblings Navio Jnr and Anna who were so funny and inviting. We ordered the veggie breakfast with a side of big bang ciabatta which was so delicious and their homemade pesto is to die for.

Thank you for such a great experience! 🥰

Side note: Go in early because by 11am there was a really long line. Very popular!

Almost am hours wait. No problem as was expecting it busy on a Saturday.
Asked if I wanted to share a table....no problem (I was on my own).
Atmosphere, food, staff, pricing spot on.
Came from Norwich as been past before and it looked great

Aw man, I wish there were more cafe restaurants like this everywhere. The good old days still lives in this establishment. The old cockney hospitality from days gone are still present in this amazing little place. The food is outstanding. I own two Italian restaurants and I can tell the food here is nothing short of delicious, authentic and fresh. The owner (Pellici) still cooks every plate in the kitchen but still has time to laugh and play with all the customers. His wife is amazing. The staff is amazing, the food is amazing and the atmosphere is second to non. Love this place, thank you.

Got the Have the Lot (meat) and portion sizes were huge. 2 plates for 3 was enough. Special mention to the white sausage and fried toast, both were absolutely delicious. Space was slightly small and the queue can get quite long out the door. Owner was friendly and always checked in on the food and food was served quick!

Incredible, loved the food menu and enjoyed the 2-4-1 cocktails as well. Very generous as ends at 8pm on a Friday (unsure about other days). Perfect for sharing, small groups or solo dining in a quieter part of N1. Highly recommend the pork belly, lamb skewer and chimichurri potatoes. For drinks, the bees knees was a hit and well balanced. Definitely returning

Morr Coffee Brunch has quickly become one of my favorite spots. Every time I visit, I notice improvements and new additions, which shows their commitment to quality and customer satisfaction.

Their salads are absolutely delicious, with plenty of vegetarian and vegan options available. Recently, they've expanded with a new bar, which is a fantastic addition to the atmosphere.

You'll also find a great selection of pastries, sandwiches, and toasties—perfect for a quick bite or a relaxed meal.

The prices are very competitive, especially for the Islington area. You really get great value for what you pay.

I highly recommend Morr Coffee Brunch and truly hope they continue maintaining this high standard of service and ongoing improvement.

Special thanks to Berkay and his team for their cooperation and dedication!

Very nice cafe. On an expensive side for tiny baked goods but they taste amazing, actually. Tried their salad and sandwich and they are good as well. Nice atmosphere and nice friendly and efficient staff members. Great cafe to go to.

What a breath of fresh air: These guys have passion and look after their place well, they offer a chocolatey Brazilian house coffee and may well have a more fruity alternative as a guest roast, just ask. I had their Brazilian decaf flat white, which was very mellow, but had enough body to shine through the full fat milk.
They recommended their ricotta and leek swirl as a smaller savoury food option, which was delicious, cheese, vegetables, and pastry were perfectly balanced.
Will make this my default stop whenever I am in this area, which sadly is not very often.
Lovely place, welcoming staff, great food and great coffee!

Perfection in everything! What a bunch of passionate hospitality people serving the best coffee, cocktail & food! The Lamb Skewer so tender! I also love the dip of Aubergine and Hummus with the baby patatos! So flavorful! I can't wait to have it again!

Well done guys!

The only question is too cheap!! Please take my money guys!

places.name: Dulce Coffee London
places.formatted_address: 86 Whitechapel High St, London E1 7QX, UK
places.editorial_summary: A classic coffee shop drink menu alongside assorted sandwiches & baked goods with outdoor tables.

reviews.text:
Dulce Coffee Shop has quickly become one of my favourite spots in London! From the second you walk in, the vibe is warm and welcoming – you instantly feel at home. The staff are so friendly and always up for a chat, which makes the whole experience even better.

They’ve also got a great range of food, from fresh savoury dishes to amazing cakes and desserts. Everything I’ve tried has been delicious, and the portions are generous too. One of the things that really sets Dulce apart is that it’s HMC approved, so you know everything on the menu is halal and prepared to the highest standards. It’s such a relief to have that peace of mind when eating out.

The place itself is stylish but still cosy – perfect for catching up with friends, working on your laptop, or just enjoying a quiet coffee break. Prices are really reasonable for the quality you get, which makes it even better.

All in all, Dulce Coffee Shop is a real gem

Special place for breakfast brunch
So happy we found this place. Set us up for the day with really yummy food and amazing tea. We were seated downstairs and it was super busy but everything flowed like clockwork.  Good vibes. Great service too thank you

We had the full (English) breakfast on the menu consisting of Toast, mushroom, baked beans and turkey rashers.
My wife and I don’t take eggs so we requested for more portions of turkey rashers instead and they were lovely to oblige us.
We had it with orange juice - and speaking of the orange juice, the best so far I’ve had in the uk. Real Orange juice which I believe was just blended and not Tesco orange juice.

The breakfast was tasty and filling.
The service was great too.
12 pounds ish for what you see in each of the photos. Decent, considering our ibis hotel next door was also offering a 12 pounds breakfast. But expensive if you add coffee or juice.

Dulce Whitechapel is a lovely spot for a vegan or vegetarian breakfast. The dishes are thoughtfully prepared with fresh, wholesome ingredients that deliver good flavour without being overwhelming. I usually buy their croissant and enjoy their smooth, well-made coffee. The service is friendly and welcoming. While the cafe is small, it offers a cozy environment that makes it a pleasant place to visit. I would recommend Dulce Whitechapel to anyone looking for a reliable vegan or vegetarian breakfast, fresh pastries, and a nice cup of coffee in a warm setting.

Stopped here to pick buy some food for a picnic and were not disappointed.
We were served immediately and asked if we were dining in or taking out. Said we were taking out and were promptly offered two menus: one for food and one for drinks.
Our server then promptly took our order which was confirmed at the till point before payment.
The cakes and pastries on display, looked delicious and there were other secondary items for sale such as chilli oil, olives and sauces.
The staff were so friendly and you could tell there was some genuine camaraderie in the team.
Order was carefully  packed in paper bags and boxes. We were asked if we'd like our food heated. I was also asked which milk I'd like in my coffee.
Thank you Aayush, for making us smile with your banter with your colleague on the till whilst I was ordering. ☺️
The food was really enjoyable.
Would love to go back and sample the pastries next time.

Stylish café with amazing food!

EL&N London – Park Lane is a beautiful, Instagram-worthy spot with top-tier service and a relaxing vibe. I had the truffle omelette breakfast — rich, flavorful, and cooked to perfection. The staff were lovely and the whole experience felt effortlessly chic.

Perfect for a luxe brunch or coffee break in Mayfair. Highly recommend!

Fantastic little spot with a variety of refreshments,  Bakery goods, sandwiches,  salads, teas, and coffees.
Lovely staff, and fast service!
I enjoyed the avocado and egg for breakfast with peppermint tea.

This is one of the best and most elegant branches in terms of service. I requested a dish that was not available on the menu, and the staff member made every effort to fulfill my request, also offering other options in a very refined and polite manner. Thank you to all the staff at the branch opposite The Dorchester Hotel for their classy service, cheerful demeanor, and lovely spirit.
We had a lovely lunch. Hema made sure that we could sit together (we were with a group of 8). Everything was perfect, we had some sandwiches, pancakes and pastries.

Googled this cafe on the morning we went to the close by Postal museum instead of eating at our hotel. We are so glad we did. Sat down straight away and served quickly, efficiently and with genuine enthusiasm. Smashed avocado,poached eggs on toast for Wife, No5 breakfast for me ( I think ). Served quickly, hot and plenty of it for both of us. I mentioned to the owners I’ve had less breakfast for more money in the midlands. Highly recommend this gem of a cafe. Thanks guys.👍🏻

Found this delightful cafe around the corner from our hotel. We had breakfast every day during our short trip to London. The staff were friendly and polite, and the food was simply scrumptious. Lots of variety on the menu, and lots of healthy options if you don't fancy a classic fry up. Everything was also decently priced. I can't wait to come back again the next time I'm in London!

Just great. Fair choices for the hungry omnivore, veggie, vegan and the ultra restricted nibbler! Staff happy to mix things up and go off menu to be creative with what they have. Great coffee and the good ol’ English Breakfast with no corners cut. Great Mediterranean choices too. 10/10
Can’t wait to come back to this place. Perfect and delicious english breakfast, cozy environment and very friendly service!

Royal salmon with scrambled eggs and sourdough 10/10
Advocado and poached eggs to perfection 10/10. Lovely presentation, quick & amazing food. Salmon was so good. 😊

places.name: Feya
places.formatted_address: Unit 4, 6 Marble Arch, London W1H 7EJ, UK
places.vicinity: Unit 4, Marble Arch Tower, 6 Marble Arch, London

reviews.text: This restaurant was amazing and I would definitely recommend it. Food was full of flavor and they were able to accommodate without issue our Gluten Free requirements. (Sim) was an amazing hostess and we will certainly came back to eat at Feya any time we are in the area. Try this place out and you will not be disappointed. And the staff there are awesome.... Thank you Sim and staff for a great experience!

Although my food arrived a bit late, I still really enjoyed this restaurant — especially their breakfast and brunch! 🍳☕️ they also have great deserts menu 😋😋
The dishes were creative, full of flavor, and beautifully presented. If you ever pass by this area, make sure to stop by — it’s definitely worth a visit! 😋🌿

The atmosphere was quite nice, and the staff were very attentive and friendly, especially our waitress Pratibha who was very helpful and gave amazing recommendations. The food was great and came quickly.

The food was nice but the drinks and service were disappointing. Also didn’t help that it started to rain and they really should’ve opened the umbrellas but waited until it was pouring to open them. Interior was pretty but very crammed. Very very slow service. For the price one expects better service and better seating. Between the two of we paid over £65 for our brunch (just for 4 items) including the service fee.

An absolute gem on Bond Street!
This little place is a true find — stylish, cozy, and full of charm. The attention to detail and quality is outstanding, from the beautifully presented dishes to the carefully curated setting. Whether you’re stopping by for a drink or a laid-back brunch, you’re in for a treat. Everything feels thoughtfully done, and you can really tell they care. Highly recommend!

This is good coffee!!! % wise 100%. Love the place, the staff and the coffee. As a coffee enthusiast I appreciate the quality, consistency and staff professionalism! Love it, my go to place daily on my week stay in London! Highly recommended!

Arabica Coffee is my not-so-secret London vice. The coffee is Tokyo-level precision — smooth, complex, with that clean finish that makes you involuntarily close your eyes for a second. Every cup feels like it’s been brewed with borderline obsessive care… in the best possible way.

I’ve started “accidentally” navigating my day past here. Quick meeting nearby? Oh no, guess I have to pop in. Oops, wrong tube stop — might as well get a Kyoto coffee.

It’s the kind of place that quietly ruins other coffee for you. Once you’ve had Arabica, everything else feels like a compromise.

Note that this location doesn’t really have seating and gets heavily lined up so takeaway only.
outstanding coffee with diligent staff. Absolutely delightful. They should have more stars than this.

As a coffee enthusiast I would highly recommend their coffee. The coffee is smooth, flavourful and one of the best I've had. More so, I was served by a cute, chatty barista who made the experience even more delightful with their friendly attitude and genuine smile. It’s not just the quality of the coffee that stands out, but also the welcoming atmosphere and wonderful service. I’ll definitely be coming back for both the great brews and the warm hospitality.

I've seen quite a few people online try this place in cities like Tokyo and Hong Kong so when I came across it and needed a pick-me-up before a play later that night I decided to pop in.

The space was clean, contemporary, and chic, the perfect spot to grab a coffee and catch up with friends before heading out to do something else in the area.

The staff were friendly enough. It was nearing the end of the day and it's an area with a lot of tourists so I didn't expect anything out of the ordinary.

The coffee was excellent. I got the Kyoto latte and it was super smooth and the perfect treat after a long day.

If I come across another location during my future travels, I'll definitely pop in to try the other offerings.

places.name: Prufrock Coffee
places.editorial_summary: Expertly trained baristas serve bespoke brews in a buzzy open-plan cafe with minimal furnishings.

reviews.text:
#toast 521
— I would’ve never quite thought that coffee would go well with hollandaise but it’s such a complementary flavor- it’s a nice sweet, bitter floral note that adds to the overall dish. hollandaise wasn’t too heavy especially paired with grilled courgettes (seasonal greens)🥒🍳

I would definitely love to come back here on a weekday and people watch a bit— it’s a little crowded even on the weekdays all day but they have nice counter seats for single diners. Cozy for sure!

Follow @nomkakaii on Instagram for more toast travels!

This coffee shop is located in nice area where you can buy good coffee alongside excellent street food.
They use Red Brick Coffee Roasters beans and flat white is served in 6oz cup.
The taste is full of flavour and well balanced.
Barrista has done great work as you can see on picture.
I’ll no doubt keep coming back as there is something unique about this place,
On a scale 1 to 10 I would give it 7.5 points.

Have been here before and this place never disappoints! I vividly remember how good it was the first time we were here.And being back here is such pleasure. My partner is very particular with coffee, he follows James Hoffman and probably the reason why we went here before in the first place. He definitely knows this is a great place to get that good coffee especially if you are meticulous about the pouring technique and the coffee beans. Plus I love the simple but elevated dishes they serve! The staff are nice too. I think this place is really popular, so it can get quite busy…
The guest roast Lumen coffee from Colombia was AMAZING. Great coffee shop with super friendly staff. The seats outside can be amazing in good weather too. Massively recommend for their coffee beans.

This was one of the few coffee shops in London that I knew about before visiting, and it absolutely lived up to any expectations that I had. The filter coffee I had was delicious, and the space was big enough to have people both eating and just there for coffee. Would happily come back any time!

places.name: Monmouth Coffee Company
places.vicinity: The Riverside Bldg, 27 Monmouth St, London
places.editorial_summary: Fair-trade coffee & gourmet treats in the cafe & whole or freshly ground beans bagged to take home.

reviews.text: Loved the coffee. I tried it iced and hot and loved it in both ways. It wouldn’t be my go to place though as they don’t offer disposable cups. Also make sure to go in a good weather as most of their seats are outdoor.
Their flat white looks good and smooth, coffee aroma isn't strong enough for me. The pain au chocolat looks tasty but not crispy enough.

Flagship of the coffee place. Almost a must have for me each time when I am in London. No complaints, seats are scarce but they are very fast available if you are sharp!

Ask the Barista for the coffee recommendations. Iced or hot. I have tried them all. I am usually at the Borough Market branch.
Hands down, the best coffee in London! I’ve been coming here for over a decade and it never disappoints. Friendly people, amazing smell, and consistently great coffee. Highly recommend!

Very well made coffee but busy.

The cafe itself should feel relaxed and laid back - the decor gives it that feeling. It doesn’t though due to how many people queue. It feels quite busy and not somewhere you can easily relax. If you can get over that though they do make an excellent coffee, worth the hype!

places.name: Omotesando Koffee
places.editorial_summary: Boutique coffee chain across SouthEast Asia, light wood interior details, & Japanese-style design.

reviews.text: Better to study the menu online before, because you can only see the menu until you reach the till. Quiet, in favour of the wood interior, although the barista crazy busy on making coffee and super speedy. Coffee normal, and sit in experience is recommended. May need to wait for the seats.

Lovely little coffee shop with a sleek, minimalistic vibe. Great location and ideal for grabbing a quality drink on the go. I met there with friends before heading to an event and we enjoyed our drinks inside. The drinks are definitely the highlight – my hot chocolate was rich and full of flavour (though I do wish it came in a larger mug!), and my partner’s mocha was excellent.

The staff were friendly and attentive, which really added to the experience. That said, seating is a bit limited and not the most comfortable, and it can feel quite cramped when it gets busy. Also worth noting there’s no customer toilet. Still, for the quality of the drinks and the overall vibe, it’s definitely worth a visit.

I usually pick up a matcha to go and the taste is always strong and it’s clearly made well. Very cool spot but often can get incredibly busy and is a bit cramped. Service varies but it’s also a morning coffee pick up, so hard to expect much when churning out coffees. The square Japanese style little treats are really good.

Decent coffee place

Small and no tables . I got a cortado, which was ok. it was quite busy inside. Coffee is a bit on the pricier side. They only have one option of sweet
Staff could be improved and coffee

🤩This small, stylish coffee shop offers a cozy atmosphere with a sleek, minimalistic design—perfect for grabbing a high-quality drink or catching up with a friend.
👍The standout here is undeniably the hot matcha latte, which is crafted with noticeable care and precision. Smooth, rich, and perfectly balanced, it’s a clear sign that the shop uses high-grade matcha powder, making it one of the best matcha lattes around for true matcha lovers.

🙁The staff are just fine,
👎👎👎They had so dirty aprons that I immediately wanted to see the manager and say it to him/her. I just was in shock where these staff looks and what is in their minds, that they don’t see it and can’t see their colleagues too... It doesn’t add the welcoming vibe at all, though the space itself is quite compact with 👎😥limited and not particularly comfortable seating. It can get crowded, and it’s important to note there’s no customer restroom🤯😱.
Still, the overall drink quality more than makes up for the small drawbacks. Whether you're a matcha enthusiast or just looking for a well-made beverage, or a 👍coffee which is definitely is very good es well, this spot is definitely worth a visit. 👍It's a great place for a short break, a quick catch-up, or simply enjoying a perfectly made hot drink.
I definitely come back here to try something else and want to see what matcha powder they use.
🤯But I definitely know that there is NO washroom
If the manager or someone from this place will read my review, please write me what matcha powder you use🙏 It was the best I ever tried👍😜
👍👍👍🤗I definitely recommend this place

places.name: Kiss the Hippo Coffee
places.editorial_summary: Easygoing coffee shop with an understated interior, serving artisanal brews, cookies & pastries.

reviews.text:
Excellent coffee, they know how to steaming the milk for Flat White.. Many choices of coffee beans.. The Staff are friendly.. Also I try Almond Croissant.. It's tasty
One of the best cafe serving specialist coffee..

I went to collect a to good to go bag and I fed up getting a cappuccino, I got their George street blend it was delicious!! The staff was so friendly and added to the experience.  Tried their banana bread, mozzarella focaccia and the aubergine focaccia. Their sweet bakes were definitely worth trying but I wasn’t the biggest fan of the savoury. A solid 8.5/10

It was a nice cafe and we enjoyed the matcha lattes.

There were just a few times that the noise really escalated to the point we couldn't hear each other.. but most of the time it was average cafe noise.

Kiss the Hippo is one of my favourite coffee shops in London, they have other locations but this is the one I go to the most!

They're known for their amazing coffee but I don't really drink coffee so I usually get their Iced Chai Latte with Oat milk! It hits the spot everytime and the cup is so cute. I also got their banana bread, there's a nice bite to it as there's walnut chunks which is amazing.

The interior is also super nice, everything is smooth and wooden with a minimalist style.

Would recommend!

Absolutely love this spot. Kiss the Hippo Fitzrovia is a haven for coffee lovers — every cup is brewed with care and precision. The vibe is calm and stylish, perfect for a quiet break or catching up with a friend. Their flat white is consistently excellent, and the pastries are fresh and flavorful (highly recommend the croissant!). Staff are friendly, knowledgeable, and always happy to chat about the beans. Prices are on the higher side, but totally worth it for the quality. One of my favorite specialty coffee spots in London.

places.name: Kaffeine
places.formatted_address: 66 Great Titchfield St., London W1W 7QJ, UK
places.editorial_summary: Independent Aussie/Kiwi-owned coffee shop with deli-style breakfasts, sandwiches and salads.

reviews.text:
Great find in the famous Great Titchfield street of London , a stone’s throw from Oxford Circus.
The food was excellent, ditto for the coffees. This café/ restaurant is really small and seems to be over staffed. There are two wooden benches outside that can probably take no more than four people. There is not ample seating inside either.
My biggest disappointment was brunch not being served after 12 noon from Mon- Fri, why?
The atmosphere is somewhat non existent and their clientele consists of people from the neighbourhood, BBC employees having their coffee or the passing tourists that somehow feel unwelcome.
Payment is made upon ordering at the till but how cheeky of them to display on the till screen  prior to making payment if one would like to add 10%/15% or 20% gratuity or nothing ? Are we now in U.S mode in the UK? And what service are we talking about ? Serving you what you ordered at the till? Perhaps if this restaurant was bigger and offered table service than we could possibly talk about service charges?
I would highly recommend going there and I hope that management is thinking of having more spacious premises with perhaps more kitchen staff.

Cosy little coffee shop. Amazing staff! It can get a bit crowded in the morning, but the atmosphere is relaxed.
Good quality coffee. The pancake is on point and looks cute! Just maybe maple would be a better syrup for it (instead of chocolate).

Kaffeine, Great Titchfield Street, London W1

Kaffeine had been on my Fitzrovia hit list for ages, and I finally made it there one morning—and loved it so much I returned within days. This much-loved Aussie-style café is known for top-tier coffee (from Square Mile) and a refined brunch menu. Think espresso-drizzled pancakes, wild mushrooms on sourdough, and one of the best breakfast baps in London. Cosy interiors, great people-watching benches outside, and friendly vibes make it a standout for coffee lovers and brunch seekers alike in London W1.

#kaffeine #kaffeinefitzrovia #greattitchfieldstreet #londoncoffee #fitzroviacafe #w1coffee #brunchlondon #londonbrunchspots #squaremilecoffee #coffeelovers #coffeetime #brunchmenu #pancakeslondon #breakfastbap #fitzrovialondon #independentcoffee #flatwhitefix #londoncafes #brunchclub #coffeelife

Nice location. This area is like coffee shops mining. Nearly every step you can see and buy coffee. In Kaffeine  they sell Square Mile beans but after ask them you will be awarded to taste single origin Skylark Coffee Roastery product.
Good taste and aftertaste.
Thumbs up for barista.
On a scale 1 to 10  I'd give it 8 points.

Lovely small cafe tucked away a few minutes behind the busy Oxford circus. Coffee was ok very small cup, personally wished it was served warmer . They offer a limited selection of baked sweet treats, and they do serve a few breakfast dishes.

places.name: Rosslyn Coffee Queen Victoria Street
places.formatted_address: 78 Queen Victoria St, London EC4N 4SJ, UK
places.vicinity: York House, 78 Queen Victoria St, London
places.editorial_summary: Small, industrial-style coffee shop with window seating for espresso drinks, tea and baked goods.

reviews.text: Such a cute little coffee shop right in the heart of London, and it’s got such a great vibe. The staff are super friendly and make you feel welcome every time you visit. I keep coming back for their seasonal drinks; they’re always amazing, especially the winter and summer specials. It’s one of those spots that’s usually filled with locals, which I love because the energy is always so relaxed and positive, with everyone just enjoying their coffee and chatting. The location is perfect and easy to find, so it’s a great spot to pop into whether you’re in the area or just looking for somewhere to chill. Definitely one of my favorites in the city!

Locating at a corner of the street, the cafe can be spotted far away from the street. The design of the cafe was simply and comfortable. Plenty of benches were provided outside the cafe. There were a variety of coffee, tea and chocolate provided. We ordered an iced oat latte, a hot latte and a hot motcha. All were great. Service was efficient considering there were quite a lot of customers (we visited at 4:30pm on Wednesday). Would definitely come here again next time.

Quite simply the best coffee in London City.
Primarily takeaway, with half a dozen stools inside and a bench outside. Positioned to get a lot of sunshine: beautiful spot to enjoy a good flat white on a sunny day
Fantastic coffee. Very pleasant atmosphere in the nice part of The City. And yes, they work on Saturday.

I get my coffee here very rarely and it’s always good but recently they have brought out an espresso soft serve and it’s the perfect post lunch time sweet treat - for £3.70 you get the perfect size of delicious goodness! Highly recommend!

places.name: Ozone Coffee - Shoreditch
places.editorial_summary: Artisan roastery's coffee shop, with onsite bakery for breakfast, cakes, eggs and lunchtime snacks.

reviews.text: my go-to place for breakfast when in london. the scrambled eggs are so good that i specifically chose my hotel for this trip by the walking distance to ozone. could (and honestly did) eat here every day. the whole place looks really cool, the staff are lovely and the teas and coffees are always great too. totally recommend!

Poached eggs were lovely. I ordered spicy mushroom as a side dish which it was nice.
Anyway, lovely staff and atmosphere…good coffee. Just a little bit pricey but they are still the good place for breakfast.

I’ve been to Ozone Café in Shoreditch a few times now, and it always hits the mark. The coffee is reliably good, but the hot chocolate is easily the best I’ve had — rich, smooth, and comforting. I’ve tried a few dishes here; the minced lamb with mint yogurt was a favourite, though it’s not on the menu anymore. That said, I don’t mind the seasonal changes — keeps things fresh. I had the burger this time and it was really tasty and satisfying.

The atmosphere is relaxed and not too busy, making it a great spot for a proper catch-up with a friend. It’s also perfect for an early morning pick-me-up. Whether you’re after a hearty breakfast or a filling lunch, Ozone has you covered. Definitely one of my go-to cafés in the area.

For US travelers:

This place is probably one of the best brunch cafes that I have been to in England. It's a chain so there are a few others in various parts of London, but by this one in Shoreditch knocks the others out of the park. It was so good that I went there twice on back to back days that I stayed in Shoreditch area.

The food was great! I got the brunch menu that they have on weekends and the lunch menu that they have on weekdays (went on both Sunday and Monday). Portions are a bit small compared to America, but for London standards, it was very good.

I don't remember exactly the food we got but the scrambled eggs and sausage was on point. The lamb meat thing on the bread was on point. The mushroom thing was also on point. The kombucha and the latte was also on point. So good so good.

Just letting you know that there are only two restaurants I went twice in London. Dishoom and this place. If you somehow come by this place, its a good place to go. It's not like a must go place necessarily, but still very very good.

When they brought my plate I literally said WOW, first what a presentation and the taste matched!

I ordered mushrooms on toast but this was the best I’ve ever had. Very filling.

I’m not vegan but I try my best to always order vegan when I’m out and this hit all the levels needed. Full of flavour with a bit of spice, if you don’t want the spice just move some of the sauce away but it’s really good.

I also got a Aperol Spritz & a juice, I always have to order two drinks. Complimentary water.

I was able to bring my chihuahua and he just sat on he’s coat beside me, got some work done on my laptop.

There is certain times that you can sit and eat so make sure to check out the timings. But other times you can still get hot or cold drinks.

Definitely will be back, cosy warm and comfortable.

places.name: Rosslyn Coffee London Wall
places.editorial_summary: Pastries & custom-brewed gourmet coffee offered in a trendy, compact environment.

reviews.text:
One of the busiest coffee shops I’ve ever seen and even with all the chaos and having over 5 people working, they manage to give the best costumer experience.

Congrats to the team for having a really good coffee with nice tones and as well having a smile at all times.

They seemed like they were having the best time even though we know how busy it is and how things can be tricky.

Coffee was really good with strong flavour and I had a vegan protein ball which was tasty.

Once again congrats to the team and recommended to pass by and enjoy

A sign post of espresso soft serve beckoned outside the shop. Willingly I heeded its command and ordered one. The place had people going in and out and it was not hard to see why. The baristas are all female with happy energy working together. I guess if your house is a happy one, you don’t need social media for advertisement; people are drawn to it like moths to a flame. I added my order too so you can admire its beauty.

Whenever I am in London this is my go to place for coffee.
Both the drinks and the sold bean are solid quality.
Use the stamps to get one coffee free every 10 purchased.

Found the coffee tasteless brown water and threw it away after a few sips.

Each to their own I guess. The shop looks cool but £3.60 for tasteless coffee. Think Pret coffee tastes better. Ended up throwing it in the bin after a few sips and buying a coffee opposite the road at another place as didn’t want to waste my daily caffeine hit on this.

One of the best coffees in London. Soy and cow Flat whites like they were straight from a Melbourne hipsters teat.
All gals behind the counter definitely made a difference!
They all deserve a raise for their efficient and exceptional service.
Could do with a better line up /waiting set up as people milling about in the way of the doors was a bit chaotic.
Not the fault of the staff though, perhaps the owners could make it a bit easier for staff and customers!
not really a space for sit down, more a takeaway option. Although some bench seating and outside on the forecourt.
Thanks Ladies!

Come backing again (2 Oct 2025), my last day in London. This time I came here via Smith's Court.  I tried their cortado, beautifully made with latte art stayed intact. This is definitely a testament to skill -  the dense of the coffee, the right temperature to steam the milk, of course the coffee beans, all play a critical role.  Their croissant was good, though it would be even better offer a heatup service.  I also saw their cold brew is readily available in the fridge when I lined up the queue,  which I appreciates as I always enjoy cold brew without ice.

2nd time visit on 1 Oct 2025 for quick lunch. I ordered a cold crew and almond apricot pastry. Both are lovely. This is the best spot in the area.

1st time visit, 14 Sept 2025. I ordered the long black and it was excellent. The cafe had a very chill vibe, especially with Westerman's music playing during my visit.

This is the good place to have a snack before going to watch the musical.

The staff here are all friendly and considerate. I came twice for my holiday in London this time. I seem couldn't find anywhere else better than this cafe❤️the coffee is nice and the cake and apricot pastry are both delicious. No. 1 recommendation in central london.  Thank you🥰

I absolutely love this coffeeshop, especially the beautiful courtyard. It’s such a peaceful little oasis right in the middle of the city. I’ve had Flat Whites, Iced Coffee and most recently a Pumpkin Spice Latte made with real pumpkin purée. Honestly the best one I’ve ever had. I love sitting outside with a book or my headphones on, just enjoying the moment next to my coffee

Stopped by Hideaway Coffee around 10:30am on a Monday—it was already quite busy and a bit tricky to find a table. The shop itself is small with limited indoor seating, but the courtyard is a charming little sanctuary when the weather is nice. I ordered a chai latte (though the pumpkin spice latte seems to be the seasonal favorite right now). The chai was lovely—balanced and not overly sweet. Of course, reviewing a coffee shop without actually trying their coffee feels a bit like reviewing a movie after just watching the trailer… so I guess I’ll just have to come back. It’s a spot I’d happily return to if I’m in the neighborhood, but not one I’d go out of my way for.

I visited this café several times during my 10-day trip to London from Korea. It’s quite popular back home, and after going, I can see why. The space is stylish, and the coffee is excellent. I often ordered the iced vanilla lattes but even when I asked for it to be less sweet, they made it perfectly.  여기 넘 좋았음

Beautiful cafe with soya milk available as alternative option. Very peaceful, quiet and nice area. We had flat white and it’s amazing the temperature of the coffee was just right. Music wasn’t too loud and the staff were friendly.

The coffee was absolutely outstanding! I walked in on the first day of my trip and ended up coming back every single morning. The owner was incredibly kind, and the whole experience of choosing your coffee felt so personal and customizable. They’re extremely accommodating and happy to make suggestions based on your preferences. One highlight was trying the owner’s homemade peanut butter flavor—phenomenal! I sampled everything from iced lattes to hot lattes, and each one was perfect. This spot quickly became a daily must-visit for me and my mom :)

If you want coffee in London, you need to check this place out. I was just looking for a place to have a coffee in Mayfair and I’m sooo glad I went there.

The pastry I had was amazing too and I’d definitely go back there every time I visit London.

Great location , one of the staff very friendly the other a bit cold (I guess tired, who knows what's going on in their life). The space is small but good if you are one or two people. Some nice seats outside for larger group. Coffee is expensive but good: you are paying for location and ambiance. Worth a visit.

Just had one of my best coffees for quite a while, this time at Chill House Coffee Shop on Shepherd Street. Quite a cosy coffee shop but plenty of seating both inside and out and the delicious coffee is served in a china cup which for me makes a big difference. Service is quick and with a smile, thank you.

This small coffee shop in Central London started as a small food truck which eventually expanded to a shop because of the amazing quality and demand for their coffees and baked goods, so I had to put them to the test!

I tried their iced Chocoalate, Hazelnut croissants and their coffees and I can’t lie, they tasted amazing! The 4.9 rating on Google is valid so definitely check them out🙌

I’ve been trying cinnamon buns everywhere and this is one of the best! It was a delicately baked cinnamon bun that you can tell from the taste, appearance and texture.

The way they balanced the level of sweetness was absolutely outstanding. The sweetness comes from the combination of the cinnamon paste, sugary crunch and a fine layer of glaze on top. Surprisingly, you would not find it too sweet at all because of the hint of savoury coming from the dough and cinnamon paste. The chewiness of the bread paired with the crunchy sprinkle on top made the texture 10/10 for me. Not to mention the fragrance of cinnamon that lingers in your mouth, making you want to take another bite right away.

This would be my motivation to go to the uni lol I’m going to try the cardamon bun next time!

PS: Super friendly staff too! - thanks for the treat btw ;)

One of the best cardamom buns in town and plenty of choice of other delicious pastries. Cappuccino was also very good.
Lovely area to sit and read on a bench, I’ll be back
Best coffee shop in London! Thanks to the lovely and kind staff~

How lucky we were we had this spot right in front of UCL! Some of the best matcha in London, whisked in front of you and they know what they’re doing. Lovely staff and delicious pastries too! Will miss going here regularly:(

places.name: Batch Baby
places.formatted_address: Rose Lipman Building, 43 De Beauvoir Rd, London N1 5SF, UK
places.vicinity: Rose Lipman Building, 43 De Beauvoir Rd, London

reviews.text:
There is always a que at Batch Baby and for weeks I would cycle past and wonder why. Today I stopped by and found out why.

Great coffee, good pastries, a friendly service and good crowd of customers.

An Americano and fig Danish pastry cost me £8 and I had to que for 10mins on a busy Sunday morning, but it was worth it.

The coffee was very good and the pastry was light, crumbly and moist. In short I would suggest joining the que, I will be.

Cool. Hip place. I've been going there for 3 years consistently and saw it expand which is amazing. It's always busy so it's good to get there early to grab a table if you want to work or even get a coffee. The weight full of coffee is quite long usually, but it's definitely worth it and the people working there are always super kind. The pastries are also amazing as well as the sandwiches that they serve. It feels very homey in a way and a snapshot from the past.

The first time I came here I ordered a 1:1 which wasn’t great and I left thinking that I could’ve ordered better. Came back a second time and got the house batch and a flat white. Batch was served too cold and I couldn’t drink it all. Flat white was good however. I really want to like this place because the staff seem knowledgeable and the vibe is good but I’ve been underwhelmed each time. I was expecting better from a place I’d heard good things about. Maybe I’ve come on an off day??
Buzzing atmosphere, 3 exceptional batch brew filter coffees available (from Spanish roasters this month) and an awesome breakfast sandwich too. Really pleasant team at all times too.

I so much enjoy when I see specialty coffee shops taking care of their filter coffees (even more, when it's part of their name ;) ).

There was a selection of batch brews (4 if I recall correctly) and the one that i had was in a very good shape with rich flavours.

The people behind the bar were very polite and they took their time to explain me the available varieties.

places.name: Saint Nine Coffee
places.editorial_summary: Artisanal, barista-made coffee drinks served in a trendy counter-serve with splashy art.

reviews.text: Absolutely amazing looking specialty coffee spot. Loved the vibes and interior design. Most importantly, Saint Nine impressed me with very friendly service and the most welcoming host. Definitely a recommendation when in the area and also worth a detour when looking for great coffee in London.

The gentleman inside provided outstanding service and hospitality — truly first-class. I was amazed to find such a warm and welcoming coffee shop right in the heart of London. The coffee was excellent, and I even bought some drip bag coffee to take home. Truly recommended!
Top coffee, top service. A little bitter on the betty but the milk work is nice and smooth and it’s a perfect first cup of the day to get you going!
Laith and his team were so friendly and my macchiato was delicious! The stunning mural and decor make a very trendy atmosphere. Will come again!

Highly appreciation to this place. In my mind the owner is the equivalent to Heißenberg in Coffee Business. Must do for all coffee lovers&addicts, superb taste in every cup. Greetings go out, from the boys nearby Frankfurt ;)
I wasn't sure whether to give it a go as it looks quite new, but I am glad I gave it a shot. I'll be back definitely.

no Ac, disgusting decor with sticky tables and dirty chairs. nobody comes to serve you. and most importantly less than half the menu was available on my visit.
no ice-cream, barely any of the sides, just pizza
Amazing place to go and great customer service. Breakfast was amazing.
Lovely food and lovely customer service. Will come back again for sure.

Coffee London is a lovely place to enjoy a good coffee in a relaxed atmosphere. Their menu offers a variety of options, from classics such as espresso to more original alternatives, such as cold coffee with oat milk.

The service is fast and friendly. A perfect place to unwind or have a good time with friends.

places.name: Attendant Coffee Roasters | Fitzrovia
places.editorial_summary: Tiny, quirky coffee bar in restored Victorian public convenience, serving breakfast and light lunch.

reviews.text:
Very unique dining environment.
The entrance like the train station, the interior design like a man washroom BUT very clean of course.
The food is amazing. I love their sauces, all ingredients are well matched. The bread is soft and in good texture.
The coffee is great as well. I would said the best I had tried in London, even not many I had tried.

Such a great find!
It was small yet cozy and cute. The “train toilet” theme was executed perfectly and i found it quirky than weird. The match was so delicious and amazing priced considering its in central london

I highly recommend the avocado toast with a sunny-side-up egg — it’s honestly one of the best and most worth-it dishes I’ve had in London! They were super generous with the avocado, which made it even better.

The iced oat milk latte was also excellent, with a perfectly balanced coffee flavor.

The service was outstanding, and it was such a great way to start my morning as a tourist. A truly satisfying breakfast experience!

Quite possibly the best latte I’ve ever had—smooth, rich, and expertly crafted. If you’re a true coffee lover, this place is a must. The experience is made even more special by the café’s unique history, and the food holds its own with thoughtful, well-executed dishes. A memorable stop for both caffeine and culture.

Incredible place, small but full of charm. The coffee is the best I’ve had since I’ve been here, and as for the breakfast, I don’t even know what to say — it was delicious.
The service, without a doubt, is also on par with their products, as it was absolutely top-notch.

places.name: Coffee Island
places.formatted_address: 4b Upper St Martin's Ln, London WC2H 9NY, UK
places.vicinity: Orion House, 4b Upper St Martin's Ln, London

reviews.text: Coffee Island has the best coffee in Greece and London. What most people don't know is that they also offer excellent customer support.Since I live outside London, I placed an order with the London store so I could still enjoy proper Greek coffee at home. The order was unfortunately delivered incorrectly, but Ms. Dimitra was incredibly responsive and personally took care of everything. Thanks to her kindness and professionalism, the package was re-sent and arrived safely. A big thank you to Ms. Dimitra – excellent service and highly recommended!

A nice greek cafe on the heart of London. It was around 12 minutes walking distance from my hotel. The place is nice, the staff are friendly and fast. The freddo cappuccino was delicious. The price was good.

They have two cup sizes.
I've ordered Coffe Latte in bigger 12 oz cup.
I think is too big to taste real flavour of goodness. My suggestion is take 8 oz.
I've chosen single Brazil Alta Mogiana.
Thumbs up for barista for excellent skills.
On scale 1 to 10 points I'd give 7.5

Decent enough but the mugs were awful. I don't know what it is about certain types of food establishments but they seem to go for form over function and this cafe is definitely one of them. The mugs are completely impractical, lacking a hole in the handle to enable you to lift it safely. If you have any sort of restricted mobility in your hands you'll need to look elsewhere.

Visited yesterday when in London shopping for the day. Great location, very convenient but tucked away from the hustle and bustle. Decent amount of seating and no pressure to be really quick. I enjoyed the flat white I had, as well as the chance to sit and relax for a while. I didn't have any food but the options looked tasty. Nice environment, quiet but warm. Staff were friendly. Only downside was the toilet was blocked so couldn't be used but other than that it was excellent.

September 2025

Good coffee
Good Croissant
No non-sense minimalist interior
Average seating...could be better. May be they can have setup outside.
This was my first visit so liked it.
Amazing coffees from champion roasters and baristas. Friendly service, good location, accessible entrance. Coffee equipment and beans are also available for sale. Coffees are really exceptional!
Really excellent coffee at Formative! Service is good and friendly. The coffee is worth raving about, bean choice and milk work are on point. In my London Top 10 for sure! Highly recommend!

Stopped here while staying in Westminster. Flat whites were very well made! They had a small selection of what seemed to be very well made pastries. The pain-suisse was excellent! The place is very modern/clean and the staff were very friendly! Well done!

Stopped in for two flat whites and a pain au chocolat — everything was excellent. Perfectly balanced coffee, fresh pastry, and a cozy atmosphere. Honestly, nothing more needs to be said; I’ll just let the pictures speak for themselves.

places.name: Coffee & Friends
places.formatted_address: 12 Regent Street Saint James's, London SW1Y 4PE, UK

reviews.text:
This coffee shop is an absolute gem! The lattes are incredible—smooth, rich, and crafted with real care. Each one is perfectly balanced, and you can tell the baristas know their coffee inside out.

The cakes are just as impressive. Fresh, flavorful, and beautifully made—they strike the perfect balance between indulgent and comforting. It’s the kind of place where you can’t resist ordering a slice with your drink.

On top of that, the atmosphere is warm and inviting, making it a perfect spot to relax, catch up with friends, or enjoy a quiet moment.

Definitely a must-visit for anyone who loves great coffee and cake!
Beautiful art i ever witnessed on a cappuccino, it’s way more than a cup of coffee. Thank you and will see you next time!

Love this coffee shop, it's really friendly with a fantastic atmosphere. Absolutely love visiting here as the food and range of drinks is simply amazing and taste great too. Even love the difference in the coffee froth designs. Nice to have a coffee shop that's different from the usual chains.
Had an amazing experience with my friends here. From the service to the food it was fantastic. If you are looking for a cheeky coffee date with your friends this is the place to go

Coffee & Friends is the perfect spot for great coffee and good vibes. The atmosphere is cozy and welcoming, ideal for catching up with friends or even working on your laptop.

The coffee is top quality, always well prepared, and the menu offers tasty options to go along with it

places.name: Monmouth Coffee Company
places.editorial_summary: Fair-trade coffee & gourmet treats in the cafe & whole or freshly ground beans bagged to take home.

reviews.text: Coffee is amazing here. It's busy but there are still places to sit and the staff here know their coffee and happy to suggest different beans. Variety of beans to choose from if you like filter coffee. They have oatly oat milk if you are particular with that as well! Love the atmosphere.

Amazing coffee definitely worth the hype and then some 🔥🔥🔥🔥🔥🔥🔥🔥. I will be returning for another caffeine hit. A must visit. For non dairy people like me they do oat milk. I would be great if they had other non dairy options like coconut. The quality of the coffee was amazing. You can also buy coffee beans to take home. ☕☕☕☕🫘

There’s many things to like here. Pastries are great, service is very good, the set up of the whole cafe is very enjoyable to be a part of. Unfortunately the standards have dropped in the coffee over the last few years, flavour of the beans has gone down in favour of stronger more bitter cups. The milkwork is still really good. I’d still recommend a visit if you’re around Borough Market but I wouldn’t go out of your way to come here.

Loved the coffee here. The shop is very popular and it was packed inside. The service was quick even with the full house. Staff were friendly and lovely to deal with. The coffee was spot on, will definitely come back.
Highly recommended 👍🏼

My fave coffee joint in London whenever I stay nearby on my visits. They're proper coffee nerds here, who don't offer coffee in wasteful takeaway cups. So please remember to bring your reusable mugs, as this is a great initiative from this place and I totally support this cause. Great coffee flavours. It's always busy. Just note they're closed on Sundays. Staff are friendly, welcoming with a while and efficient, all of which is a lost art in hospitality these days. Reasonable prices for great coffee.

places.name: Arôme Bakery - Mercer Street
places.editorial_summary: Cosy bakery with a trendy vibe dishing up a fusion of French & Asian confections.

reviews.text: Great bakery and awsome pastries. Apple miso danish was wonderful, crispy dough and balanced taste. Also cappuccino and hojicha latte were very good. Honey toast wasn't to good as I expected, but not bad. It was too dry for me. Some cream with toast will be better. Nice, cozy atmosphere with asia influence. Very nice and helpful services. I am glad for recomendation and talk. Their another savoury and sweet pastries looks also interesting.

My favorite bakery in London by far. Everything I tried was amazing. The doughs are just perfect — whether it’s a brioche that makes the best toast, a croissant that’s laminated and shaped so beautifully (which is really hard to pull off), or a quiche that’s creamy in just the right way, not too eggy and not too heavy on the veggies. Everything felt super balanced and delicious. It’s one of those rare spots where every single thing you pick is a winner.

No doubt many people are aware of this bakery and its excellent reputation, so perhaps leaving a review is somewhat redundant. However, it’s been a couple of weeks since our very first visit and I’ve not stopped thinking about how much I enjoyed it! The Apple Miso Danish frankly deserves its own national holiday. That pesto mozzarella wonder was all but inhaled. And the fight over the last bite of pistachio and chocolate snail nearly ended in divorce with my husband. You know the drill though. Somewhere this good and this hyped gets queues. And we arrived first thing on a Saturday morning too! Be prepared to wait if you arrive later in the day - or just do as we did, which is grab and go as there’s plenty of seating dotted around where you can people watch while you scoff! Definitely one of those places which will beckon you to return to try out their other delectable looking items. In fact, it’s in my diary for this weekend! Oh and shoutout to the team at the counter who patiently dealt with my decision paralysis.

We queue for more than 45 minutes to get a seat. The croissant was crispy, fluffy and tasty. The homemade butter and jam enhanced the taste further. The pistachio, chocolate, escargot was good too. However, the coffee was average. Another  small unpleasant experience was people who queue for takeaway decided to have a sit, spoiling the if enjoyable experience.

As I’ve mentioned I love a dessert that’s also egg so you’re damn right I booked it over here when I caught wind of something called a giant egg custard tart. They were busy but the people working were very organized and kind and got me a fresh one from the oven!! The precision at work here, I mean just look, their pastries are so stupid pretty. I want to come back for the honey toast, pistachio roll and strawberry matcha tart if they have it again, on this day however I was on a mission so I just got my tart and rushed it home. I think they should consider making this with a different kind of pastry crust, maybe short, something with a snap because this current one was very buttery and on the soft side and I think texture contrast would take this to another level. That said, it was very good, and it was in fact a giant egg custard tart, so really, can’t complain. Thrilled this exits. Dreams do come true people

places.name: E5 Bakehouse
places.editorial_summary: Artisan bakery & cafe with a community focus serving sourdough bread, organic lunches & cakes.

reviews.text: Loved the feel of the place and how it has a mini market. Very spacious and clean bathrooms if i may add. Delicious coffee didn't like the cookie they braged about, was kinda dry for me. Will definitely try other things if I ever was in the area again

Holy cow this was good!! I had the fried egg & halloumi bun, as well as a corn madeline/scone thing. The bun was yummm — super tasty bread with just the right balance of sweet/savoury/umami.  I had the corn snack a little later and it really threw me off: moist inside but with a satisfying crust.  Would 100% return, this time with an empty stomach and some grocery bags.

I had an amazing time at the sourdough bread course at e5 Bakehouse last Saturday. It was a beautiful day, and the whole experience was inspiring from start to finish.
Alex, our teacher, was fantastic—so enthusiastic, knowledgeable, and clearly passionate about his craft. He made the learning process fun, clear, and really engaging. The rest of the team was just as warm and welcoming, creating a great atmosphere throughout the day.
I learned so much and left with new skills, more confidence, and, of course, lots of bread! Highly recommend this course to anyone curious about baking or just looking for a special and enjoyable experience in London.

First time coming here and loved the space. Great selection of bread and cakes as well as drinks. I ordered a BLT and a slice of their danish which tasted great! They have outdoor and indoor seating. I had a lovely time catching up with a friend here for a few hours, staff were very attentive and quick to clear up empty plates. Laptop friendly environment, would definitely love to come back on my own and do some work.
Excellent place where they make their own bread starting from the wheat with a mini mill, we ordered sandwiches and soups, there was a lot of space outside.

places.name: Aux pains de papy
places.formatted_address: 279 Grays Inn Rd, London WC1X 8QF, UK
places.editorial_summary: Quaint French bakery offers baked goods, sweets and sandwiches in a nook with limited seating.

reviews.text:
Stumbled upon this hidden gem near King's Cross station by chance and after trying couldn’t believe it wasn’t much busier than it is. The chocolate almond croissant was perfect - flaky, rich, and generously loaded with sliced almonds and had a gorgeously melted bar of good chocolate inside. The plain croissant? Deep golden layers, buttery aroma, crisp on the outside and soft within.

Coffee was spot-on. Strong, smooth, and made with care. Friendly service, no fuss, no rush. Just great pastries, great coffee, and a quiet spot to enjoy them. One of the best bakeries I've tried in London. Will return.

Croissants are one if my favorite things and so are boulangeries. I go to Paris quite often and I love trying different boulangeries. The croissant from this place is a croissant you could get in Paris and it's the best I've tried in London. Super crispy, flaky, a hint of butter, fluffy inside. I will come back for more!! We also tried the almond croissant and the chocolate eclair. These two were good, but for me the plain croissant was outstanding.

From the window, everything looked and smelled delicious, and it was! It was very difficult to choose what to eat because everything looked delicious. The chocolate bar and cappuccino were delicious! A special mention for the friendly and warm service I received.

I came across this cozy little café back in February. It looked so inviting and warm that I stepped inside, and the staff were incredibly kind, even recommending their favourites and a little backstory of the cafe. I’m not usually a coffee drinker, so I went for a hot chocolate, and it was absolutely stunning. Looking forward to my next visit when I’m back in London!

After being recommended this location by a friend, I'd made a point to visit it for a weekly treat when possible around my lectures in the autumn/winter. The staff was always nice, and though the goods could maybe be considered expensive, you absolutely get your money's worth! Everything I have had here has not only been well made and decadent, but filling too. Lovely place!

Stopped here somewhat recently on a whim. Super busy! They have a really great selection available - We both had one of the beignets, which were very tasty but I think they could've been a bit more generous with the toppings for the price, service was quick and friendly, will definitely be back again if we're in the area.

The street it’s located on, along with the overall vibe and style of the place, was really charming. The coffee was excellent. The baked goods we tried were tasty, though the savory ones we chose were a bit too oily for our liking. As for the sweet option, it was nice, but we would have preferred it without the chocolate sauce. Overall, it’s a lovely spot with a cozy atmosphere, definitely worth a visit.

It’s definitely an “Instagram” spot - everything was oversized and well made. The proportions of the pastries were a bit off, aka not enough pastry to sausage roll or croissant to chocolate ratio.
Plenty of options means there is something for everyone, but I do believe this is one of those over hyped places

I WANT TO GIVE FORTITUDE 10000 STARS!!! My fav bakery in town. Always come for the feta & spinach. Other recommendation is the almond croissant!

Better to come before 11.

The coffee is also amazing. Vanilla latte with oat milk.
High prices for high quality goods! Did not disappoint in the slightest. Lovely flavours and light pastry for both sweet and savoury items. Benches to sit out the front, no toilets available.

places.name: Beigel Bake
places.editorial_summary: 24-hour bakery known for traditional Jewish-style filled bagels such as salt beef and smoked salmon.

reviews.text: Honestly the best place for beigels!!! The salt beef-gherkin-mustard combo is always my favourite, but even a plain cream cheese beigel here is amazing. The texture of the beigel is just simply the best. Never fail to pop in here whenever I’m back in London!

I happened to pass by and saw that there was a long line of people, and because it was a Sunday I chose to come two days later when there were fewer people and at a more convenient time. On the one hand, the saleswoman didn't understand that I asked for the 'house dish', on the other hand, the bib sandwich was full of tender meat and was delicious. I enjoyed it very much and will go back there again.

Decent bagel at this bakery that is an institution in London. I had a salt beef beigel with extra of pickles. There is a good amount of meat in the beigel per serving . Meat is not dry and it’s flavoursome. Service was fast (I was not stuck in a queue). I would say if you are in the area looking for something to eat /after a night out this is your best bet. Good value for money.

It’s been quite a while since I’ve last been here and tried the Salt beef bagel. It was lunch time and as usual there’s the typical queue (full of tourists), the turnover was quick so I was served in a few minutes.

Sadly, it seems they have changed some components of the salt beef bagel. The mustard that was usually my favourite part was subtle and flat, missing its usual strong kick. The pickles weren’t as punchy neither with the salt beef being lukewarm. Overall it was underwhelming. It was tasty, but it did not live up to what I had remembered a few years back.

We went back twice for the salt beef bagel and sandwich after trying it the first time—it was absolutely incredible! The meat was melt-in-your-mouth tender, and the bagel was perfectly fresh. We stood in line but didn’t have to wait long, even when it's busy, the service is impressively efficient. The salmon cream cheese option was tasty too, but if you're visiting, don’t miss the salt beef bagel or sandwich—it's a must try!

Wonderful assortment of pastries but the ones we ordered were just alright, nothing mindblowing. A little too sweet for our liking. Soft serve with honey toast was an interesting offer that we don’t see many in other cafes/bakeries so it was lovely. Wanted the vanilla flavour soft serve but it was sold out so I had the chocolate one which was decent. The honey toast that came with it was a little too sweet and dry though. It’s a lovely place with great vibes for a coffee with a friend, to rest your legs after some shopping in central London but not specifically be there for the baked goods. Menu offers breakfast/brunch type of food I have yet to try but I’ll probably skip that. Staff were extremely helpful and kind though. Made us feel really welcomed despite being so busy.

We sat upstairs right by the window with the scenic view of the street. The pastries were each made to be a perfect image of itself. The labneh cherry tomato toasty was the best savory breakfast sandwich you can ask for to be balanced with the sweetness of the blueberry tart - which is easy to miss, but not in Chestnut - every bite you get fresh blueberries and never a jammy sticking to your teeth goo, but a wonderful creamy filling encased by the more exquisite laminated dough.
Not one miss!

Came in just before 6. There wasn’t any seating downstairs expect a small table near the entrance which we had to sit there was four of us. Even though the cafe was open we was told upstairs seating was closed. Wanted the Karak tea which wasn’t available, either was the brookie. Ordered two scoops of ice cream which I asked for choc. Then I see one of the guys giving vanilla asked the lady that was serving me that I asked for choc which she said there wasn’t any available even though she took my order. She wasn’t paying attention as she kept repeating my order. As we sat with our hot choc and the basic vanilla ice cream. We can see the bins getting taken out, everything getting cleared up. There was still people coming in. Considering we were in convent garden and you pay more than average I don’t expect to see huge bins going past me multiple times, aswell everything getting cleared up. The cafe is open and should accommodate accordingly during the opening hours. Won’t be coming in a hurry anytime soon.

Chestnut Bakery in Covent Garden has quickly become one of my favorite spots in London for pastries and coffee. The atmosphere is warm and welcoming, with a modern yet cozy design that makes it perfect for a relaxed break during a busy day in the city.
The staff are friendly, which adds to the overall experience and makes you feel at home even in the middle of a busy area like Covent Garden.
The highlight for me is definitely their tiramisu Danish. It’s unlike anything I’ve tried before. It feels indulgent without being overly sweet, and it’s the kind of pastry you’ll think about long after you’ve left. I honestly would come back just for that one item.
They also offer a wide selection of baked goods, The coffee is consistently good too, which makes it a perfect pairing with any pastry. I also appreciate that everything feels fresh, and the presentation of the pastries makes it hard to choose just one. The place is great whether you want to sit inside and enjoy the calm atmosphere or grab something to take away while exploring Covent Garden.
What’s exciting is that Chestnut Bakery also has another branch in Riyadh, so it’s great to see them bringing their unique style and quality to different parts of the world.
If you’re in Covent Garden and looking for a bakery that goes beyond the usual, I highly recommend Chestnut Bakery.

Top notch bakery, cute, great baked goods, and just super tasty. All the pastries were buttery, especially the croissant. The zataar knot was fantastic, especially with a bit of labneh. The pistachio croissant was sweet, but not sugary. Overall just great, the service was a bit too slow though.

places.name: The Dusty Knuckle Bakery
places.editorial_summary: Light cafe fare such as creative sandwiches & salads with coffee drinks & fresh breads to-go.

reviews.text:
so yum! ive had this bakery on my radar for a while now, and it was so worth the wait to come along.
whilst £11 is obviously a lot for a sandwich, you 100% get what you pay for. The homemade bread was absolutely lovely and the sandwich was packed full of flavourful filling.
the atmosphere was lovely, and sitting outside was great. service was brilliant and hardly a wait for my food either. i came at about 12 o’clock and didn’t have to queue, however when i left at 12:40 there was a large queue, so definitely get there a bit earlier if you want a sandwich! they deserve the popularity though, i absolutely loved this bakery.

After being recommended this bakery I was eager to visit and it didn't disappoint.

Maybe one of the largest bakeries you'll ever visit, hidden down the end of a back lane with extensive outdoor seating it's a great spot for brunch or lunch on the weekend just be prepared to que.

I visited on a Saturday and waited no more than a couple of minutes and tried two of my favourite UK stallwards the Morning Roll (chai spiced sugar dusted cruffin) and the go-to Honey and Feta swirl which was laden with sesame and poppy seeds and was absolutely banging!

All their pastries and bread looked top tier. Flaky lamination and a deep caramel crust on all their sourdough (just the way I like it!)

The breakfast sando looked unreal, and is clearly a top seller for good reason.

I look forward to my next visit to try the rest!

Keep up the good work team! 🤘

Unbeatable breads, amazing sandwiches, and really creative options! The queue this past July 6th weekend was wild, but worth it! We waited in the queue about 20 minutes until we ordered, but there were plenty of tables and we were able to sit 4 of us at a table inside. Despite the crowds, service was so fast! Our sandwiches + drinks arrived within 8-10 minutes of ordering and were of course, the best in London.

It’s the first time I’ve seen it this busy, but even with the queue, these baked goods are always worth it.

Best sandwich I’ve ever had! If you want the focaccia sandwiches then you need to come at 11:30! The till doesn’t take payments for the order unless it is exactly 11:30 and after. Takeaway orders are collected outside of the shop.

Although I’m not a big fan of coronation chicken, but they’ve done very well at combining different ingredients, crunchy nuts, herbs, green apple slices, not to mention the airy and flavourful sour dough potato bread, I can see why people queue up here for food.

The only downside to me is that the place gets so busy and it can be crowded. Also as a first time visitor, there’s not much guidance on what to do, you just sort of figure it out. The location for me was a little hard to find, you walk down the alleyway and it is the shop to your right, the name of the shop wasn’t visible unless you step opposite the shop.

I had the pleasure of visiting The Dusty Knuckle in Dalston for breakfast today, and it was an experience worth sharing. Nestled in the Abbot Street Car Park, this café offers a unique blend of industrial charm and warm hospitality.​

I opted for the Egg, Chilli Cheese on focaccia with a side of bacon. The sandwich was a delightful fusion of spicy pickled green chillies, spring onions, and fresh coriander, all between slices of soft focaccia.

Their sourdough bread is renowned, and the pastries—ranging from morning buns to cinnamon rolls—are simply irresistible. The open-plan kitchen allows patrons to witness the baking process firsthand, adding to the authenticity of the experience. ​They also have bakery classes going on simultaneously!

Beyond the food, The Dusty Knuckle stands out for its mission to empower at-risk youth through mentorship and employment opportunities. This dedication to community enrichment adds a meaningful layer to the overall experience. ​

The seating area, both indoors and outdoors, offers ample space, making it suitable for individuals, families, and groups. Be prepared for popularity, especially during peak hours, but the quality of food and service makes any wait worthwhile.​ ❤️

1. Egg chilli cheese focaccia with bacon - £9.8

2. Hot chocolate - £4.5
3. Bacon Sarnie - £8.5

places.name: COMMON BREADS
places.formatted_address: 110 Buckingham Palace Rd, London SW1W 9SA, UK

reviews.text:
The cheese manakish, musakhan, and spinach pies were absolutely incredible. The owner manages the restaurant himself, and the location is just perfect. I truly congratulate him and wish him even more success and new branches in the future.

You can actually ask them to make the pastries in a small size for takeaway — they were absolutely delicious, arrived hot and fresh, and perfectly clean. Truly amazing!

We recently hosted a work event and chose Common Breads for the catering. From start to finish, the experience was exceptional. They tailored our order perfectly, offering a wide variety of options to suit everyone’s preferences. The food was outstanding — fresh, delicious, and of the highest quality — and the service was just as impressive.

Our team and guests were genuinely impressed, and it made the event feel extra special. I would wholeheartedly recommend Common Breads to anyone looking for catering that combines quality, variety, and excellent service.

The chicken musakhan manouche was the best dish - highly recommended. The other dishes were alright. Worth a try but nothing to rave about.

Service is great and staff are friendly.

Got some quick bites on a weekday evening. Loved the ambience, decor and the layout. It was quiet when I went and the perfect spot to read.

The food and service is lovely, would love to come back to try more items on the menu.

Every visit is perfect! the food is always fresh, flavorful, and truly the best Lebanese in the city. Their oat chai is unmatched, and the owner ( Kamal) is so warm and welcoming. Clean, professional, 10/10.I’d love to see them open more locations.

places.name: Bageriet
places.editorial_summary: Compact Nordic bakery & cafe with traditional Swedish cakes and pastries to eat in or take away.

reviews.text: As a Swedish Londoner this place will always have a warm place in my heart!! I also had the most wonderful few shifts working here just before Covid started, and got to learn about how everything’s made on the premisses! Can’t recommend enough if you want some authentic Swedish cinnamon buns 💕

They are comparable to any bakery in Stockholm👌 they even make the princess cake. It is pretty small, but the atmosphere is cosy. The pastries were delicious, but the pistachio one was a little too sweet for me. The coffee can be improved.

Wow!! What a selection, what a bakers, what customer service!! I ordered a special cake and 48hrs it was ready to collect and the engraving I asked for, perfectly done, just as I asked for! Would recommend any day, even just for a visit to see (or sample) the cakes!

We visited this cute and cosy bakery for breakfast. They have different kinds of Swedish pastries, cookies and cakes. Everything looks so delicious that it is quite hard to make a decision. Great and varied tea selection. The staff is very polite and helpful and overall good ambients with perfect lighting and music.

Service was warm and friendly, recommending which pastries to try.

Notgrotta (Extra buttery shortbread with hazelnut chocolate) indeed had a buttery crumbly melt in your mouth tart base with molten chocolate within.

Josefin (Almond tart with orange) had a nice balance of almond (not artificial taste) and refreshing orange.

The cinnamon bun, which I thought would be the highlight, was quite disappointing. Not as fluffy as I thought it would be. And a bit too much cinnamon.

places.name: Miel Bakery
places.editorial_summary: Cosy, classic French bakery offering housemade breads, pastries & seasonal tarts, plus hot drinks.

reviews.text: I wanted to love this bakery but I felt my almond croissant was a little too sweet. It was well filled and the pastry was extra buttery. The cinnamon buns looked amazing here so I would come back to try. Only two outdoor seats for seating. Pastries range from £3.5-£6 so some are definitely on the premium priced side. My almond croissant was £4.50.

As we were eating our croissants outside an older lady walked past and blared out “I can’t just walk past, I have to get one”. And it makes sense once you try one. Delicious heavenly croissants. This is an exceptional bakery offering a range of both sweet and savory croissants.
A truly lovely local bakery with amazing pastries. Out of the oven fresh, all absolutely delicious made with fresh and quality ingredients. Their coffee is also phenomenal.

The worker made our experience greater than expected! Friendly and helpful worker. We loved the Flat White and Iced Hojicha. Nice and quiet place (we were there around 3-4pm). Overall experience is 5/5 🌟🌟🌟🌟🌟! Will definitely come back.

Amazing bakery. My favourite in London! All the classic French pastries are delicious! Don’t miss their pain au chocolat, kouign amann, banana bread and the daily special square croissants. The coffee is also great :)

places.name: Maison Bertaux
places.editorial_summary: 19th-century, French patisserie and tea rooms with marble-topped tables, plus art gallery spaces.

reviews.text: Yummy pastries and busy workers!! Recommend rosehip tea 🌹and the mixed fruit 🍓cheesecake and the raspberry tart. Both were light and creamy. ✨🤍SO good!! We got 6 pastries and two pots of tea. 🫖That FILLED the four of us up and filled the table as well!! 100% recommend if you want a cheaper afternoon tea with more bang for your buck. 💷💥

4.5/5.
I cannot get over the scones and the collated cream and the fresh berry tart. Especially the latter. The creme inside was divine. The outer whipped cream is so light and airy. The dessert itself is perfectly sweet. Not cloying, not un-satisfying. Just perfect. With the freshest assortment of berries. Their hot chocolate is comforting, especially on a cold day. The service is good, there is seating. Would definitely visit this place many, many times to try everything they have on their menu. Outstanding stuff!

Scones were very good. Very big piece and very generous with the jam and clotted cream. At first we were hesitant as the scone was not heated up but it was still very very good, especially with the tea! We also had the berry tart which was very refreshing. Price was reasonable, 40 pounds for 3 scones, 1 tart, and 2 teas. Would come back again!

Such a cute little shop!
A kind grandpa warmly introduced all the items to us.
We came especially to try their scones—served with traditional clotted cream and jam, they were super crispy and delicious.
Highly recommend the fruit-flavored ones—they’re so good!
The staff even thoughtfully reminded us to keep an eye on our belongings and phones.
Sitting inside with a gentle breeze and enjoying these classic British treats—totally worth it!
Absolutely delightful! The pastries are fresh, beautifully crafted, and full of authentic French flavor. A must-visit for anyone with a sweet tooth. 🥐✨

places.name: Chestnut Bakery, Belgravia
places.editorial_summary: International breads, pastries & sandwiches featured in a high-end bakery & cafe setup.

reviews.text:
Wonderful place to kick start the day. My favorite Chestnut Bakery branch in a very beautiful and aesthetic area of the city (posh 😅). Big selection of sweet and savory pastries plus the breakfast dishes, you can’t go wrong here. Service was very good and staff were welcoming and helpful. Don’t miss their crispy cinnamon roll.
Highly recommended 👍🏼
