As we soaked in the lively atmosphere, we couldn’t help but admire how perfectly the lighting and acoustics complemented the stunning church setting; it's truly a party in a place you’d least expect.

The food was as memorable as the music. We kicked things off with the Amazing Grace Sharer, a generous and flavour-packed platter featuring crispy Japanese Fried Chicken, sticky-sweet Korean Chicken Wings, smoky Padron Peppers, juicy Corn Ribs, and moreish Korean Potato Bites. Each bite offered something bold, spicy, or savoury, a masterclass in Asian-inspired comfort food.

We followed this with a couple of Fried Chicken Baos, which were soft, fluffy, and bursting with flavour thanks to the tangy pickles, creamy Gochujang mayo, sesame, and spring onions. But the standout dish for us was the Chicken Burger. A free-range chicken coated in crunchy panko and sesame, layered with Kewpie mayo, fresh lettuce, and pickles. It’s rich, crispy, juicy, and a definite must-try. On the side, I ordered the Amazing Rice, which lived up to its name: a fragrant mix of spring onion and ginger oil, tare sauce, crispy onion, and sesame. It’s the kind of side you could happily eat on its own.

For dessert, we shared the Salted Caramel Brownie, served warm and delicately dusted with icing sugar. It was rich, gooey, and exactly the indulgent finale you want after a night of dancing and feasting. We also had a trio of Japanese Mochi Ice Cream—Mango, Chocolate, and Vanilla—which added a refreshing, chewy, and cool contrast to the brownie.

All chicken served here is halal, which made our meal worry-free and even more enjoyable. The mocktails were just as thoughtfully crafted as everything else. My wife had the Espresso Martini (alcohol-free), made with Amazing Grace’s house coffee mix and vanilla syrup; she called it one of the best she’s ever had. I loved my Grenadine Bramble, a bright, citrusy blend of Lyre’s Original, lime juice, sugar, and grenadine . It was refreshing, not overly sweet, and paired well with the food.

A special mention goes to Dio, who looked after us throughout the evening. Friendly, attentive, and genuinely warm, he made us feel right at home, even in a venue buzzing with energy.

By the end of the night, we’d not only eaten incredibly well, but we’d danced, laughed, and soaked up one of the most unique dining experiences in London. If you’re looking for a place that hits all the right notes, food, vibes, and service , Amazing Grace London Bridge is the one. We can’t wait to return.

Feel like this place has so much potential… The food was good and the music was entertaining, however found the staff rude. I could understand if the restaurant was extremely busy and staff were under pressure, however it wasn’t. Food is ordered from the bar and when I went to order, the staff member wasn’t friendly and it seemed a chore for them to take my order. I feel like the atmosphere was let down by the customer service. Overall, I don’t think I would return unfortunately

We went through using first table and the food was delicious! Atmosphere were great and the staff were 10/10, I lost something in there and the staff went above and beyond to help me find it. They also had a live performer ANDD a photo booth! Nothing to fault

I was out for First Fridays at the Tate Modern this month and a friend suggested we grab a drink at Amazing Grace afterwards. I wasn't totally sure what to expect, and while the walk over felt a bit longer than I anticipated, it ended up being so worth it.

There was a modest £5 cover, which honestly felt like a steal once we got inside. The energy in the room was electric! The live performers were phenomenal—seriously, the kind of voices that make you stop mid-sentence just to soak it all in. The upstairs lounge had a great vibe, and the dancefloor was already buzzing... and it was only around 10:15pm!

I spotted a few people still enjoying food, but unfortunately the kitchen had just closed by the time we arrived. Not a huge deal—just means I’ll definitely be back to give the menu a proper try. Between the music, the drinks, and the atmosphere, Amazing Grace has officially earned a spot on my regular date night list.

If you’re in the area and looking for something fun, lively, and a little unexpected—this place is it.

Fun night with tasty food and great drinks. Early evening visit was perfect before it got a bit hectic but sure it’s buzzing as the night goes on! The Korean Potato Bites were the absolute stars. So yum.

places.name: Nightjar Shoreditch
places.editorial_summary: Speakeasy-style subterranean bar with live jazz and blues, for cocktails and rare spirits.

reviews.text: Great venue with fantastic cocktails and small bites, my friends and I got pretty lucky and had a blues band while we were there. We had a couple of cocktails while listening to them and got a few bites. Definitely will be back next time I’m in town. Service was great, very attentive. The door guy was great as well.

The place is really gorgeous and the concept behind is really fun. Nice jazz music, old cocktails. However, the service is terrible, the waitresses were terrible rude. We had a timed reservation and we knew our time was limited but all the time she was trying to pick out drinks even when they were not finished and just their attitude was really off.
Nightjar has a FULL menu of thoughtfully curated cocktails in an adorable menu book! Location is very speakeasy vibes. Must check this place out if you're in the area.

Worth seeking this wonderful cocktail bar with live jazz out.  Not the easiest to find but worth the persistence! Discovering this speakeasy styled basement bar made my night.  It’s small so am glad I went on a Tuesday night to secure my spot. Loved the cocktails and the great music

A hidden gem! We were pleasantly surprised to find this pub tucked away, offering not only great drinks but also that little extra touch that made the visit special. Friendly atmosphere, attentive service, and overall a wonderful experience — highly recommended!

places.name: Alcotraz London: Cell Block Two-One-Two
places.formatted_address: Unit 3B, 127 Hackney Rd, London E2 8GY, UK
places.vicinity: Unit 3B, Nichols Court, 127 Hackney Rd, London
places.editorial_summary: Theatrical cocktail bar where guests wear orange jumpsuits, drink in jail cells & smuggle liquor.

reviews.text:
I thought it would just be a prison themed bar, four of us went. It was honestly really good. Absolutely hilarious the whole time.  I'd say it's more of a story with actors involved. They keep you involved with the story the whole time. You bring in your own alcohol and they use that bottle for your cocktails.

The cocktails were all absolutely amazing, too.

We are planning to do Moonshine next door. It's the same company. I have high expectations.

The experience was amazing, the actors were so good at their roles and funny. They interact with you on side missions and you get a photo taken. Would definitely recommend to anyone was so worth it and you get quite alot of cocktails whilst in there.

This was a great experience. Have done the aurora immersive experience prior to this so thought we would give it a go. This one had a good mix of comedy and theatrics. However felt that you were left a long time in your cell compared to the aurora one that was continuous acting around you. Great thing to do though and cocktails were fun!

COOLEST EXPERIENCE EVER!

So basically you get sent into prison and get to experience what it would be like. Everyone who works there is in acting mode so it would be your best bet to also act like someone who is actually in jail.

I was talking back and getting sassy because I feel like that would just be me if I was in jail.

What school as they bring crazy scenarios to life, like there is a rebel that’s locked up with us and she’s trying to escape. So she comes around and asks who wants to escape with her and gives us a plan.

All while you have the warden and other security guards, walking around arguing with each other, people, yelling, people screaming.

Just be ready to improv, and they are absolutely ready for you.

If you want to drink, you will have to “sneak ink your sealed bottle and the bartenders will make drinks for you, there is no bar. You will get four rounds total, and while you’re in jail, it’s called chicken soup. Whatever’s left over from your bottle, will be given back to you. I guess that’s one way to ensure you going home lit.. 😂

Great experience but there were lots of gaps where nothing really happened. The actors were fantastic but there needed to be more going on in between. You need to bring your own bottle of sealed alcohol and I presumed you would have to try harder to smuggle in your alcohol. The cocktails they make you are fantastic and delicious. It would have been good to have more than four drinks or a game to get access to additional drinks. It would be more fun to make it harder to break out of prison at the end. Despite it being good fun, it did feel like it was a lot of money for what you get. I would recommend going in groups of 6 so you can all sit together in a cell and make it a fun group experience.

I definitely recommend this rooftop. It has a very modern and beautiful interior. Drinks are good and The alcohol is strong. Staff are extremely welcoming, friendly and kind. Our waiter recommended us what to drink based on our preferred flavours. One of our drinks came with a mini ice cream!

Not only the food choices are limited, the view is also limited compared to other roof bars in the world. There is only one corner of the outdoor area that can see St. Paul, the majority of the outdoor areas you are just facing ugly buildings. Food wise is so so, except for the potatoes with octopus which is quite good. Cocktails wise was a bit too sweet for our taste and just so so in general, although the presentation looks good. Service was friendly but slow. Price wise is quite pricey for its quality. Music was also so so in this place.

I had a blast in Florattica! My best friends have surprised me with a birthday brunch. Roberto, the manager was ever so kind to help us with our belongings. He welcomed us with a glass of bubbly and a big smile. The staff was ever so kind, we had fantastic waiters who served delicious food and bartenders were serving top-notch cocktails! The atmosphere in Florattica is amazing, you get that Dolce Vita vibes! I’m definitely coming back! - Well I did 😉 and got welcomed with a delicious glass of champagne 🥂🍾

Big thank you to Roberto, Michael, Juan and the lovely waitress from Nepal, you have made the end of my birthday weekend more memorable with your hospitality! 🎊🥰

Lovely seating area. Staff were polite and helpful. Drinks on the other hand were quite disappointing. Looked very different in real life compared to the menu, which I understand is meant to look artistic however it is also quite misleading. Shown photos below as an example. My boyfriend described them as tasting like acid reflux. If you favour good drinks over atmosphere I wouldn’t recommend going here.

The place is beautiful and have amazing drinks. Kabita helped us to choose the best drink according our taste and she 100% nailed it! The food was also VERY good! I was there for my husband birthday and they were above and beyond on making his day even better. We definitely recommend it.

places.name: STEREO Covent Garden
places.vicinity: Jubilee Market Hall, 35 The Piazza, London

reviews.text: A large, basement bar in Central London, right next to Covent Garden. I went there on a Saturday evening, all the tables were booked, but they let us in as there was still plenty of space around the bar. I had 2 cocktails, reasonably priced. There was live music, which added to the vibes of the place.

Loved the vibe here!! Great music, nice crowd, and an aesthetic atmosphere. The cocktails were solid, and the staff were lovely. Perfect spot for a fun night without it feeling too hectic! Definitely recommend going during the live performances regardless of the event🫶🏻

Truly an unforgettable experience. We’re here to have a meal before the theatre and what an absolutely treat and hidden gem. The space itself is dimlit and beautifully curated, the music not too loud so you can have a nice conversation without screaming at each other.

Then the food, wow what a surprise, I’d recommend the salmon fish and the tacos 🥹🥹 10/10!!

There’s happy hour until 8.30pm so that’s always a plus.

The best bit though would be the chef coming out and speaking with us - we felt so honoured for that. So thanks to chef James!

The service was also 10/10!

Anywho, would highly recommend, we’ll definitely be back!!

We came for Dinner. And the staff were amzingly attentive and so funny and fun.
We managed to even have interaction with the chef James. Such amazing food and would recommend coming here. We will be back especially as there is a live band and DJ's later. Thank you so much for the hospitality the whole team

Only had one drink but it is absolutely extortionate. Drinks are far too expensive for what they are - too much ice and barely any actual liquid. Took two sips to drink the cocktail and was left a bit underwhelmed. The bar itself has wonderful decor but the lighting was so dark and turned down you couldn’t even see anything else. Came on a Thursday so I didn’t expect it to be so busy but was more of a nightclub than a bar. Also was advertised bands would be playing and nobody was on. Just a DJ playing some average club songs.

However, I would like to come back on a Saturday when an event is on and hopefully try the food and see what the vibe is like from there on.
Bvumai was an amazing bartender. Tailored to my preferences when even I didn't know what I wanted on the menu. Strongly recommend either the Long island ice tea or the maple old fashioned!!

Roman was absolutely amazing! From the moment we arrived, he was super welcoming, friendly, and attentive. He made sure our drinks were perfect and checked in on us throughout the night, even though the bar was really busy. His energy and customer service honestly made the experience so much better — you can tell he genuinely cares about guests having a great time. Huge thanks to Roman for making the night unforgettable!

I had an extremely upsetting and unacceptable experience at Simon’s Bar near Oxford Circus. After buying a drink at the bar, I was abruptly taken outside by security without any explanation. They accused me of being intoxicated without any proper assessment or reason.
What followed was even more concerning. My coat was withheld for over 30 minutes, and I was left waiting outside in very cold weather without any assistance. When I requested my coat, staff were dismissive and unhelpful. The manager and one of the security guards were particularly rude and unprofessional. I began to feel physically unwell due to the cold. It was another guest who eventually showed some basic human decency and gave me a coat while my friend was inside trying to retrieve mine. This experience was not only unprofessional but inhumane. I’ve never been treated with such disrespect in any venue. I would strongly advise others to think twice before going here — this is not how paying customers should be treated.

What can I say about Holleigh and Ali that hasn't already been said. Sensational service. Maybe the greatest of all time. People will sing songs of these girls and what they did for our evening. Truly unparalleled.

If I had to describe the service in one word :

I couldn't x

Came into Simmons for a quick drink with my girls, from the moment we got in, Ali greeted us at the bar with excellent service. She was joking around, bubbly and all round happy. She also made very delicious drinks. Couldn’t be happier with the service but also how welcome she made us feel.

places.name: Opium Cocktail Bar - Soho
places.editorial_summary: Classic 'fancy drinks', large sharing brews and seasonal cocktails with dim sum in simple open bar.

reviews.text: We loved this bar!  The atmosphere was great, the drinks were tasty and the presentation was awesome!  The staff was totally top notch and really made us feel welcome.  Adam, Gordon, Papi OYP, Prince and Harold really worked well together and helped make it a special night.  As Americans on vacation, it was the perfect way to spend our last night in London!
Great cocktail bar with dim sum. The heavy on the door wasn't the warmest welcome but the team inside were great. Highly recommend the old fashioned and fish and fennel dimsum

⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️
I can’t say enough great things about Harry, the security guard at Opium Cocktail Bar. From the moment you arrive, Harry makes you feel both welcome and safe. He has that perfect balance of professionalism and warmth — greeting guests with a smile while ensuring everything runs smoothly.

What really stands out is how attentive and respectful he is. He treats everyone with kindness and patience, handling situations calmly and confidently. You can tell he genuinely cares about people having a good time without any worries. His presence alone creates a comfortable atmosphere, and it’s clear he takes pride in his work.

Harry isn’t just “security” — he’s part of what makes the Opium experience so enjoyable. His approachability, professionalism, and reassuring demeanor go above and beyond. A true credit to the venue!

Really cool speak easy, it was pretty busy so not much interaction with staff which is fine, I get it they’re working their butts off and it was late. However we still had a great time. Cocktails were fantastic and will definitely be back

Been here twice, this place had a cool concept with cool drinks but the bouncer is a little weird and the music is so loud and it’s very loud’! Very lovely service and the drinks are super cool. But couldn’t stay for more than an hour

places.name: The Cocktail Club - Cocktail Bar near Mansion House
places.formatted_address: 78 Queen Victoria St, Mansion House St, London EC4N 4SJ, UK
places.vicinity: York House, 78 Queen Victoria St, Mansion House St, London

html_attributions: The Cocktail Club - Cocktail Bar near Mansion House
The Cocktail Club - Cocktail Bar near Mansion House

reviews.text:
I wholeheartedly believe this is one of the greatest places in London.

The entire crew are amazing — friendly, professional, and always make you feel welcome. Their energy creates such a great vibe, and you can tell they genuinely care about the experience.

The music is always great- you can ask to add whatever song you wish to the queue. The staff will often join in, singing and dancing behind the bar, creating an even better atmosphere.

The staff, especially Milena, have always made me feel like part of the family, mixing up the tastiest drinks and making sure I have the best time.

Whether you are with friends or just grabbing a drink alone, this is the place to go to. Highly recommend 5/5.

Very cool looking underground bar.
The cocktails were all really good, we enjoyed them a lot. The prices are (typical for London) very high, we paid around 60 pounds for 4 quite small cocktails.

We went for my friends 22nd birthday and had an amazing night, the happy hour is such a great deal, we had most the cocktails on the menu and they are all so good.
The staff as also all super friendly which makes all the difference I believe!

This is a great alternative dive bar within walking distance of St. Paul's. The 6 of us hit this place for a vibrant time. We won over the bartender with DJ TMoss spinning the jams. Soon we had the place hopping until 2!
Great cocktails, great service, great atmosphere. Their selection of spirits was incredible. Thank you to Wilson for the best amaretto sour I ever tasted. We will definitely come back again.

places.name: Disrepute - Cocktail Bar in Soho
places.formatted_address: 4 Kingly Ct, Carnaby, London W1F 9RS, UK
places.editorial_summary: Trendy, dimly lit basement bar with an old-timey feel & leather booths serving creative cocktails.

reviews.text:
Had an amazing night at Disrepute! Mateo gave us the warmest welcome, Jake was a fantastic host, and Lua and David absolutely crushed it behind the bar. The cocktails were next level — we tried the whole drink menu (designed & illustrated by GiGi) and we loved every single drink. Great vibes, incredible staff, and some of the best cocktails in London. Can’t wait to come back! 🍸
The playlist is also great 🎶

Go here! The service, team, drinks, ambience, and overall vibes are always on point. The new menu is a fantastic and fun adventure, and the classics are always perfectly balanced.

This bar is great because you step outside of the chaos in London for a brief moment into a place where you can relax and have great conversations, drinks, with nice music in the background. One of my favourite cozy speakeasy’s in London that does it right.

Luca and Aidan are always making phenomenal drinks, Jake, Lio, and Acene are always providing wonderful service, with Lua and David ensuring everything runs smoothly throughout the night.

Absolutely go here if you have the chance!

Personal favourite drink on the new Menu: Domination (don’t forget to open the scroll on the bow!)
One of the best cocktail places I've been. The mixologists know flavour and balance. Great service. Will be back. Could do with making some of the stools taller though 😄

Was fortunate to stumble upon this amazing speakeasy after my birthday dinner and I have to say, the cocktails were one of the best I've ever had I London. Bar was also not overcrowded which was a huge plus! Loved the bar snacks too, especially the crispy corn.

Not cheap bur with this level of excellence, you get what you pay for. I’d argue the best cocktail menu on Earth, the most attentive staff, and a high-end ambiance rare anywhere. Could not recommend it more. Support your local artisans.

places.name: Pulse Bar London
places.formatted_address: 18 New Globe Walk, London SE1 9DR, UK

reviews.text:
We had a fantastic time at Pulse Bar for our recent work event! From the moment we arrived, the service was top-notch – super friendly and attentive, which really set the tone for the night. The owner is amazing – warm, welcoming, and clearly passionate about making sure everyone has a great experience.
We had a blast playing beer pong, shuffleboard, and darts – such a fun setup that really brought the us together. The atmosphere was lively without being overwhelming, and it’s clear that a lot of thought has gone into creating a space where people can relax and enjoy themselves.
The drinks menu is extensive and genuinely impressive, with something for everyone – from cocktails to craft beers. The food was also spot on – tasty, well-presented, and ideal for sharing during a social night like this.
All in all, Pulse Bar ticked every box. The service, food, games, and overall vibe were exactly what we were looking for, and we’ll definitely be coming back. A brilliant venue for team events or just a fun night out!

I really enjoy coming to this bar when I go out, the drinks and the food is very nice. I love playing darts. My husband and my son enjoy playing pool. It's fairly priced, we went during happy hours so it was cheap. The staff is so lovely, they are welcoming and friendly. The place is kept clean and the atmosphere is great. They show football on the screens. I really recommend this place

Had one of the best sandwiches of my life with the best atmosphere. The bar was inviting and the owner was awesome. On top of that they had one of the sweetest dogs I have ever met. If I lived in London I would go all the time. Perfect for dinner or a night out on the town. The bar has some of the nicest beer pong tables I have ever seen. They are custom made with led lighting. Thanks to them for such an inviting experience.

Had an amazing night at Pulse Bar London Bridge! Michelle was an incredible bartender, friendly and made great drinks. Nico, the owner, was super welcoming. And the best part? Meeting Hermes, the adorable bar dog! Great vibes all around , can’t wait to go back.

Go for the owner’s crazy Italian energy and stay for the food, drinks and games. Pulse bar is designed for groups of friends to hang out and get competitive - beer pong, darts, pool and more. The burgers are delicious and beers are cold. Nothing fancy - just right. Make a date.

This is an exceptional bar with an amazing theme and outstanding cocktails.
This is a DESTINATION, not just someplace to drink.
The staff is knowledgeable and play their part well without feeling like they are playing a part.
Fun loving, whimsical yet serious.
Steampunk before it was cool.

The Emerald Enchantress, a limited edition Halloween menu item, was absolutely divine.

Do you LOVE matcha? This enchantress sings beautiful earthy notes, kissed by vanilla winds.

I don’t regret stopping here on a whim.. this IS a cocktail to go out of your way for.

Super interesting experience. We walked in and loved the entrance, with the ball that goes down with you, and the bar had such an interesting interior.

I thought the train car was very cute and really enjoyed the different decorative touches around the bar!

However, I must say that the drinks were all quite subpar. Very fun, especially the camel cocktail, but just not very good. You’re definitely paying for the experience.

Had my birthday here in January and it was an amazing experience. The whole place feels like stepping into an old-school explorer’s lounge, super cool decor, detailed and immersive.

Cocktails were 🔥, staff was on point, and the vibe was just fun and different. Definitely not your average bar. Perfect spot if you’re celebrating something or just want a night out with a bit of character. Would 100% come back.

A hidden gem that is probably something of a public secret. Totally styled after 80 Days Around the World. This is a good place to go to for a glass of whisky.

We did not have the time to taste the food, but we tasted the atmosphere and decided it was great. Everything is perfectly executed into the tiniest details. That basically means that even the details of the details are great.

places.name: Bar Soho
places.formatted_address: 23-25 Old Compton St, London W1D 5JL, UK
places.editorial_summary: Cocktail bar with mirrored walls and a fairground horse, or decadent 'boudoir' with baths for seats.

reviews.text: Ryan (lead bartender) was so cordial and inviting and was just what we were looking for after a long day walking and touring the city.  Great service. Great recommendations and prob the best drinks (cocktails) we’ve had this trip.  Well done and cheers to him!

It’s a fat bar and open during the day when we popped in for drinks and light bites. Basically a club so we didn’t get the night time vibe. Service was good and the bar snacks we ordered tasty and well prepared. Next time we’ll come for the night life for sure!

Such a fun venue! Went in for drinks & pizza after work and had a fabulous evening. Staff are friendly, atmosphere is fun and bouncy - even during the more chill hours. Air con was a massive plus in the heat 🤙🏻 Will be back again soon!

I had a terrible experience at Bar Soho. My two friends and I walked in randomly just to have a drink and relax. At one point, due to a simple misunderstanding, a coat was moved along with my friend’s without us realising. The manager immediately accused us of theft and called the police.

I felt completely humiliated and intimidated. We were treated like criminals when we had absolutely no bad intentions, just three gay young guys out trying to enjoy an evening. The manager made no effort to understand the situation and, even after it was clear it was a misunderstanding, we didn’t receive so much as an apology.

To make matters worse, the service was appalling from the start. The bartender gave us wine in a dirty glass, and the general hygiene of the place was disgusting. We were planning to stay only a few minutes anyway, but this situation made it a nightmare.

The only people who treated us with dignity were the police officers who, frankly, had their time wasted by a completely unprofessional and unprepared manager.

I will never return to this place and wouldn’t recommend it to anyone. Poor service, disrespectful staff, and a total lack of customer care. Avoid it, you never know when you might get caught up in something absurd like we did.

came very spur of the moment on a wednesday, had some wings for 40p each and they were incredible and GLUTEN FREE! the staff were super helpful with my allergy and told me they even have a separate fryer for gluten free food! the mango wings were my favourite but the peri peri are super delicious too. also the only happy hour in london i've found that you can have 2 pints for less than £10. couldn't recommend more!

places.name: A Bar with Shapes for a Name
places.formatted_address: 232 Kingsland Rd, Whitmore Estate, London E2 8AX, UK

reviews.text:
A must-visit for anyone serious about cocktails. This minimalist, Bauhaus-inspired bar takes craftsmanship to the next level - from precise temperature control with thermometers to custom ice and pre-batching techniques from their own production lab.

Despite their pre-batch focus, there's real creativity and passion behind each drink. The menu includes some truly inventive ideas, and when we asked for something off-menu, they delivered a thoughtful and well-balanced twist. Staff were professional yet warm, with lovely personal touches that elevated the experience.

Highly refined, technically impressive, and quietly playful - one of the best bar experiences we’ve had.

A great time at a super unique bar! My husband & I came here on our last night in London and I am so glad we did.

Firstly, the bar was super communicative— I emailed them to ask about updating our reservation last minute and they responded within 15 minutes.

The drinks were phenomenal. We started with the habanero and the osmanthus— both had striking flavor profiles and even more interesting creation processes. We got the kazimir and atlas for our second round — perfectly balanced and wholly unique.

The service was spectacular— Brian, Juan, and Juliette were so friendly and knowledgeable. They answered all of our questions and gave personalized recommendations to what we should try on the menu.

If we ever find ourselves back in London, this spot will definitely be on list to return to.

Lovely staff and really good cocktails. Not too sweet, perfectly balanced. All of them have really interesting inspirations, as sell, if you ask the staff. But even if not, it is a great place for some drinks.

As lovers of the Bauhaus school and movement we were excited to try a bar inspired by it.
We didn’t have reservations and came late after dinner to explore and be amused .
We got seated at the bar downstairs - the workshop.
The amazing Juna, the brilliant mixologist explained the experimental ways the team explores how to achieve each drinks .
We are ordered assignment : extraction which was an interesting dive into extraction of aroma and taste which was served as a slushy (a most interesting one) and osmanthus. Here I can stop - cause I know the menu will change and I know I can try to describe the tastes and aroma . But the truth is that the process and the result are so playful, interesting and unique that it’s really about coming and experiencing this for yourself .

Such a fun and rewarding place . And I will add as someone that drinks very little - I asked for my second to be an N/A and the delightful Juna created a sort of spritzer with the essence of Palo Santo - it was remarkable. It had the aroma of the sacred tree but was lovely and refreshing .

Love this place - Highly recommended!

Just drinks? More like just magic.
My first visit to A Bar with Shapes for a Name was nothing short of exceptional. With only seven meticulously curated house cocktails on the menu, each one is clearly crafted with purpose and I chose the one with the Japanese name, made with Toki Whisky, Palo Santo, butter, and golden syrup.

The experience? Transformative.
This cocktail didn’t just taste good — it awakened my palate in layers. First came the smooth, smoky warmth of the whisky, followed by a buttery richness and a final golden finish that lingered like a memory. It was three layers deep in flavour, each one more intriguing than the last.

The service? Impeccable.
The staff shared deep knowledge about the ingredients and the story behind the drink and that attention to detail really set the tone.

This one cocktail sparked something in me… it inspired the direction for my own upcoming product: Icosa Moringa Water Blends a unique, moringa-infused beverage launching soon.

Thank you for the unforgettable inspiration. I’ll definitely be back and next time, I’m bringing friends.

The TOMATO - possibly the best cocktail I’ve ever had. Starts savoury in the mouth- like the scent of a really crisp cherry tomato. Then it transitions thru the sweetness of a cherry tomato and ends in raspberry. Still an earthier fruit so follows the tomato well but goes from savoury sweet beautifully.
Cocktail bar is inspired by Indian flavours, sweet and savoury, done so well. Curry flavours with spirits, Indian salad flavours done in a light cocktail ect. Also rec the Cucucumber and Nimbu!! Super friendly and chatty staff too

Arrived just after 6 PM about a 15 minute wait to get in. Well worth the wait, the cocktails were fantastic and the bartender is definitely put pride into their work. The Kokum was the pride of the show. Most unique, slight pepper, but delicious all around.

This super cool speakeasy bar, located in the heart of London, offers an incredible cocktail experience. The attention to detail in crafting each drink is remarkable, and the design is equally impressive. While it may be a bit pricey, the experience is definitely worth it. If you’re a cocktail enthusiast, this place is a must-visit!

Love the Indian inspired cocktails with the hip hop music vibes!  Like I was truly impressed and happy I got a chance to visit on my recent trip to London!  The creativity of the menu and the vibes at Somo were first class!  It’s a must visit on any trip to London.
One of the best cocktail bars I’ve been to in London. Very reasonably priced and well-made with great strength. Amazing service and atmosphere.

places.name: Lyaness
places.vicinity: Sea Containers House, 20 Upper Ground, London
places.editorial_summary: Swanky cocktail bar with a marble bar and river views, in a hotel setting.

reviews.text: A incredibly beautiful cocktail bar with beautiful drinks crafted with an immersive storyline. Whilst a bit pricy, the service is impeccable and the overall experience is worth it for a nice treat. I tried the Baloo-Za and Cosmo Salad, both were wonderful with a fruity taste. I also tried the Vantapink Gimlink, rather strong but a must try in my opinion. There is a special menu for vegans, I would recommend the blistered peppers and aubergine dip as they pair wonderfully with the drinks.

Wow, amazing cocktail creations and a lovely view of river Thames. The cocktail creations are described in detail in the menu, which helps to find something matching your taste and preferences.
Beside the cocktails the food is excellent! Try the tacos - some of the most amazing tacos I ever had in my life!

Some of the best cocktails available in London. Set on Sea Containers. Beautiful hotel. Really innovative choices, not seen anywhere else. Using unusual unique muxes, cornflake infusion did instance. Excellent DJ and right by the Thames. Well worth a visit

First time visiting…. LOVED It! The service was impeccable! The devote music and atmosphere was chilled and sophisticated.
Had snacks… well presented and tasty!
Seating was comfortable and had a great view on the the Thames.
Champagne ( we had 3 bottles) was crisp and cool.
Will definitely visit again!

Service was amazing, particularly Lockie. The drinks are perfect for a particular type of person. Initially what I got was very light and delicate. Not to my tastes but it did say it was light on the menu. They then didn't have the ingredients for the main drink I wanted to try (it happens) so I got what they listed as their second heaviest cocktail. It was incredibly sweet and I couldn't taste most of the ingredients.

This bar is great for a particular type of person, but if that's not you then you're out of luck. If you want very light and delicate cocktails with absolutely no alcohol taste, you'll really enjoy this place, but it just wasn't for me personally.

places.name: Bussey Rooftop Bar
places.formatted_address: Roof B, Bussey Building, 133 Rye Ln, London SE15 4ST, UK
places.vicinity: Roof B, Bussey Building, 133 Rye Ln, London
places.editorial_summary: Cozy rooftop bar with 360-degree views of London serving cocktails & beers, plus burgers & chips.

reviews.text:
After failing to get into another nearby rooftop bar, we ended up at Bussey Rooftop instead. It’s on the 5th floor of the building, but getting up there was a bit of a mission. The lift is this old industrial type that felt a bit sketchy, and you need a code to access the top floor, otherwise it only stops at the 4th. If the weather’s not too hot, I’d actually recommend just taking the stairs. There aren’t many stairs in between floors, and it’s probably quicker.

Once up there, the space itself is okay but a bit underwhelming. The menu is super limited, with only a handful of drink options. Ordering is easy with a QR code at the table, though.

The biggest letdown was the atmosphere. The whole place smelled a bit like rubbish and it was so warm and muggy. We came up hoping for a bit of a breeze and fresh air, but the space is mostly walled in and there are no fans, so it just traps the heat.

Definitely not the rooftop escape we were hoping for.
Great views, music and decor! Cocktails weren’t amazing but there were a range of spirits. Would probably return if in the area.

Can't go wrong with in made Pizzas and great beer selections. Roof top views and great temperature with easybup and down windows. Great, happy team and a DJ spinning some great beats!
Great for groups or nice intimate time too.
Hopefully the lift is working otherwise the stairs are a great way to earn that first beer!

Great selection of Alcohol free options available too.
SO gorgeous! Such a lovely vibe and great music. We went after the outdoor cinema which is right next door

Had a the most incredible private party at Bussey Rooftop Bar. The events team were so attentive in the build up, making sure every detail was covered and the bar team on the day could not have been more friendly and made the whole event run effortlessly smoothly. The views and set up inside are just magical, such a great place for a party! Thanks to Nick, Sasha-Sky, Colin and the rest of the team!

places.name: Nine Lives
places.editorial_summary: Modern house cocktails & craft beer poured in a stylish, greenery-lined space with a tropical vibe.

reviews.text:
I've been here a few times now for cocktails and have  loved each time. Friday and Saturday seem their busiest and loudest nights but I've been on a Wednesday and it's quieter but still a very great atmosphere.

Olivia was AMAZING. Very friendly and knowledgeable about menu items. My friend ordered tacos and really enjoyed but the cocktails and service keep me coming back!

Lovely cocktail bar with a fab atmosphere in a really cool spot underground and just outside London Bridge station.
I'm not a big drinker but I had heard about the food so that's primarily what we went for but I did also try the 'Mello' cocktail and it was really good, surprised by how well the cucumber flavour came through!
The mango ceviche was incredible, as was the pork, no-fish baja tacos, and beef tacos - I would 100% go back for the food alone!
The service was really good, the only negative was we were slightly rushed at the end of the meal because we were close to our 2 hour allocation, and they were super busy - but that bodes well for them if they're in constant demand so I can't really complain!

We were in last night for some food & drinks and from the get-go we loved it. Will and the guys at the front door were fantastic, so friendly and a great laugh! Downstairs decor was beautiful and created a great vibe too. Combine the delicious cocktails and food with the great service from Matin and our night was brill! Thank you for such a great evening🫶🏻

Best Baja fish tacos I’ve had in London. The Paloma sea bream ceviche was also delicious. Beef barbacoa was also super tasty.
We started with a cocktail outside, then moved inside - 2 completely different atmospheres which was nice! Inside you step into a dim light more DJ vibe space. Food and drinks were brought quite quickly, lovely waiters, you just need to catch their attention though.
Margarita was really nice and I also enjoyed a flight of 3 different mezcal to taste.

Had a celebratory drinks/dinner here and I’m so glad we chose this spot! The cocktails were amazing (had probably the best spicy margarita I’ve had in London) and the food was really tasty, especially the baja tacos and the chicharrón
Recommend going on Tuesday as a selection of tacos are reduced to £3 each!

I will surely be back :)

places.name: Be At One - Spitalfields
places.editorial_summary: Lively chain bar that serves sweet, sour and spicy cocktails, and offers mixing masterclasses.

reviews.text: Thanks for the best drinks over here. Great service by the team . I would love to visit again here ❤️ So much love .

Great atmosphere, music and customer service was 10/10. Kadir was serving us and the drinks were strong and great tasting. Would defo recommend coming here in the summer.
2 for 1 was really good deal.

Shaun was amazing!
Very warm and friendly
Plus he made fab drinks really really quick.
Deffo recommend the chilli mango margaritas for £5 on happy hour
Just had the most wonderful cocktails from Libor & Kadir, amazing service and the cocktails were delicious! we just finished a gig watching Goldie. What a way to end the night thank you gentlemen. Xx
Always a fun place to hang out! The music is for everyone and the crowd is always so lovely. Livor and  Kadir served us great cocktails and we are now regulars at this point! Can’t wait to be back.

places.name: The Rooftop
places.formatted_address: 7th Floor, 2 Spring Gardens, London SW1A 2TS, UK
places.editorial_summary: Trafalgar Hotel's smart rooftop bar offers cocktails and Nelson's Column views, plus private hire.

reviews.text:
We stayed at the hotel and were told to just to upstairs to the rooftop at any time and we’d be accommodated as guests and Platinum Honors members. We were turned away by the young hostess. By some “miracle” just as we were about to get the elevator to go back to our room a table mysteriously appeared. I’d like to say that that’s never happened to us before but I know better.

Once we got up there, it was a decent enough experience. The food was passable and not terribly expensive by London standards.  The drinks were good. The service was a touch spotty. I almost gave three stars, but it’s more of a 2 1/2.  The best views are at the bar area and we were in a place where the view was okay, but not spectacular compared to other places we’ve been to.  We nevertheless had a good enough time.

We love the hotel, so I’m sure we’ll be back.  And perhaps we’ll have a better experience next time. This one was not awful, but it also wasn’t something to write home about. I’m only writing about it here. Hopefully we’ll be able to update this with a higher review come winter.

Myself and my friend got some small plates to share. The food tasted good, but considering how extortionate the price was and how absolutely minuscule the portion was, I was not impressed. It wasn’t the best thing I’ve ever had, and it would’ve had to have been to make up for the price and lack of it.
The same applies to the cocktails- they tasted fine but £18!!! And in fun size glasses!! I’ve had far better tasting cocktails in larger sizes and at much cheaper costs. Overall, I wasn’t too impressed.

To top it all off, we had to pay a £10+ service charge; our waiter didn’t even get us a single moment to deny doing so, which I thought was extremely cheeky.

The atmosphere was lovely nonetheless.

Disappointing Experience - Not Worth the Hype

I was hoping for a relaxed, enjoyable evening, but it didn’t deliver. The 21+ rule after 5:00 pm felt unnecessary and off-putting-like we’d somehow turn into troublemakers after 5:00pm.

The view was nice, but that was the only real highlight. Our table and glasses were sticky, and the food came out cold.

Staff were polite but overly pushy, and the whole thing felt rushed - like they just wanted us out as quickly as possible to seat the next group.

I had specifically noted in the booking that it was for a birthday surprise, but clearly no one had read it.

There was no mention or acknowledgment of the occasion, which was really disappointing given the context.

The cocktails tasted nothing like described on the menu more like a random mix of ingredients thrown together.

When we asked to have the optional service charge removed, we were questioned about it, which felt awkward especially considering the cold food and lack of attention to the booking details.

Overall, it felt more like a rushed production line than a place to enjoy a special night out. Nice view, but not much else. I wouldn’t go back or recommend it.

The rooftop is really beautiful and the view is great. My husband and I booked the terrace, the weather was very cold so we asked if there was a table inside and they kindly accomodated our request without any problems. The menu is pretty much spicy and mexican, since I do not like spicy food I asked a plain hamburger and the waiter (Raj) checked with the chef to make sure there was no trace of it in my dish. I really appreciated the attention and professionalism. I reccomend this place for a pleasant evening in a central location of the city.

Nice cocktails, but nothing special for the price. Haven’t tried food. You are paying for the view. Booked table for 4 in advance. Unfortunately, got one right behind the speaker, so was hard to talk.

places.name: Wagtail
places.formatted_address: 68 King William St, London EC4N 7HR, UK
places.vicinity: HOUSE OF FRASER, Underground Ltd, 68 King William St, London
places.editorial_summary: Upscale locale with terraces & panoramic views of London from the top of a 1920s building.

reviews.text:
Been here for drinks a couple times after work and on the weekends. The drinks are GOODDDD 10/10. Recommend a pina colada, it banged differently! All the cocktails look really nice.

The service was slightly slow when I last went, and we took the service charge off. The staff didn’t really seem too bothered about taking it off which made it seem a bit weird. It wasn’t busy and it took 15/20 mins for 4 drinks to come. Only disappointing thing about this place to be honest.

Also, sometimes they serve the drinks in glass and then other times they serve it in plastic cups!!!

Views are amazing! Worth a trip if you love cocktails and really want to some stunning views of the city.

Amazing views and decent prices. We visited on a Monday evening, so it wasn't crowded. The waiter was really helpful and had a good knowledge of wines. The fact that it wasn't busy made our visit really relaxing. Would definitely recommend.

We had a fantastic time starting our day with vermouth and cocktails followed by the chef’s incredible menu. Denise was absolutely fantastic in explaining (bit of a complicated) menu. The vibe is amazing and I must also praise the music list. Overall worth every penny!

The food was fine. Steak was tasty, some main dishes were the size of the brunch portions, though we were told they were main course size. Champagne 🍾 was flowin,  and cocktails 🍸 were perfect. We could not dine in the sun but overall it was a pleasant experience and we would returned knowing the food menu better. Staff was were attentive and friendly.
Roof top bar with a fantastic view. Very accommodating  servers. You can see The Shard and see Tower Bridge from the roof top. It was a lovely evening.

places.name: London Bridge Rooftop Bar
places.formatted_address: Colechurch House, Bridge Walk, London SE1 2SX, UK
places.editorial_summary: Vibrant open-air bar on a rooftop terrace offering an extensive drinks menu & light fare.

reviews.text: Great vibe, food was amazing. Tried to extend our 2 hour booking but sadly were told no. Would come back next time we’re in London. A great time was had.

We got served by Alex who was awesome and then another Alex came and sang happy birthday to my friend which was also awesome and unexpected. This is the place to be if you are in London bridge. Excellent beer and wine selection. Amazing atmosphere and super nice staff..

It was okay, the atmosphere is what made the experience for me. It was busy and the music was good. Waiting times were good, I went around 6-7pm. The stairs weren’t that bad on the way up to the rooftop; but I can imagine it would be a lot harder coming down when you’re drunk. I liked the food, but this place isn’t something that you come to eat if you get me. The staff were friendly but as a small con; the seating area wasn’t good where I sat, it was quite cramped. Overall I would say 3.5

I was amazed when I was shown upstairs to my table…The panoramic view of London is unreal as well as the venue itself.The staff are super friendly and accommodating to your needs,I had Bebe show me to my table she was so lovely and made sure I had everything I needed. The drinks were perfect they were just as good as they looked,as well as the food being tasty and quick service so it was still hot.Overall my experience was 10/10 I will definitely be coming back with friends very soon :)
Lovely place to be and enjoy , good vibes , good service , lovely cocktails , 🍹 lovey staff , only thing your have to climb the mountain which is good 👍. I loved my time here , highly recommend

places.name: Mercer Roof Terrace
places.editorial_summary: Chic rooftop venue for creative local eats & drinks, plus views of The Shard & St. Paul's Cathedral.

reviews.text:
The food & service was brilliant. We came for my mum’s 60th birthday lunch and the whole experience was perfect.
Great views and a quiet atmosphere (we came on a Thursday)
We thoroughly enjoyed the food and the cocktails were also great!

Beautiful quiet and off the busy roads restaurant-cum-hotel. Close to station. The restaurant is on the rooftop terrace and offers sitting inside or outside.
While it's beautiful, there's something missing to add to the magic of a rooftop dining experience.
The service and staff were good but it doesn't quite hit the 5 star.

Mercer roof top terrace boasts a fantastic location with stunning views over St. Paul’s Cathedral. The atmosphere is chic yet relaxed, perfect for any occasion. Service was impeccable—attentive and friendly throughout. The food was a highlight: beautifully presented surf and turf, absolutely delicious desserts.Highly recommended!

Without a reservation, luckily, on a Monday, we managed to get a table. We ordered drinks, and mine came wrong, so they had to redo it. Then the main courses were served. Although delicious (beautiful flavours), my friend found a hair in her food, so it was replaced. I ordered lamb, and halfway through, I found a hair! The waitress was very embarrassed and apologetic. They removed the lamb from the bill and offered a complimentary drink for her risotto. A nice gesture, but the evening was quite spoilt by the overall experience.
Loved the ambiance of this place, perfect for summer vibes. The food was surprisingly nice. I will come back again.

places.name: Madison
places.formatted_address: Rooftop Terrace One, New Change, London EC4M 9AF, UK
places.vicinity: Rooftop Terrace One, New Change, St Paul’s, London
places.editorial_summary: Rooftop, 6th-floor bar and tapas restaurant, with hand-blown glass chandeliers and large terrace.

reviews.text:
We had a wonderful dinner at the Madison. The views of Saint Paul’s and the London Eye can’t be beat on this rooftop restaurant. We particularly enjoyed the shrimp rigatoni, green goddess salad, and bread with Brie. Both the skillet cookie and chocolate sea salt brownie were chocolatey and delicious.

Overall we had a positive experience but a few minor remarks are that the service was a bit slower than we’d like, we had to ask for our bread, ask for the check, etc. Additionally while the salmon was flavorful we wished it came with hot sides rather than cold boiled eggs, lettuce and green beans. It seemed more like an afterthought.

Lovely rooftop bar and restaurant. It met our expectations but seating is limited near the bar so unless you are dining in you will be standing most of the time. The music is ok but I would say it's more catered for the older generation, not something you can dance or vibe to. The aesthetic and views on the other hand was beautiful and stunning but price of drinks definitely matched the clientele of the area.

Had a couple drinks here. It's got great views, very busy on a Thursday with loud DJ. Not much seating if just grabbing a drink at the bard but it's a bustling city vibe. Lovely view of St Paul's and the sunset is beautiful. The restaurant looked nice to chill and have a view without the crowd. Much quieter inside. Seating outside with the view but can't take your drinks with you!

The rooftop dining experience that gets delivered as is promised. The service is prompt and efficient. The food tastes great and it's presentation makes it even more appetizing.
The views, specially from the outdoor section are spectacular.
The gentleman receiving the guests as soon as you come up the lift is all in to ensure the first and last experience is as memorable as the food inside.

There is a lift to take you up to the restaurant. Whilst going up, St Paul's is in sight all the way.
The staff are friendly and helpful.
The food was delicious, as a party of 7 went for the set lunch on a Sunday and it was just divine. The only setback was the poached egg was unfortunately tasteless.
The views are amazing, needless to say and there is space to walk around outside on the roof terrace.
I recommend this restaurant.

places.name: Kitty Hawk
places.formatted_address: 8 St. Martin's Pl, London WC2N 4JH, UK
places.vicinity: Charing Cross Underground Shopping Concourse, 8 St. Martin's Pl, London

reviews.text: Julio was amazing, very welcoming vibe! We came here for coffee and they were great! Lovely view of Trafalgar Square. Would recommend this place for drinks, brunch or even just a coffee. Fabulous interior!

Came on Sunday for roast, to celebrate my birthday with a friend. We were warmly welcomed by the gentlemen who checked us in downstairs. When arriving, the other host was ready to lead us to the table. Great start.
The waiter serving us was on training I believe, and he was very attentive and nice. Also, the person who seemed to be the manager was very attentive and present on the floor.
The down was the food - firstly they didn’t have oysters which I was craving for but fine, I had a great cauliflower soup. However, the roast itself, although the veggies were good, the chicken was pretty dry. Additionally, we had the chocolate fondant which was pretty bland.
I was also slightly disappointed as I expected a special touch, maybe a candle or a happy birthday platter (anything really) as we had mentioned we were celebrating my birthday - which was nicely acknowledged on our arrival, by the host downstairs - but I guess that’s not the type of thing they do there (?)
Nice spot/view but the brunch was extortionate for what I got. £54 for a very average vegan burrata, tiny portion of pancakes and a beer. Wouldn’t return although staff were lovely and attentive

This is a great rooftop bar, lively with a DJ.
Adequate seating outside with views across Trafalgar Square but the majority of the seating is in the large comfortable internal space.
The staff were friendly, helpful and genuine.

The food was underwhelming. The fettuccine with the addition of what my companion thought would be whole prawns as the menu  stated grilled prawns turned out to be the addition of 8 tasteless peeled prawns. He would rather have had 3 whole grilled prawns than 8 tasteless ones for the additional £5 charge. The wagyu burger was small which was fine for me but some may find the portion size lacking. Presentation wise it sat very alone on its large plate with no garnish. The ‘triple’ cooked chips arrived anaemic looking and in need of further cooking to bring them up to what was promised. This was dealt with apologetically and promptly with a good outcome ie. delicious triple cooked chips. The green salad instead of being refreshing and crisp was as over dressed as Danny La Rue ….sodden.
Three glasses of wine and the bill came to £133….perhaps just a drink next time.

Kitty Hawk provided a fabulous evening out from start to finish. The staff were consistently friendly, attentive, and helpful, greeting us at the door with warm smiles and welcoming faces. The seating was comfortable, and the ambiance exuded a chic and modern vibe, complemented by ample space throughout the restaurant. The restrooms were immaculate, and the food lived up to the overall high standards.

If you plan to order the steak for two, I highly recommend starting with some starters, as the 600g may leave you wanting more if you are hungry. On a sweet note, the sticky toffee pudding was one of the best I’ve enjoyed in a long time it was perfectly moist and flavourful, resembling a loaf. (The plant based mains option though could be better).

Overall, it is a top choice for a memorable dining experience and great for
A date night.

places.name: Miradora Rooftop Restaurant Tequileria
places.formatted_address: above Assembly Hotel, 31 Charing Cross Rd, London WC2H 0LS, UK
places.vicinity: above Assembly Hotel, Alhambra House, 31 Charing Cross Rd, London
places.editorial_summary: Views over the city are on offer from this modern 10th floor restaurant filled with live plants.

reviews.text: This is a very fun restaurant! Great views of the city! The food was fine you’re mainly paying for the great views. All the workers were very friendly. It definitely can get pretty busy so you might want to book ahead.

We came for a Bottomless Brunch beforehand a theatre matinee. The menu is fixed price and it's clear before you arrive whats included so do take a look at the menu before booking to be sure it's right for you. We had  3 x soft tacos, rice and a dessert. All were great and quite filling. To drink, it was as much Prosecco and frozen margarita's as you fancy in the 2 hours.  The atmosphere is fun and loud. The views are great given it's a rooftop restaurant. Would recommend if you are looking for somewhere fun with friends especially if it's not all about the food and more about having a good time.

I had a really nice time here celebrating my friend’s graduation. First time experiencing a rooftop restaurant and was impressed. This was a nice intimate spot

We ordered a few large plates, though our chicken and potato dish wasn’t enough to share between 7 people. Food was lovely and flavourful.

Had a really lovely young waitress who served us.

£55 for bottomless sugary margaritas (with 0 alcohol in them) uncooked rice and burnt chocolate sauce....

Not happy.

I had 10 or 12 frozen margaritas, the waitress made sure she kept them coming. Even with minimal alcohol I would've been atleast a bit tipsy. Instead I had a lot of sugar. There's also a.prosecco option but that has sulphites and gives me a migraine.

The tacos were okay. Nothing to scream about.
The rice that accompanied them was undercooked and crunchy. You could cut it with your nail and see the white line in each grain. Rice isn't hard to get right.

And for dessert, the churros were nice and chewy but the sauce??? When you burn chocolate it almost tastes sour. I tried to salvage it by mixing the white chocolate with it but no. Just had the churros.

The view is nice but wouldn't come again.

Absolutely loved it!
I had an amazing experience at this rooftop Miradora restaurant. The atmosphere was vibrant and full of energy — perfect for a fun evening out.

The view over London was absolutely breathtaking, especially at sunset – definitely one of the highlights.

But what truly made the night special was the bar – the cocktails were outstanding! Every drink was beautifully crafted and full of flavour.

Huge compliments to the bartender Alex – not only were the cocktails delicious, but he was also incredibly friendly, professional and clearly passionate about his craft.

Highly recommended for anyone looking for great vibes, amazing views, and unforgettable drinks! 🌇🍸🌮

places.name: Circe's Rooftop Waterloo
places.formatted_address: Mercury House, 117 Waterloo Rd, London SE1 8UL, UK
places.vicinity: Mercury House, Rooftop Mercury House, 117 Waterloo Rd, London

reviews.text: Zohair was amazing ! Great and swift service. He gave great recommendations - will defo be back just for him !! The food was unreal. We ordered almost every dish and it came quickly and tasty. My fav was the prawns! It’s tapas but big portions in my opinion! Love it ! I myself don’t drink and the bartenders made some lovely alcohol-free options which I enjoyed. Very grateful. We stayed in the cute pods up top, great skyline view and warm too! Olly was a great help. Coming back asap! I’d be here everyday if it was summer🙏🏽🙏🏽💖
Great deals for Witching Hour on a Sunday afternoon. Good vibes, not too busy and good music. Friendly attentive staff (thanks Navya our lovely waitress) and great food/portion sizes and cocktails.

I chose this rooftop place to celebrate my birthday and I was so happy with the experience! We were a group of 10 and everyone loved the venue 🥳 We had such a nice celebration,  the Aperol Spritz was delicious and the appetizers were great too. Since it was my birthday, they even treated me to a free drink, which made me really happy 🥂 It’s self service place. The atmosphere is amazing, with warm colors that make you feel like you’re in a southern European café. Plus, it’s very close to the metro station. Definitely a place I’ll be coming back to 🥰
Zouhair and Steff were the best waiters, they were so attentive. Rory was an excellent bartender and Ollie was an all round legend. Honestly, we had the best time

Much more elevated experience than the previous offering at the same location. Lovely set up and lots of different areas. I think quite difficult for the staff working across things that are quite spread out but everyone was really friendly and helpful. The drinks and food are a bit on the pricey side (canned mocktail for almost £8) but worth it for the surroundings.

Perfect chilled rooftop for sunny evenings with friends.

places.name: Aviary
places.formatted_address: Royal London House, 22-25 Finsbury Square, London EC2A 1DX, UK
places.vicinity: Royal London House, 22-25 Finsbury Square, London
places.editorial_summary: Elevated seasonal dishes served in a stylish rooftop restaurant that has sweeping city views.

reviews.text: We came here on a Saturday evening and can say im surprised this place doesnt have solid 5 stars. Absolutely lovely place. The venue is very nice, decor is stylish but subtle. Views are amazing outside too. Staff were all very friendly and service was great. But the food, that was the best part. Really impressed with the flavours of both the mains we had, lamb and the pork. Even the side dishes were amazing! Fries and the potatoes. Eton mess was nice although the chocolate dessert was nicer I think. Cocktails were great flavour too. Obviously price is higher than some places here but id say its worth it considering the quality.

The Aviary proved to be a great place to meet up with old school friends for Sunday lunch - this place is quite the little gem! Waiting for my friends, I enjoyed a frisky picant0 mocktail on the roof terrace, soaking up the sunshine and the fabulous view. The manageress was very welcoming and attentive, and helpful with the wine selection. We shared a selection of starters, all nicely presented, substantial and delicious - especially the tuna crevice. For my main course I chose the Asian Summer salad - adding the pork belly as I thought a salad wouldn't be enough.In fact it was enormous - and extremely tasty! The vibe was chilled and we were able to have a good catch up over a really nice lunch in a restaurant with a 'wow' factor! All credit to the staff and chef for a great experience.

Good selection of drinks
The Montcalm hotel’s rooftop bar, good atmosphere and panoramic views of the city skyline. The seating strikes the perfect balance between comfort and style. Good selection of drinks.
Ahmed provided exceptional service throughout our visit, maintaining just the right level of attentiveness without being intrusive.

Unfortunately, I didn’t have a great experience at The Aviary. While the venue itself is stylish, the space was extremely crowded and noisy, making it hard to hear each other and enjoy the meal. The ambience felt more chaotic than relaxing.

I ordered the seafood pasta, but from the very first bite, the tomato sauce tasted unpleasantly acidic, so I had to send it back. I replaced it with the sea bass, which was a decent dish, but the wait for it was so long that my family had already finished eating by the time mine arrived — it really spoiled the flow of the lunch. They would’ve had to eat cold food if they’d waited for me, so I asked them to go ahead.

Another disappointment was the so-called “large octopus salad,” which cost £23. It came with just five small pieces of octopus, no dressing, and very little flavour — definitely not worth the price or the name.

I did raise the issues with the manager, who politely apologised and offered a dish replacement, but that had already been done. She also suggested we try the terrace for a drink — not complimentary, of course. I want to be clear that I wasn’t looking for compensation, but I would’ve appreciated a more thoughtful response, especially since these kinds of mistakes can affect a special occasion.

Overall, it felt like a place more focused on image than experience. I left disappointed and wouldn’t be in a hurry to return.

Despite having above average food, Aviary misses on the fundamentals.
We went for brunch at 12pm and were escorted to our seats by a flustered hostess who apologized for the delay as she was in her morning huddle. Well, the huddle continued as we walked by and so we heard all about their service goals for the day. 🥴
Our server was a bit odd and seemed overwhelmed, although we were her first table.
Our drinks took 10-15 minutes to be delivered although they sat at the bar for more than half that time.
The seafood platter was well made and worth the £20 supplemental fee to our brunch set menu.
The vibe was definitely “Girls Brunch” and all you can drink. We were surrounded! 😆
Not a bad restaurant.
Just not our scene.

places.name: Savage Garden Rooftop Bar
places.formatted_address: Floor 12, 7 Pepys St, London EC3N 4AF, UK
places.editorial_summary: Chic cocktail lounge with large rooftop terrace overlooking Tower Bridge and Tower of London.

reviews.text: We had just flown into London and spent the walking, we were staying at the Doubletree and didn’t want to venture far for dinner.  They have a club/restaurant on the 12th floor.  It looks bougie but very nice, the food was delicious and we were happy with the Bou Beef and Pizza.   The view from here is awesome!

You never forget how people make you feel 🫶💖

I celebrated my birthday here and came back a week later for drinks. It was the most incredible evening - everything was perfect! The DJ banging out amazing tunes, unbeatable views over London and delicious drinks - but above all it’s the service from the staff!

They remembered me from my birthday, they were so lovely, kind and welcoming. I really can’t recommend Savage Garden enough!

It’s my favourite place in London. I can’t wait to come back! 🤩😍

Savage Garden is perched on the 12th floor of the DoubleTree Tower Hill, and from the moment you step out onto the rooftop, you understand why it is often described as London’s best-kept secret. The views stretch far and wide across the city, with a sweeping panorama that includes iconic landmarks such as The Shard, the Tower of London, and much of the historic skyline. It is one of those rare places where the setting feels just as memorable as the food and drinks.

The design of Savage Garden is striking and deliberate. Inside, the décor is bold, with a balance of raw urban edges and refined finishes. The reflective, scored, and textured surfaces contrast with plush velvet seating and marble-style floors, creating a space that feels sultry yet comfortable. It feels decadent without being overdone, and it sets the stage for an evening that is both stylish and relaxed. Whether you come for a casual meal, an after-work drink, or a special occasion, the atmosphere here makes it feel unique.

Our meal began with the Pizza Padellino, topped with truffle mushroom cream, pickled shallot onion, and stracciatella. This dish stood out for its rich flavour and perfectly balanced toppings. It was indulgent but not heavy, and easily a favourite at the table.

The Red One Burger followed, a pulled beef dirty burger with crispy shoestring fries and an egg. The beef was juicy and tender, and the combination worked beautifully. It was the kind of burger that leaves you satisfied without being overwhelming.

We then tried the crispy chicken wings served with a fermented pineapple and chilli sauce. These were excellent, with the wings cooked to the right level of crunch while the sauce added both heat and a tangy sweetness. They disappeared from the plate quickly, a clear sign of how enjoyable they were.

Another highlight was the Weeping Tiger Beef, a dish that paired tamarind dressing with spicy cucumber and fresh herbs. The flavours were bold and refreshing, with the tamarind giving a sharp note that cut through the richness of the beef. The cucumber and herbs added freshness, making it a well-balanced dish overall.

For something a little different, we tried the cheese selection board, which featured Stilton, Somerset Brie, and Godminster Cheddar. This was served with damson chutney, water crackers, and grapes. It was a simple yet very enjoyable course, with each cheese offering a distinct taste that worked well with the accompaniments.

The finale was a real standout: the warm Savage Doughnut filled with yuzu and peach custard and topped with coconut crumble. This dessert was nothing short of excellent. The doughnut itself was light and warm, the custard had a lovely balance of citrus and sweetness, and the coconut crumble gave it texture. It was a memorable way to finish the meal and one of the best desserts I have had in recent months.

Alongside the food, we ordered a selection of mocktails. Each was refreshing, carefully prepared, and nicely presented. My personal highlight was the Aroa Nui, which had a balance of tropical flavours without being overly sweet. It paired perfectly with the food and was something I would order again without hesitation.

The service throughout the evening was faultless. Maya and Iba looked after us from the beginning, making us feel welcome and comfortable. They provided helpful recommendations on both the food and drinks, and their attention to detail was clear. Their friendly and professional service elevated the entire experience, showing that Savage Garden is as much about people as it is about food and views.

Overall, Savage Garden is a destination worth visiting for anyone in London. The panoramic views are unmatched, the food is creative and delicious, the drinks are refreshing, and the service is excellent. Whether you are looking for a rooftop spot to enjoy with friends, a romantic evening with a view, or a place to celebrate a special occasion, Savage Garden delivers on every level.

Halal options available

We came here for the bottomless brunch for £60pp. This included a main, side & dessert. All the food was really good and I loved the bao buns! The service however was really slow. Considering the brunch is "bottomless" we had to keep asking for refills! Other brunches I go to they just fill you up even before you finish your drink. We were all without a drink for a good 20 minutes. It also seemed a little bit quiet for a Saturday but then we saw there was more seating around the corner and outside seating. I think the area around the corner would have been a bit more of a better vibe.

I had an amazing experience at this rooftop bar! The ambiance was stylish yet relaxed, with cozy seating and a stunning view of the city skyline. The cocktails were crafted to perfection—creative, well-balanced, and beautifully presented. The staff were very friendly and attentive. Whether you're looking for a chilled evening with friends or a romantic night out, this spot hits all the right notes. Highly recommend catching the sunset from up there—truly magical!

places.name: 1 Leicester Square Rooftop Bar & Restaurant
places.editorial_summary: Rooftop bar serving cocktails, burgers and gourmet mains in a contemporary space with skyline views.

reviews.text: Fantastic views over Leicester Square and the London skyline.  Great cocktails and fantastic food - the halloumi fries were amazing and the best I’ve ever had!  Service was great too and yes; it’s a bit pricy - but what do you expect given the location?!  I do think it’s worth it though and reasonable value. Great place to start a day or night from.

I had a booking with my partner on a Tuesday afternoon to celebrate her birthday and we were both blown away by the attention and care we received. We were served by Victoria, who constantly checked on us and gave us the attention we desired and expected. I am also very grateful to the other three staff members: Jay, Pavlo, and Alp, who surprised us with a loving birthday gesture. They were all very attentive.

The view from the bar is surreal, with all of London visible (including Canary Wharf in the background, beautiful). And the food and drinks were even better than expected, somehow. We had an unforgettable experience, and it certainly added a lot to this special day.

We had breakfast at the 1 Leicester Square Rooftop Bar every day during our stay at Hotel Indigo, and it quickly became a highlight of our trip. The service was exceptional—Manager Ali and his team made us feel warmly welcomed and well taken care of. The food exceeded our expectations, both in quality and variety. And of course, the stunning view of the London skyline made every morning memorable. Highly recommended!

TRAGIC - Bottomless Brunch

Nice view but that’s the only good thing. Food was awful — a dry piece of fish with fries, an ice cream sundae that looked like a school dinner, and overall very low-rent. Basic plates, dirty salt and pepper pots, and dated music from a tragic DJ. To top it off, we were told “last refill” 30 minutes before our time was up. Definitely one to avoid.

Lovely atmosphere and beautiful view. Although cocktails are generally more on the expensive side with the cheapest at £16. We had the loveliest server: Niral, he was very tentative was kind. Lovely view and had a great night overall. Would be back again

places.name: JOIA Restaurant, Bar & Rooftop
places.formatted_address: 15th Floor, 1 Electric Blvd, Nine Elms, London SW11 8BJ, UK
places.vicinity: 15th Floor, Electric Boulevard, 1 Electric Blvd, London

reviews.text:
We visited JOIA Restaurant as a group of nine. The venue and customer service were excellent definitely 5/5. The food presentation was impressive, and overall the dishes looked great.

I ordered the arroz de mariscos, which I’d rate 3.5/5. I found it a little salty at first, but after squeezing the lime on it, the flavour balanced out nicely and became much more enjoyable. They also served these small potatoes that were absolutely delicious.

In my experience, JOIA is a beautiful spot with top notch service, a welcoming atmosphere and lovely food. I would visit again. ❤️

Went to this restaurant with my girlfriends on a Friday evening.
Upstairs is a rooftop bar with a great atmosphere and a wide selection of drinks.
The food and drinks are on the pricier side, but the ambiance makes up for it.
The cuisine is a fusion of Portuguese and Spanish flavors.
We ordered a variety of dishes to try — the food was flavorful and satisfying, especially for someone trying Portuguese cuisine for the first time.
The service was also very good.

Beautiful restaurant
Not much of a view if you look down because it is train tracks.
However, if you look up then it’s gorgeous specifically when the sun is setting.
Service impeccable. Attention to every single  detail.
The food was delicious too however for me a bit too oily.
The quantity served for the price is disappointing.
Unfortunately they don’t have any vegan desserts.

We celebrated our wedding anniversary at Joia, and it was a truly lovely experience. The food was amazing, with authentic Portuguese flavors and a stunning view of Battersea Park and the Power Station. We highly recommend the octopus—it's fantastic! We tried the Chef's Menu, and it was a great way to enjoy a variety of dishes. It was also a pleasure meeting Chef Rafa. We’ll definitely be coming back!

We had a lovely visit to this restaurant!
Must say that to get there it was a bit confusing due to the lifts system within the hotel. We had to find staff to allow us to get up there as we were pressing the buttons and it didn’t seem like it was working. But maybe it was just a “us” thing!
We arrived at the restaurant and we were greeted warmly by the staff and the atmosphere was brilliant. Service was flawless and the food was excellent.
Must say that I drank London Essence for the first time (White peach & jasmine flavour) and this is now my favourite drink ever!
Additionally, this was a meal out to celebrate my partner’s birthday and according to my note left on the booking form, they presented him a cake at the end with a happy birthday note. Really thoughtful gesture and the cake was brilliant. Definitely coming back.

places.name: Pergola on the Wharf
places.editorial_summary: Contemporary, plant-filled tavern on the water offering cocktails & casual bites.

reviews.text:
Came here with some colleagues for an evening meal.
Service was good and efficient, and we all enjoyed our food.

I had the cheeseburger, which was made of 2 patties (not really smashed as per the description) which had a good taste.  Plenty of cheese and a nice soft bun.

The place is really nicely decorated and they have some amazing wraparound views with tables outside.

Another birthday celebration done! This was a last minute booking but very much worth it! We thoroughly enjoyed our time at Pergola. Loved the the vibe and will have to return to dance a little more. Thank you to our waiter for it night, unfortunately I cannot remember his name.

A lovely place to eat, food is great, with great service and a nice atmosphere.
In the middle of the iconic Canary wharf- what is not to like. We were a party of 11 after a work operations meeting and the company was enjoyable to boot, with some belly laughing.

📍 Pergola on the Wharf, Canary Wharf
