After seeing Pergola all over my feed—lush interiors, rooftop vibes, and bold plates—we finally booked in for an evening visit. And yes, booking ahead is essential—this place gets busy, and for good reason.

🍽️ What we ordered:
• Korean-Glazed Flat Iron Steak with Yuzu Hollandaise & House Pickles
• Sweet Potato Fries
• Korean Pulled Beef Bao Buns with Kimchi Slaw & Gochujang Sauce
• Camden Pale Ale
• Diet Coke

🥩 The Korean-Glazed Flat Iron Steak was cooked beautifully—tender, smoky, and packed with flavour. The Yuzu Hollandaise added a citrusy zing that cut through the richness perfectly, and the house pickles brought a bright, crunchy balance. The Korean Pulled Beef Bao Buns were equally epic: pillowy-soft, filled with slow-cooked, spicy-sweet beef, creamy kimchi slaw, and a generous drizzle of gochujang sauce. And the Sweet Potato Fries? Crispy, golden, and dangerously snackable. Drinks were simple but hit the spot—Camden Pale Ale for a hoppy kick, and a Diet Coke to keep it classic.

📝 What I liked?
The evening atmosphere was vibey—think fairy lights, chilled music, and a buzzy crowd without feeling chaotic. The space is airy and beautifully designed, with greenery everywhere and waterfront views if you time it right. Food came out quick, portions were solid, and every dish delivered on flavour.

👎 What I didn’t like?
Honestly, not much. It’s definitely a spot you plan for—not ideal for walk-ins—but the payoff is worth the booking. Prices reflect the location and setting, but the quality backs it up.

✅ Would I go back?
Absolutely. I already want to try more of the menu—and the cocktails next time. It’s a perfect mix of relaxed and refined, and ideal for an after-work treat or a casual date night.

🔍 Note: First visit review—excited to return and try more soon.

Rating: ⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️ out of ⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️

📌 DISCLAIMER: All reviews are based on real visits to the listed establishment, items ordered, my personal experience on the day, and a true reflection of my visit.

#PergolaOnTheWharf #CanaryWharfEats #EveningEats #KoreanFlavours #FlatIronSteak #YuzuHollandaise #PulledBeefBao #KimchiSlaw #GochujangGoodness #RooftopVibes #LondonFoodie #SweetPotatoLove #FoodieLondon #FirstBiteReview #SkylineDining #PergolaVibes

To begin with, at the front the security asked to check my bag which it wasn’t a problem till he decided to get my wallet and started removing cards, money.. which I thought it was way too much, I really didn’t like it and he should have mentioned the reason why the thorough search.
The food had everything to be great, the Korean chicken burger sounded delicious, weirdly it arrived 10min after ordering, it wasn’t good it wasn’t warm.
Music was good but a bit too loud when trying to have food and a conversation.
The waitress was nice

I went with my girlfriends and we had such a great time. The atmosphere was lovely, the cocktails were amazing, and the food was absolutely delicious. I had the risotto and it was honestly one of the best dishes I’ve ever tasted. Everything was fresh, flavorful, and beautifully presented. Highly recommend this place — can’t wait to come back!

It’s a very nice atmosphere to have a nice meal with nice music and friendly staff. The food was amazing! We ordered the steak, schnitzel and risotto for dinner with appetizers and drinks. The steak was wonderful. The risotto was rich with flavor and the schnitzel was delicious. Definitely coming again!

Soho Social offers a delightful dining experience with its warm, inviting ambience that perfectly balances modern chic and cozy comfort. The food is flavorful and well-presented, with each dish crafted to satisfy both the palate and the eye. What truly sets the evening apart, however, is the exceptional service provided by two attentive and friendly ladies who made the entire visit feel personal and welcoming. Their professionalism and warmth added a special touch, making the evening not just a meal, but a memorable experience.
Loved the food and cocktails, really tasty and fresh. Great attentive service and cozy atmosphere, would definitely go back. Seafood pasta and Mac n Cheese croquettes were delicious!! 10/10 place

Amazing drinks, great espresso martini!!
Katerina Irisa and Ersi were so friendly and helpful! Great service.
Couldn’t recommend enough

places.name: Blacklock Soho
places.formatted_address: 24 Great Windmill St, London W1D 7LG, UK
places.vicinity: Duke Of Argyll, 24 Great Windmill St, London

html_attributions: ดร.เก๋ กมลวรรณ พรหมศักดิ์ Dr.Kamonwan Phromsak

places.editorial_summary: Atmospheric basement restaurant and bar for seared meat chops, plus cocktails from trolley carts.

reviews.text:
Better than the average.
Their steak was fantastic. Went for the butchers cut, 300g sirloin, medium rare. Sadly a few inedible chewy bits which I had to  dispose of but the seasoning and sides were incredibly well thought and became a mini buffet, taking your buds on a culinary adventure. A special shout out to the Ash roasted sweet potato. The chips were the best I've had in a steak house. Think authentic hand cut chipppy chips, but cooked in beef fat and extra crispy and incredibly pillowy soft on the inside.
The bone marrow left me a little wanting, not a huge amount of flavour for something that is otherwise normally a flavour bomb.
The salad added a much needed cut through the overall richness and doubled as a convenient palate cleanser.
The white chocolate cheesecake was incredibly rich and ended what I felt was a very good meal.
The service was very good and our waiter was incredibly positive and helpful.
Thank you for a memorable meal, this was my first time and will definitely not be my last.

The place is so popular that you need to book a table in advance. We did not; but could still have dinner there after spending 2 hours in a nearby pub. The meat was grilled to perfection and the service excellent. The waiter knew everything in the menu and his advice was excellent for choosing the food. They were out of rib eye so we went for the rump cap which was very good. And finished everything with a more than generous portion of home made cheesecake. Will definitely go back next time in London.

Blacklock Soho is my favourite spot in London. If you like all kinds of meat, go for the All In Sunday Roast (£26) – beef, lamb, and pork with all the trimmings and endless gravy. Personally, I stick to the beef medium-well and it’s perfect every time. And don’t leave without the cheesecake – easily the best I’ve ever had. Great hospitality and service, easy booking. The atmosphere is relaxed but lively, perfect for a Sunday meal with friends or family.

This restaurant is my absolute favorite place to eat in London, and we made sure to book a table three weeks in advance—it was the one place I knew I couldn’t leave the city without revisiting.

As always, the service was exceptional. John, our server, was a delight—attentive, personable, and spot-on with his recommendations, which set the tone for a memorable evening.

For starters, we ordered the cheese and pickle biscuits and the mushrooms on toast, both excellent choices to open the meal. For mains, we had the prime ribeye and a tenderloin fillet steak, accompanied by chips and roasted sweet potatoes. The steaks were flawless—juicy, tender, and cooked exactly to our request. Both cuts were packed with flavor, melt-in-your-mouth tender, and so well-prepared that they hardly needed sauce. Even so, we tried the garlic bone marrow and chopped sauce, both of which complemented the meat beautifully without overshadowing it.

The sides were well-executed, though the sweet potatoes deserve special mention. The chips were classic—crispy on the outside and fluffy inside—but not extraordinary. The roasted sweet potatoes, however, were spectacular: charred on the outside, fork-tender within, and perfectly seasoned, easily one of the best side dishes I’ve had in London.

The true star of the evening was dessert: their famous white chocolate cheesecake. Creamy, rich, and indulgent without being overwhelming, it remains my favorite dessert in London—simple yet brilliant, and the perfect way to end the meal.

For anyone seeking a steak dinner in London, you cant find any better than Blacklock. From service to execution, it delivers consistently, and for me, it’s unmatched.

We came yesterday for a dinner - and I couldn’t wait to leave a review. This place is fantastic! First of all, they only had one table at 10pm but after messaging the team on OpenTable despite them clearly being really busy they very kindly slotted us in earlier (thank you Olga!) The atmosphere is lovely, it’s not a large place but it’s buzzing and feels cosy and lively. The service was excellent - we got talked through the menu, the advice we got on what to order was great and our waiter suggested a primitivo instead of a house red which was amazingly light and one of the best reds I’ve had. We went for pigs head for starters (pulled pork on sourdough which comes with gravy), that was 10/10. We also ordered a Denver and a butcher cut Fillet with a side of broccoli salad and sweet potato. Everything was delicious! Denver reminded me of flat iron but thicker and gamier - not chewy at all and perfectly cooked. The fillet despite the size was melting on the inside with a charred exterior. Lovely sweet potato but the broccoli salad was phenomenal - it doesn’t even taste like broccoli, very crunchy and moreish with a beautiful dressing. Chop sauce is a classic peppercorn and we tried bernaise as well however in hindsight the meats didn’t need any sauces. We finished with sharing the white chocolate cheesecake and black coffees. The cheesecake was great but I’d maybe say it’s a white chocolate mouse constructed like a trifle almost with different layers you then sort of mix up - light, not too sweet, a perfect finish. And their coffee was spot on too. Our bill came to 101 for two with drinks, mains, starters, sides and a shared desert with coffee which is incredible value. All of the waiters that served us were attentive, friendly and looked like they are having fun which honestly makes such a great change from the usual. Thank you so much to the team for making our evening in London special and for the best food we’ve had in a while, we’ll be back!

places.name: Kapara Soho
places.formatted_address: James court, 14 Greek St, London W1D 4DP, UK

reviews.text:
Got a £50 voucher, so give it a try with a friend!

We really appreciate the service by Jubear as he is very patient to explain all the drinks and food since the beginning. Thank you!

Overall food is really nice however it’s really pricey so maybe it’s best for celebration?
Or I will definitely revisit if I got the voucher again!

Food: HUMMUS WITH SHORT RIB, CEVICHE CATCH OF THE DAY (sea bream) SWEET POTATO WELLINGTON, and BLACK & GOLD.
Drinks: Tibi tibble and Passionfruit & Basil

What a great place to eat, especially for when the weather is nice and you can sit outside.
We were a group of 6 and ordered a large selection of items from the A la carte menu which we all shared including several bottles of wine.
Everything tasted fresh, was flavoursome and arrived pretty quickly. Out of all the dishes, my favourite had to be the beef short rib and burnt edge rice. It was succulent and full of flavour. The aubergine and dates was a close second.
The service was great too, attentive but not overbearing. We had a 50% discount voucher so our bill came to just under £70pp which could’ve easily have been £140pp if we had paid full price. So not cheap but definitely worth it. Would recommend.

We loved our dinner experience at Kapara. All of the staff were friendly, welcoming and helpful. Food was delicious, plentiful and beautifully presented. We had the vegetarian tasting menu and some ceviche. Can’t wait to go back!
Fantastic small plates. We tried many items. The watermelon carpaccio, date & miso aubergine, and the cauliflower vegan crumble were standouts for us. Everything was wonderful.

Great service, knowledgeable staff and not pushy.
Chickpea cake, aubergine salad, cured salmon all beautifully done. But it’s the golden chicken that impressed me the most

places.name: The Devonshire
places.formatted_address: The Devonshire, 17 Denman St, London W1D 7HW, UK
places.vicinity: The Devonshire, Devonshire Arms, 17 Denman St, London

reviews.text: Believe the hype. This restaurant serves up the best steaks and service, truly unforgettable both times I’ve been. The set menu is incredible value, however I do insist that their scallops are some of the best I’ve ever had in my life. Go for an early dinner, it’s an ideal spot for pre-theatre as well.

I was pleasantly surprised by everything this pub had to offer. Instagram gave it all the hype and it is well deserved. On walkup to the pub, I saw after-work patrons grabbing a pint. On entry, the acoustics were on par for a pub and the decor of the place matched that of a pub. Our hostess was accommodating of our early arrival and seated us promptly on the 3rd floor. Our waitress Siri and her trainee were nothing but phenomenal. For 146 pounds we had 2 glasses of wine, 1 Guinness, one 3 scallop appetizer,  one 12oz ribeye, 3 lamb chops, mashed potatoes, salad, and sticky toffee pudding with ice cream. At this price point I will certainly be returning. Also I would be remiss if I didn't highlight the details of each portion of our meal: the wine (Devonshire special) was spicy but a great pairing for red meat, the scallops were tender, the meat items were true to temperature, the mashed potatoes were delicate, the salad sufficient, the sticky toffee pudding was to die for: a warm coarse texture intricately balanced by cool smooth ice cream. The Devonshire deserves a 10/10 and nothing less.

Having lunch at the Devonshire was a brilliant and memorable experience. It's really popular for a good reason. We had the set menu which was £29 for three courses. Such fantastic value for what you get. Everything was so tasty, and the bread and butter that is also served with it is so good. Just a cracking experience and I highly recommend you book, if only for the wonderful pint of Guinness. It just tastes better! Thanks Devonshire and all the staff for making me and my wife's experience a memorable one. Shout out to the waiter on Saturday lunch time who served us, we were on table 28 if that helps! Brilliant service.

Incredible food and excellent service. We had a reservation months in advance to enjoy Sunday roast while in London for vacation and it exceeded our expectations. The place is packed and the environment was fantastic! Loved everything we ate and although so full had to try the Sticky Toffee Pudding as well. 5 stars all around

This place is known for doing the best Guinness in London, but having been here, this is the best place for steak. Never have I had such an amazing steak in my life, it was cooked over charcoal right in front of you which is just amazing!

The service was brilliant, the food was superb, and the sticky toffee pudding was out of this world. The scallops were beautifully cooked as well with that vinegary taste which was lovely. You do also get bread and salted butter for the table, and it was very good. We had the Guinness Zero and that was like the ones you get in Dublin.

Need to book in advance to get a table, though during the quieter hours of a weekday, you should be able to get a table.

places.name: Dirty Bones Soho
places.editorial_summary: American plates and cocktails offered in a chill, industrial space lined with white-washed brick.

reviews.text: Myself and fiance stumbled across this place (we had been recommended the French restaurant around the corner). The cocktails are amazing and the food is fantastic. The lamb fries are so filling they could be a main not a side. The mac & cheese burger is so juicy. While we couldn't manage a dessert we would definitely go back.

Had a Bottomless Brunch at
Denman Street last weekend.

Firstly let me say the KEN our waiter was excellent.  Such a great example of how to  host a table properly.  He was attentive, knowledgable and made the whole lunch a very enjoyable experience - hence the star rating.

The options for food for the brunch were excellent either from a set menu or from some of the main menu.   The drinks were flowing as you’d hope at a Bottomless Brunch and we weren’t rushed during our allotted time.

Overall a very nice experience with quality meat and sides.

The majority of the food was good but, the portion sizes and the prices were not the best to say the least. The chicken tacos were good but the beef ones were below average if not worse. The chips were well received. Left the restaurant still hungry after spending £120 for a group of 4. The service was great tho and our main server was very chill and friendly.
Had a great bottomless brunch - Ken was great at keeping the drinks flowing. Great large food selections including steak! Highly recommend.

Excellent service and attention to detail by the service staff (an example being that we were celebrating and so at the end of the meal were given a complimentary shot, though the server/team, noticed that we were not drinking alcohol and made it non-alcoholic, which was pleasing).

The food itself was delicious and great portions. The lamb ribs were some of the best ribs we have ever had and we left feeling very full and satisfied.

Will definitely be recommending to friends and will certainly return.

I ate at The Seafood Bar in Amsterdam a number of years ago and thoroughly enjoyed it. So I was glad to see a location in London and it did not disappoint. I was able to get a seat at the counter even though it was a busy time. I started with the sea bass ceviche, followed by the octopus from Galicia, both dishes were very good. For my main, I order the fish and chips, and it was fantastic. Their signature fish batter had a nice flavorful kick to it making different than your usual fried fish.

The food here is genuinely exceptional. We ordered the 'Fruits de Mer' platter, oysters, and champagne, and it was a wildly satisfying experience. The quality and freshness of the seafood are undeniable and absolutely five-star worthy. The kitchen is clearly doing a phenomenal job. However, the reason for not giving a fifth star comes down to the service, which unfortunately did not match the quality of the food. For a meal at this level, you expect a certain standard of attentiveness that was missing. For example:
We had to pour our own champagne from the bottle throughout the meal.
I repeatedly had to get up from my table to find a waiter to ask for simple things like a finger bowl and, eventually, the bill.
It was very difficult to get anyone's attention, and while I understand they were very busy, the service shouldn't suffer to this extent. A final small point is that they dont accept cash and its a WiFi dead zone so I had to use their WiFi and again finding out the password required me to stand up and find a waiter. I paid by card without a problem, but its a policy some customers might appreciate knowing in advance. Overall, I would return for the incredible food, but I would have to adjust my expectations for the service. If the front-of-house could match the excellence of the kitchen, this would be an easy 5-star recommendation.

We had an incredible experience at The Seafood Bar. Everything we ordered was excellent. We shared several appetizers — octopus, scallops, and shrimp — each cooked perfectly and full of flavor. There’s a clear Spanish twist to many of the dishes that makes them stand out from traditional seafood fare. Our server, Yorkina was awesome!

The fish and chips were the best I’ve ever had — light, crispy, and beautifully seasoned, again with that subtle Spanish influence that makes the dish unforgettable. Even the fries deserve a mention: thick-cut, golden, and perfectly crispy.

Overall, The Seafood Bar delivers fresh, creative seafood with top-tier quality and presentation. Highly recommended for anyone who loves seafood done right.

Had the Fish and Chips plus calamari as a starter. The portions are big and the seafood is very fresh. The atmosphere paired with the music selection made for a relaxing experience and our server Caitlin made us feel very welcomed.
Visiting from NYC, would 10/10 come back here when I’m in London!

A brilliant seafood restaurant. As soon as you walk in, you can smell the essence of fish almost as if you had jumped into the sea with your very own gills. The staff were very nice and accommodating, and the food was good too. Would recommend the scallops starter, and fish and chips which were excellent. The monkfish dish was okay, not the best. Would definitely recommend a visit.

places.name: Noble Rot Soho
places.editorial_summary: Elegant, snug eatery with a European menu featuring seafood & meat plates, plus a robust wine list.

reviews.text:
Overall the dining experience was amazing.  We were warmly greeted, which was a great start!

Began with a variety of local breads, big meaty olives, and Cornish crab and Tomato salad.

Paired starters with a lovely dry summer Rose (in the picture)

Followed up with the Roasted Chicken and morels and rice pilaff. It was obviously prepared and roasted with care.

Some suggestions to elevate the experience: The service was excellent but more attention should be paid to the empty wine glasses.  I should not have to refill myself. Add some light background music to create a more relaxed and intimate atmosphere. Finally, when wait staff transitions, say goodbye and introduce colleagues.

Overall, I highly recommend a visit and will definitely return to try other items in the menu!

A beautiful meal in a lovely spot. The food really packed a punch on the flavour. I would say quite expensive as the portion sizes are on the smaller side - but it’s London, and you are paying for the name as it’s an institution. We got sea bream and a gorgeous rissotto with two sides of potatoes and a salad. Plus a bottle of wine it came to £130. A nice treat. Thank you also to our lovely waitress Mia.

Been to the Lambs Conduit location which I love but first time in Soho. Dined alone. Was seated in the cozy upstairs room. Service was impeccable. Had a lovely starter of cold tuna with courgette and capers. Perfect for a hot day. The Hake main was outstanding. This place couldn't provide a better dining experience.

Great dinner at Noble Rot SoHo. Had to try the famous chicken, for two it was super filling, delicious and creamy (note that it takes around an hour to cook so be prepared for a wait, but worth it!). Also tried the bread and butter and ox tongue as starters. Overall great experience and atmosphere, lovely service, and delicious food. A bit pricey at £60pp (excluding drinks), but recommend!

From the understated exterior, you can already sense the atmosphere inside: refined, elegant, and warmly inviting. On a rainy London evening, it makes the perfect spot for dinner. The staff and bartenders were friendly, professional, and efficient, always with a smile and impeccable manners.

The interior is sleek and dark, exuding sophistication, though the occasional creak of the wooden staircase can be a small distraction.

As for the food, the bread trio was fragrant with herbs, butter, and grains, though slightly over-seasoned for my taste. The chicken liver profiterole was the standout dish—silky, rich liver balanced by the refreshing jelly, though the choux pastry itself felt a bit firm and lacking in buttery aroma. The roast chicken was excellent: tender, juicy, and deeply flavorful with a wonderfully crisp skin and the aroma of wine. The only regret was that the morel mushrooms didn’t fully shine.

Overall, highly recommended—an ideal place for a date and a glass of wine.

places.name: Bill's Soho Restaurant
places.editorial_summary: Contemporary European chain dishing up separate breakfast, afternoon tea, lunch and dinner menus.

reviews.text:
We had the absolute pleasure of being served by an amazing  girl named Katerina, at this marvelously spot in London! She was incredibly friendly, full of positive energy, and made our whole experience unforgettable. Her warm smile and attention to detail truly stood out — she made us feel so welcome, like we were old friends.

It’s rare to meet someone who combines professionalism with such genuine kindness. She went above and beyond to make sure everything was perfect. If every place had someone like her, brunch in London would always be this special!

Highly recommend visiting — and if you’re lucky enough to be served by her, you’ll see exactly what I mean. 💫

Bill’s Soho Restaurant is a fantastic place that I highly recommend in the heart of London. I visited for a late breakfast (brunch), and it was an excellent experience from start to finish. The food was fresh, flavorful, and beautifully presented – I tried the eggs with sides, and everything tasted perfect. The restaurant has a cozy, stylish atmosphere with a mix of modern and classic décor, making it a great spot for friends or family. The staff were friendly, attentive, and provided quick service with a smile, which made the visit even more enjoyable. A must-try in Soho!

A decent option for a quick bite in central London. Ensure though that you have booked a table in advance as it gets popular.
This restaurant has a number of vegan and vegetarian options.

Food was very good. Recommend the porridge and the eggs Benedict. The ham they used is great. As an essentially vegetarian person i made an exception for it.
Service was good not exceptional bit no complaints.
Love the atmosphere. Always visit when in London.

Delicious eggs, avocado and mushrooms.
Welcoming atmosphere with great relaxing music.
The place to be for a healthy breakfast in the core of London.
So accommodating to our dietary needs too 😉
And good news: prices are fair and you won’t be ripped off 🤩

places.name: Cahoots Underground
places.formatted_address: 13 Kingly Ct, Carnaby, London W1B 5PW, UK
places.editorial_summary: Afternoon tea & cocktails served in a vintage-style speakeasy set in a disused underground station.

reviews.text: Some call it a tourist trap, others might just not like themed bars, but this place is London-coded and worth a visit if you’re willing to indulge in the thematic fun! Beware the price, at £16/cocktail, you’re really paying for the atmosphere and bizarre but fun display of each drink. The staff gave entirely fabulous former theatre-kid energy, the decorations were a feast for the eyes, and the entire experience will be sure to please any tourist who comes through.

Popped in here for a cocktail as had seen videos of it online before a trip to London. We visited on a weekday evening, didn’t have a booking but were given a table within a few minutes of arriving. Service was great and the team were all very friendly.

Good selection of cocktails and the theming in the bar is very immersive throughout. Definitely a place to visit!

10/10. The theme and commitment of the staff really makes it feel like your in another time. The bar is so cool and unique. Bar area and multiple seating areas. The menu had me actually giggling it’s so silly. They have crazy cups and the drinks are mixed perfectly. You can’t go wrong. Bathroom teaches you how to keep a man, I was laughing the whole time. Excellent experience, highly recommend

What a fantastic cocktail bar - great themed decor, gorgeous cocktails, quirky nostalgia and the most fantastic service. Great place to start/end or spend a night in Central London.  Will definitely be back!

I had the most amazing experience at Cahoots Underground! The service was absolutely fantastic – our server was so attentive and made sure everything was perfect throughout the night. The atmosphere was incredible, full of character and charm, which made the whole evening feel really special.

For my birthday, I was surprised with a handwritten letter, a fun pin badge, and even some free shots – such a thoughtful touch that made me feel truly celebrated. It’s not often you find a place that goes above and beyond like that.

Highly recommend Cahoots Underground for anyone looking for a unique spot with top-notch service and unforgettable vibes!

places.name: BAO Soho
places.formatted_address: 53 Lexington St, Carnaby, London W1F 9AS, UK
places.editorial_summary: Intimate, wood-furnished space for steamed milk buns & other inventive Taiwanese eats & drinks.

reviews.text:
This place was great. It’s on the Michelin list. We walked in on a Friday and there was about a 30 minute wait for 2.

All the dishes we tried were good, but I loved the steak rice, mackerel bao, and daikon bao. The ambience is also nice - it’s a very cozy/intimate restaurant.

Good service as well. Reasonably priced. Would come back.

I decided to stop by this spot because of the positive reviews and it’s quite busy, but worth the wait!

I got the long day menu and extras. Overall it was a delicious dinner and well curated. The flavors were well matched and the fowl bowl was delicious along with the traditional Bao bun. The fried chicken was also phenomenal.

The drinks were just right and not too strong. The peanut drink at the end was a great way to recap the night! Overall a solid dine in with excellent customer service and I’d definitely come back again.

This place is a trendy Taiwanese restaurant. It's VERY popular, so I recommend that you book in advance.
For Mains: I had the Classic Pork Bao, 3 pieces of Taiwanese Fried Chicken Nuggets and Sweet Potato with Plum Pickle Ketchup.
For Drink: I had the House Roasted Peanut Milk.
For Dessert: I had the Horlicks Ice Cream Bao.
All very good and the total bill came to £29.15 (including service charge), which I thought was reasonable 👌🏽
The customer service was friendly and the waitress helped me pick the best options to suit my taste.
The place is a bit of a squeeze but I feel like that adds to experience 😊

Fabulous experience at this restaurant. Had 4 different Bao, each special and unique and my favorite bite of the night, the Soy glazed Aubergine. Staff incredibly kind, helpful and engaging. Highly recommend this little gem!

Wanted to try this place for long time. I loved the chicken BAO and scallops in the shell. However, the prawn BAO was too overwhelming as the bread was sweet, and too much garlic ( I’m a garlic lover by the way) yet this one I couldn’t eat.
The drink o ordered, salted lemonade was delicious .

places.name: Señor Ceviche Peruvian Restaurant Soho
places.formatted_address: Kingly Court, Carnaby, London W1B 5PW, UK
places.editorial_summary: Peruvian BBQ, ceviche and pisco cocktails served in a bright environment, reminiscent of urban Lima.

reviews.text:
Senor Ceviche is a fantastic spot for anyone who loves vibrant, flavorful food. The dishes are absolutely delicious, packed with fresh ingredients and bold tastes that really stand out. Pairing the food with their fantastic selection of drinks makes the experience even better, whether you’re after something refreshing or a little stronger.

On top of the great food and drinks, the atmosphere of the restaurant has such a great feel—warm, lively, and welcoming. The lovely staff go above and beyond to make sure you’re well looked after, adding to the overall charm. It’s the perfect place to relax, enjoy, and come away feeling like you’ve had a really special meal.

This was our first experience with Peruvian food and we had no expectations going in. To our surprise, we loved it! It’s the best food we've had in London so far! Every dish was incredibly delicious and the drinks were great too. The restaurant gets fully booked quickly, but they do accept walk-ins. It's the perfect spot for a date or a dinner with friends. We will definitely return!

I went to this restaurant for my birthday and everything was fantastic—the service, the atmosphere, and the food. If I could give it more stars, I definitely would. It's a bit pricey, but every bite was worth it—the food was absolutely delicious. A truly delightful experience.

At the end of the meal, the restaurant took a Polaroid-style photo of us for my birthday and gave it to me as a keepsake. Such a thoughtful and lovely gesture. I totally recommend this place. I had an amazing time and enjoyed every moment.

I have been coming to Señor Ceviche for YEARS and I can’t believe I’m only leaving a review now! I have never been disappointed, they have some of the best ceviche I’ve ever had and their chifa chicharrones are to die for. Service is always so nice and impeccable and today had the pleasure to be served by Diana who tempted me into trying the brunch menu, which was amazing value for money! The chocolate mousse for dessert was outstanding. A great choice and pretty much everything on the menu is a safe option cos you just know it’s gonna be delicious! Can’t wait to be back!
Lovely vibe in restaurant. Waitress explained the menu & was very knowledgeable. Fantastic food, every dish was 10/10. The cocktails were so tasty too! Will be returning.

Very friendly waiter and exquisite food. We asked the waiter to surprise us. That worked out very well! Indian with modern touch/feel to it. Fresh and comforty food, with subtle flavours as well as small explosion bombs, without being heavy or fatty. Loved the color scheme and the space. Hope to come back. In the meantime I hope the will consider a restaurant in Amsterdam.

Nice place and it did get very busy! The waiter telling us we only had 30 minutes to eat out mains was not good. Otherwise food is good, I recommend the venison. The coconut lassi was not for me and also if you order their chai tell them you want it hot otherwise they will serve it cold! Odd but true.

Went to Kricket in Shoreditch for dinner and had a really good time. The vibe was cool and relaxed, and the staff were friendly. Food was packed with flavour – a great mix of traditional Indian with a modern twist. They even brought out a grilled squash dish on the house, which was a nice surprise (and actually really good!). Everything we ordered was tasty and well put together.
Great Indian food. The best biryani I have had in a long time. The shrimp and chicken were delicious as well. We liked this place better than Dishoom.

Delicious and unique flavours of India with a twist. Beautiful pink decor. Friendly service. Recommend the pork neck curry, samosa and all the naan breads. The fried chicken could have been crispier and more flavourful. Overall a great experience

Flat Iron has an efficient and friendly service. It is reasonably priced and tasty. An easy option to recommend to people looking for a quick and reasonably priced steak.

The sides are also good. I enjoy the creamed spinach and the cheesy aubergine.

I dont go often as my one issue is that the steak comes out too oily for my personal taste. But a relatively minor and personal preference point

Amazing experience. Christian was brilliant. He took our order and remembered everything we wanted exactly, brought it out perfectly and cleared our plates. He checked up on us regularly and genuinely cared about how we were doing. I have been to this branch multiple times but when I went on Wednesday, it was without a doubt one of the best experiences I have had. I also noticed he was treating other customers with the same level of care and attention. He was really attentive. He definitely deserves a raise!

We love to a lunch here. The best steaks in town, very well pre-selected and curated. The place is charming and Hygor was an excellent host, making us feel very welcome and comfortable. Thank you so much!

Nice looking restaurant and a yummy steak dinner. The host welcomed a table-for-one with zero fuss and he had me seated in no time. My server was delightful, unfortunately, I didn’t catch her name (blonde, red bandana, iconic). She brought my food over quickly.

Food-wise, the creamed spinach had a mysterious flavour note I couldn’t quite pin down, and the mash was tasty but definitely leaning on its garlic butter and crispy topping for star power. The real MVP was the beef dripping popcorn. Life-changing. I’d happily come back just for a bucket of that.

Overall, the food was good, fairly priced, and felt like a luxury treat without emptying my wallet. Bonus points for the adorable knife token that allowed me a free ice cream for the walk home! A 10/10 ending.

What is not to love about a flat iron. As a single diner I loved the big table at the back, didn't feel like I was dining alone and I was happy to chat to another single diner had a lovely evening. Good value steak, love the popcorn at the start and an ice cream when you leave, although I couldn't fit that in after dinner and then lost my little cleaver token. Guess I'll just have to go back for another one sometime soon

places.name: Blacklock Shoreditch
places.editorial_summary: Set in a renovated furniture factory with mid-century, industrial interiors & modern, British menu.

reviews.text:
Fantastic food and generous portions.

My wife said it was the best lamb she’s ever had, and even as someone who doesn’t usually eat lamb, I thought it was perfectly cooked.

The brisket was tender, flavorful, and fell right off the bone.

The cauliflower mac and cheese was delightful as well.

Drinks were spot-on – balanced and not too sweet., and my server was extremely helpful in choosing the best ones.

The atmosphere has a lovely old English pub feel, which really adds to the experience. Highly recommend!

Delicious Sunday Roast Dinner! They sat me quickly & food was brought out hot & savory.  Very nice cuts of beef and yummy gravy.  Yorkshire pudding was phenomenal.  Carrots,
potatoes, and cabbage were perfect sides.  Nice wines by the glass and the martini was perfect. Great service.

We had an absolutely amazing dinner here! We did the all in which was £28 for some starter bites, 3 pieces of deliciously cooked meat, flatbread and a side each. Everything was cooked perfectly and flavoured so well. The staff were super friendly and helpful with the order too. Definitely recommend!

I'm going to be dreaming about the next time I eat here again. Everything from the food, service, and atmosphere was amazing! I loved how prompt the service was despite it being busy. We got the All-In Sunday Roast and it was so delicious. The meat is super tender and the potatoes have such a crispy texture. Not to mention the unlimited gravy refills. The drink flavors there are really unique and refreshing. Large assortment of different alcohol as well. The atmosphere here is really bustling and laid-back, and I would recommend going here for a date or just to hang out with friends and family.

First but not last visit to Blacklock for Sunday roast. Great food in (very) generous portions with equally generous servings of gravy, as well as attentive and friendly staff. The star of the meal was the meat and the roast veggies. Recommended to book a table!

Great menu and a little overpriced, Italian tapas style. Loved the freshness and quality of the ingredients, really top notch.
Only natural wines, which was a deciding factor for me.
Overpriced for the size of the dishes and the size of the restaurant, and they will put the bill on the table as soon you put your fork down.

We went to Popolo because it was recommended in the local Michelin guide. The food and service was good, but we would not come back a second time, as we expected a bit more in this price range. Especially the size of the portions was a bit disappointing (£20 for 9 Gnocchi and £7.5 for 3 slices of Focaccia).

The food is nice. Favourite is actually the bread and pork cheek pasta. However, I find it hard to justify the price, especially the smaller portion you are getting. I mean the asparagus is fresh and juicy but 17 pound is a bit too steep. And the 6 piece of pasta for 28 pound. Ummmmm..

We were lucky to score two seats at the bar around 9pm on a Thursday evening and what a treat it turned out to be!

We ordered the focaccia, burrata with chickpeas and olives, the crab pasta and the beef with salsa verde. Everything was beautifully prepared, but the standout by far was the crab pasta, unbelievably good and packed with flavour. It’s the kind of dish you want to go back for!!

What also stood out was the open kitchen. It’s a compact space, and with the bar seating wrapped around it, you get a full view of the action. Despite the pressure and pace, the chefs remained impressively calm and focused, quietly producing plate after plate of delicious food. It’s no small feat to work in such a visible and intense environment, hats off to them.

One lovely personal touch: I didn’t manage to get a photo of the fish (which was excellent), but when the chef noticed I was struggling a little with the bones, he kindly came over and helped us debone it. Such thoughtful service.

Highly recommend Popolo—great food, a cosy vibe, and seriously talented chefs who make it all look effortless.
Food was great , absolutely loved the pork cheek agnolotti I. Particular and the basque cheeses cake is a must have!

places.name: Padella Shoreditch
places.formatted_address: Padella, Shoreditch, 1 Phipp St, London EC2A 4PS, UK
places.editorial_summary: Laid-back restaurant specialising in pasta dishes amid industrial-chic surroundings.

reviews.text:
Fresh pasta everyday - loved this place!

The food are absolutely delicious. The marinated peppers were really flavorful, combined with burrata over sourdough made for a heavenly food. The pasta are absolutely delicious. Simple ingredients but just burst with flavor.

Get the kitchen counter, so you can see the efficiency of the chefs cooking all the pasta - it was mesmerizing.

Service was great - constantly checking on us despite the fact that it was a busy lunch service.

We booked Padella for our summer team dinner (a group of 20) and honestly, it was flawless from start to finish!! 🥳

The pasta was exceptional! Fresh and full of flavour, and the tiramisu was one of the best we’ve ever had. The service was also fabulous. A massive thank you to Ajar, who went above and beyond to make sure we were looked after. Friendly, attentive, and made us feel really welcome.

Perfect spot for groups, incredible food, brilliant service. We’ll absolutely be back!

🍝🍝🍝🍝
The food was good. Service was a bit weird. Some of the front doors and staff were a bit odd toward us. But our waiter was really nice.

Had the crab pasta, carpaccio, and tiramisu. everything tasted great. Service was friendly and smooth. Only downsides: portions were pretty small for the price, and the menu is limited, mainly pasta and antipasti.
Still, a nice spot for a relaxed meal. Would give it 4 out of 5 stars.

Really solid pasta spot.
We went twice—once for dinner, once for lunch—and both times were consistently great. Super satisfying.
We’re big fans of the thinner tagliarini—lighter than your usual tagliatelle, but perfect for clinging to the sauce. And the sauce? Flavorful, moorish, and just rich enough without being oily or heavy. They really nailed the balance. The slow-cooked tomato is a standout, and the spinach pesto is a close second.
If you order the sourdough, definitely ask them to toast it. It’s good, but £5.50 feels steep (especially when you’re used to free bread in France).
Service is lovely, and booking’s easy even on the weekends—a big plus in London.

places.name: SMOKESTAK
places.editorial_summary: A smoker and grill take centre stage at this stylishly rustic barbecue joint with a bar and terrace.

reviews.text:
We shared this feast among 5 people, and it was absolutely perfect.

The brisket, pulled pork, and ribs were all smoky, tender, and rich in flavour — each with its own character but balanced beautifully together. The sausage added a nice contrast, juicy and slightly spicy. Everything came with thoughtful sides: pickles, chili slices, and that signature house BBQ sauce that ties it all together.

The charred greens with feta, pomegranate, and nuts were a great fresh counterpoint to the meat platter, and the fries with aioli disappeared instantly. Drinks were excellent too — the house lemonade with chili and lime was surprisingly refreshing and unique.

Service was friendly and efficient, the vibe industrial rustic and warm, and the food came out perfectly timed for sharing.

If you’re visiting with a small group and want to taste a bit of everything, go for the shared meat platter — it’s spot-on in both portion and variety.

📍 SMOKESTAK, Shoreditch
🔥 Perfect for: small groups, casual dinners, meat lovers, and anyone craving authentic slow-smoked BBQ in London.

Fantastic meal. The meat was outstanding, and the starters and sides were just as good. Service was great, with spot-on recommendations. Portions are generous and the prices match the quality. It’s a busy place, so booking ahead is wise if you don’t want to gamble on a last-minute table. We ended up outside since that’s all that was left, but with perfect weather it turned into a highlight rather than a drawback.

We absolutely knew the food was going to be top tier, but it was the service that really smashed it out of the park here. From the moment we were greeted on the door by Kitty and Cristian, the rapport and bonhomie was already a dead cert: Charming, cheerful and a little cheeky in all the right quantities, we were promised VIP treatment from the get go, and boy did we get it. The equally charming Alexandra took our order, but sat opposite the pass, even the chefs engaged us in a deeply convivial manner, only ever enabled by an open kitchen like this.

Attentive, affable, and amusing, the team put on the perfect display of service with a smile, with a dash of well placed humour to really make us feel like part of the furniture or family….. not sure which.

Go here, eat well, and enjoy the experience created by an exceedingly well-matched team who love their jobs (I hope)!

The toffee dessert and the pork dishes are amazing. They are juicy and tender, especially the pork belly, highly recommended! Beef is a bit tough. Reasonable price. We sat downstairs and it was a bit dim. The taste of eggplant is subtle and there is too much raw green onion. Its strong flavour overpowers the dish.

May come back for the pork dishes.

Super cool place. Exceptional service from David!!! Very knowledgeable and attentive. We got a starter, 2 mains and one dessert 🍮 and a sorbet 🏠 super full for 2 people.

Definitely the sticky toffee pudding stood out the most. Good combo and not greasy. Warm dessert on a cool day. Otherwise beef brisket, beef ribs (super soft) and oxtail are all recs from us.
Great thanks to David again very observative, when the starter came he realised we were waiting so he asked if we preferred all dishes to come together, and also when the bottles were empty he bought a new one without us saying or asking 💓. Super lovely and made us feel very welcomed. Definitely a revisit soon.

places.name: The Blues Kitchen | Shoreditch
places.editorial_summary: Eclectic, industrial space offers areas for live blues music, dancing and Cajun-BBQ dining.

reviews.text:
Hands down, my new, absolute, favorite spot in London!
Far away from all the touristy spots, this hidden, not-so-hidden, spot is a gem amongst the other establishments close by!!! From the door security, Justina, to one of the most fantastic waiters we have ever had (Daryl), and bar server (Michelle), the place radiates with a charming atmosphere screaming, "come and stay awhile."
I was pleasantly surprised by the delectable aroma and essence of flavors that burst in my mouth from the smoked port rib (fell off the bone!!!!), and the earthy and nutty tastes of cheese from the macaroni and cheese. Daryl recommended the mac n cheese which I was hesitant about but glad I tried it! Daryl and Michelle managed to turn a routine work task of serving customers into a joyful, memorable evening simply by being attentive to our needs and having good conversation. Kudos to the restaurant manager for stopping by the table several times to check in on services. Well done! The staff worked well together and did so gracefully and happily.
The drinks were well made! The live band was playing good soul music that encourage you to bop and sway while indulging in the atmosphere and your company. Timeless scenery and decorating... England has a sophistication with that that America can't match! A+..... I could stay there forever if I wasn't full from the delicious meal! Easily accessible place I'd visit all the time if I were a local. Thanks for a wonderful evening, all because of an outside conversation with a door staff. You're a wonderful person Justina! A+!

We waited for our cocktails for about 40 minutes. The waitresses were pushy, constantly trying to get us to order more food. I even went to the bar to cancel my order because waiting 40 minutes for cocktails, despite reminding them several times, is simply unacceptable. As soon as I complained and cancelled, the waitress came and asked us to pay for the food we hadn’t even finished yet. Awful! I was very disappointed. One of the cocktails we did receive tasted so bad that my partner couldn’t even drink it.

Before the musicians started playing, we had about an hour and a half to enjoy our food and drinks — but we didn’t enjoy it at all. Once the music began, it was so loud that I couldn’t hear the waitress, my partner, or even myself. It felt more like a nightclub than a blues venue. I was expecting a real blues atmosphere.

I had wanted to visit this place for a long time, but it turned out to be more about showing off than about quality. And it was so expensive!

I would not recommend this place to anyone.

Excellent first time visit! All of the staff were very friendly, welcoming, checked in on us multiple times and said thank you as we left. Service was spot on. Appreciated being given a jug of tap water straight away without even having to ask too. Food was so tasty, we had the pork belly rib, and bacon cheeseburger, both dishes were great but particularly the pork belly rib - I would come back just for that! 😋
Decor was cool and overall nice relaxed atmosphere (we dined around 5:30pm so before it gets busy). Highly recommend and looking forward to our next visit!

Food, drinks, ambience, service - 10/10!! Blues Kitchen is always such a good time and the standard is consistent. Would highly recommend the Popcorn Squid and Buffalo Wings as a starter. Their Brisket Sandwich and Cheeseburger is always a hit as well - perfectly cooked and extremely flavourful. I tried the Salmon for the first time yesterday and it was, as expected, sensational -marinated and cooked to perfection. The staff are always super accommodating which really adds to the experience :)

This restaurant in Shoreditch offers some of the best service I’ve ever received. The atmosphere is lively and the food is delicious. We tried the fried chicken and the seared salmon, but both were a bit under-seasoned for our taste. I highly recommend this place for live music and excellent service. Don’t forget to make a reservation, though!

places.name: Lina Stores Shoreditch - Italian Restaurant & Bar
places.formatted_address: 180 Shoreditch High St, London E1 6HY, UK

reviews.text: I stopped here impromptu on my way elsewhere and was so pleasantly surprised by the level of authenticity in the food and outstanding service.  I haven't had Italian food this wonderful since Italy. Smaller (right-size) portions, a wonderful wine selection, really kind attentive service. This place should not be missed.

Lina Stores is a really good Italian option at reasonable prices. The food is simple but with fresh ingredients and the ambience in the Shoreditch branch is slightly quirky and quaint with its monochromatic pale green interiors. The desserts were super moist and delicious too! Overall, this is a fantastic option for great tasting Italian food at good prices.

There are a few Lina Stores in London with each always guaranteeing a great Italian meal, but the one in Shoreditch boasts a very cool basement bar with excellent cocktail choices. The atmosphere is quite intimate and moody, perfect for a romantic date or a friendly conversation. The food as always was excellent.

PASTA & HIDDEN COCKTAILS 🇮🇹
📍 Shoreditch, London
⭐️ 5/5
💸 ££
🍴Honestly… I’m in love! 😍 We visited the #Shoreditch branch of @linastores, set inside a beautifully restored former bank (yes, with all the charm and grandeur you’d imagine), and it instantly became one of my new favourite date night spots in London✨

We went a little wild with the #Antipasti and it was so worth it:
🫒 #Burrata e Olio d’Oliva – creamy heaven.
🐟 Vitello #Tonnato – MY FAV, so delicate yet packed with flavour.
🍞 #Focaccia al Rosmarino e Sale Marino – so fluffy and salty, a total must.
🦐 #Gamberi Grigliati – grilled prawns that were honestly some of the best I’ve had in London! 🔥

For mains, we went full #pasta mode:
🍅 #Ravioli con Burrata e Salsa di Datterini – huge, soft parcels of joy
🍝 #Pappardelle con Ragù di Salsiccia di Agnello – rich, spicy and comforting

Desserts? Of course!
☕️The #Tiramisù was dreamy
🍮 The #PannaCotta was my personal fave — silky and light!

But wait, there’s more! 👀 We then snuck downstairs into their secret #speakeasy aperitivo bar: @bar___lina 🍸 So mysterious, so chic, and honestly the perfect post-dinner vibe. We were overwhelmed with amazing #cocktail options but the bartender was super helpful and made incredible suggestions.
My top picks:
🍊CONFORMISTA – Adriatico #Amaretto, Cadello 88, Grapefruit, Rooibos
💚BASILICO – Basil-infused #Gin, Mancino Secco, Milk… refreshing and smooth

Truly a 10/10 experience. Delicious food, elegant setting, hidden cocktail bar… the dream cute & sexy date night combo!
I’m a little bit of an Italian food snob, and the green salad, fried artichokes, and pici pasta were all amazing! The staff was really kind, and I felt comfortable dining solo there.

places.name: Lahpet Shoreditch
places.formatted_address: 58 Bethnal Grn Rd, London E1 6JW, UK
places.editorial_summary: An array of small & shared plates in a contemporary setting with lively hanging plants, & full bar.

reviews.text: Absolutely delicious food with friendly stuff. Super nice place to have a lovely evening. The superstar dish for me is the coconut noodles. Cocktails are great as well

BEAUTIFUL SPACE
The interiors are bang on the money, this location has a homely and welcoming and communal feel. The paper menu placemats and beautifully curved reusable branded coolers and bamboo straws, felt intentional, purposeful and reflective of the brand. It's clear I'm in love with the space (the bar stools with backrests sealed the deal for me).

The food, is done well. We ordered a number of dishes so we got a good sample of the menu. It was delish!
The menu is selective without being limiting.

This is a really nice spot. Highly recommended.

Excellent Burmese food in a modern restaurant with good service and ambience! Shared tea leaf salad, papaya salad, hake curry, chicken coconut noodle soup, coconut rice and crème brûlée between three people. All dishes were consistently reasonable in portion, flavoursome and delicious. The crunchy salads and the perfectly cooked fish were my favourites. The chicken noodles were lovely but I wouldn’t have again (personal preference). Highly recommend this place - ticks all the boxes ie enjoyment, quality and value.

Incredible food at a good price - Burmese cuisine is one of the most underrated in my opinion! Pyae was a really helpful and kind waitress, and Min is a terrific head chef! Dishes were super delicious!

This place has the most amazing food. The portions are really good as well. I went here for my birthday and was entirely pleased with the whole experience. I'm definitely going back, I recommend you all give it a try, too.

places.name: The Clove Club
places.formatted_address: Shoreditch Town Hall, 380 Old St, London EC1V 9LT, UK
places.vicinity: Shoreditch Town Hall, 380 Old St, London
places.editorial_summary: Cutting-edge restaurant and bar for innovative British menu using often-overlooked ingredients.

reviews.text: A lovely tasting menu with a few surprises along the way. The extra course of Scottish blue shell lobster was the most memorable, especially the curly noodles in lobster bisque in the 2nd serving. The portion size with the extra course was good.  In fact, most dishes were quite small and light, although understandable for a summer menu, the overall portion could be more generous throughout. The restaurant was situated inside the Shoreditch Town Hall but the interior design was not able to capture the classic elegance of the original architecture. It was more or less a typical London restaurant establishment. Service was prompt and friendly, with a minor error on the bill in the end that the more experienced server admitted the mistake right away and took it to rectify.
My daughter and I had a wonderful meal. The wine and NA pairings were a great compliment to each dish. Stellar dining experience and top notch hospitality. Very much looking forward to returning.

Had the best birthday dinner here.
I have been to many fine dining places before as a former New Yorker and The Clove Club topped a lot of the previous experiences I had.

All dish were experimental and creative but very well balanced in every aspect. There are some dishes with flavors and textures I've never tasted. Overall exquisite!
The service and hospitality was also exceptional. I would definitely recommend The Clove Club to my friends and would love to come back!!! Thank you for completing my perfect birthday celebration.

I had a blast at The Clove Club. The food was fantastic across the board- with some of the highlights being the scallop sashimi,the lamb, the langoustine and the granita. Portions are perfectly sized and the flavors balanced so that you never feel too full and bloated. Excellent selection of wines and a sommelier who's clearly passionate about his trade.  In fact, every member of the staff was courteous and attentive while leaving enough space for the guests to feel relaxed.

Truly, a pillar of the London fine dining scene.

Be respect to the most kindness, warm and focus on detailed services from Mr Pablo, Daniel and the team.

And for sure, the atmosphere, the taste of the each section, as I also I want to highlight the best dishes “Raw Orkney Scallop”, excellent excellent excellent.

Definitely will recommended to our friends if drop by London. And we must come back later.

places.name: Camino Shoreditch
places.editorial_summary: Colourful, eclectic venue with a relaxed ambiance for inventive Spanish tapas and interesting wines.

reviews.text: The food was generally very good, but the mushroom coca was truly unique and special — the best mushrooms I’ve ever tasted. The succulent pig was a little on the dry side, but everything else was excellent. The service was outstanding, and the atmosphere was beautiful, with wonderfully tasteful décor.
Firstly, the service was top notch. Lovely, friendly staff. The food was as good as I’ve had in Barcelona. They even got it out to me in a couple of minutes as I was in a rush. 10/10 will be back.

Ended up going twice on two consecutive nights! Really nice tapas, selection wasn't huge but everything I had was really well done. Ended up trying both the tomato bread, tortilla, ox cheek, flattened pork, croquettes, bravas, padron peppers and the cheesecake. Everything was really tasty. Cheesecake in particular was incredible - creamy but not too sweet. Prices were about what I expect for the area. Service from Sergio and the other guy (sorry didnt catch his name!) was really friendly and attentive. Will 100% be back when I'm in the area again.

Went to Camino a while back for a bit of dinner with an old pal and it was a really enjoyable experience. The place was quiet (which is why I’ve only given 4 stars for atmosphere) but the food was great, the wine was delicious and the over experience was top notch.

Highly recommend Camino if you are looking for somewhere for good quality tapas that’s centre to the City or Shoreditch

Really good tapas dishes with decent portions. We had 6 plates between the 2 of us and that was enough to fill us up. It was relatively quiet as it was a sat afternoon but would expect it to be busy in the evenings. Would definitely recommend

places.name: BRAT Restaurant
places.editorial_summary: There’s strong Basque influences on the menu of this rustic Spanish spot with open wood fire grill.

reviews.text:
The restaurant had been on my list for years but I did not know they got a Michelin star in 2025.

Food was amazing from start to finish. With some Tartare, Mussels toast and Pigeon skewer to begin with.
And then some Dover Sole, Mallard, vegetables and potatoes. All that with a side of bread and butter. And a cheesecake finish.

Service was great and they explained everything. Wine list was also great with lots of options (including Sherry and Dessert wine)

I highly recommend the place

Beautiful restaurant with highly imaginative cooking. The only areas where it comes up a little bit short are, first, value for money - the portions are small considering their prices, and the pricing on the grilled fish and meat is particularly dear. Second, the dining room is packed in a little bit tight and there is very little room to manoeuvre, once you arrive and are sat you pretty much have to stay put as the dining room is very dense and very busy. The vegetable dishes were the star of the show and if I were to do it all over again I would order only vegetarian dishes and a bottle of wine. Standout items were the red peppers cooked for 24 hours in sherry and olive oil, the skewer of squid and sobrassada, the squash with seasonal greens and yogurt, and the chocolate sorbet with plum. I’d booked the restaurant for a special occasion, and besides acknowledging that from their notes nothing was done about it including not providing the table by the kitchen as I had requested and they’d promised to do. Overall glad we went and we did enjoy the vibe and the overall experience.

Excellent and attentive service. Super friendly and engaging staff who take the time to explain the menu and story behind it : thank you for all the dishes and wines recommandations!

Lunch was delicious from start to finish: a special mention for the Dover sole & grilled veggies and sparkling white wine👌🏾

Loved watching the big open kitchen work while enjoying my lunch, as well as seeing the other options ordered by fellow guests. A must try when in London. I will definitely come back, MERCI !

Mix bag feeling after my first visit and considering the price point and the 1 Michelin star rating.
Quality of ingredients is great and flavours are clean and strong. However, food was like warm and a very long wait between starters and mains. This was also the case for the 2 tables next to us and even the waiter was advising other tables to place their order all together as there will be long delays in serving the main. So it feels like a regular issue.
Service was great and attentive. When commenting on the delays, they positively reacted.
Atmosphere is more one of a gastro pub than a Michelin star. Tables too close to each other, you are literally touching elbows with your neighbours. I would also expect a proper napkin at this price level and not a paper one. Cutlery and china are basic.
Maybe the venue in Hackney delivers more buck for money but I was not really impressed here. Feels like they are squeezing the maximum juice from their reputation here and rely on tourist to fill their seats.

Wonderful grilled bread and wood pigeon. Very difficult to book though. Tables were too close to one another to be fully comfortable and servers were always behind or above my head trying to get cutlery to serve other tables as I was seated next to the cultery station. Nonetheless, seeing the kitchen in action was amazing.

places.name: Rochelle Canteen
places.editorial_summary: Cafe/restaurant in bike shed of school turned arts and media complex serving short, modern menu.

reviews.text:
This is a lovely restaurant tucked away behind a wall. You need to be buzzed in to eat here. What this means, of course, is that you have to be intentional to eat here, and make a reservation. It is worth it.

It was a lovely day, so we ate outside under the pergola filled with ripening grapes. For starters, we had the cod roe dip with fresh baby radishes and absolutely delicious tomato salad topped with feta. The tomatoes were fresh and juicy, and it was just a lovely summer dish. For an entrees, one of us had the tuna with white beans. The fish was perfectly cooked, and the portion was substantial. The rest of us had two of the specials of the day. I had the crispy lamb ribs, which were quite an unusual preparation, but they were very tender and tasty. The wagyu beef entree was sensational. Perfectly cooked beef served with horseradish and some spicy greens. It was truly a lovely meal.

They have several cocktails plus a nice list of wines by the glass.

The staff is great, and the ambience very calm and beautiful. Beautiful. I highly recommend this lovely restaurant.

The food was great with good ingredients. The service was excellent and very quick. The restaurant was in a covered area which was nice but would have been nicer in the outside garden area in the summertime. Overall was a bit pricey but the quality of the food was good. Portion sizes were normal

Been wanting to come here for a while now.
Food was mostly good. Cod was cooked perfectly, short rib was a beautiful cut in a delicious gravy. The lamb croquettes were a highlight!

Sides were a bit undercooked for my liking. Tough cabbage and potatoes. Wine was excellent and service mostly good.
One waiter would just dump our plates on the table without talking us through the dishes. Maybe that's not their policy but it's a nice touch to be reminded of the elements.
Otherwise, our main waitress was excellent.

Rochelle is certainly one of the institutions in East London and I have been trying many times to visit.
I left very disappointed.
The food was ok, good products but nothing to rave about. My main garnish was stone cold and the steak cooking instructions was not as requested. The service was so slow, although they do ask you to place your order within 15 minutes of your booking to get the tables back, but didn’t deliver speedy delivery.
That’s a shame as the setup is great, a little oasis in the middle of London.

Delicious food with delicate and amazing flavours - loved the scallops, the mussels, the courgettes and the pumpkin soup (bread was a bit disappointing as it was cold and the butter was hard to spread - excellent to dip in the sauces of the dishes though). Excellent wine list. Servers were friendly and attentive. The garden area is really beautiful on a sunny day. Will definitely be back!

places.name: The Light Bar & Dining
places.formatted_address: 233 Shoreditch High St, London E1 6PJ, UK
places.editorial_summary: Converted warehouse with beer garden and roof terrace, Modern European dining and weekend DJs.

reviews.text:
We booked the Loft at The Light Bar this weekend to host our wedding drinks and couldn’t be happier with the top tier service we received!
Great communications and explanation throughout. Excellent food & bar service and very grateful for the little extra mile they went on countless details of hosting a wedding party night for 90 approx people.
They provided ample amount of the amenities needed, kept me updated throughout a smooth running night. Fantastic staff and service. Thanks team!

I was there once and I liked the experience! We were 3 girls, ended up at The Light Bar on a Friday evening. We ordered cocktails and I loved mine! The service was good, the staff is nice and the space is spacious. I do think that it might be also a good venue for celebrations or events. There was a live DJ playing and he really nailed it. Although it is a bit loudy, I really liked the place and you can still find a place to chill and hear each other somewhere upstairs. Recommended!

The Light Bar hosted my VIP Dinner for women in my professional network in London. From the moment of booking, the staff were so helpful and communication and planning was spot on. We did a group set menu and the food was spectacular, so delicious and very generous servings with wonderful fresh, rich flavours. They kindly catered to dietary requirements and the service was impeccable - they really took care of us and we were all super impressed. They accommodated us moving to an outdoor table given it was such a beautiful balmy June evening and it was truly magical to relax and connect. Would absolutely recommend it for any corporate or personal event - it was an amazing venue.

Along with cocktails, the group set menu was absolutely spectacular starting with burrata and peppers, salmon fennel citrus salad, trout and crème fraiche, flatbreads both plain and topped with olive and tomato, and crispy chickpea hummus. Next came shared mains - delicious hispy cabbage on ratatouille, basil pesto baked orzo with rocket and Parmesan, and a baby chicken with gravy and greens. And of course we squeezed in the mountain of crispy churros with chocolate pots because dessert obviously goes into another tube.

I was truly blown away by the fresh flavour-packed dishes, perfect location, and wonderful service. I’m still dreaming of that heavenly trout dip…

the burger is decent but not really really good. the menu got limited choices. service is alright but it took a while to get a pint from them. dj music is a bit too loud at dinner time. dont really know the positioning of this restaurant / bar. it is below average if you consider it as a restaurant. it is ok if you treat it as a bar. probably not visit again in the near future.

Nice little after work hang out spot, but I would definitely book a table if you can, especially if you’re coming in a bigger group. Margaritas were fantastic and the food was even better!!! I really recommend the flatbread and they have loads of different toppings for it. As soon as they closed the retractable roof, it became very cosy and intimate. Also good music!

places.name: Barrio - Shoreditch
places.formatted_address: 141-143 Shoreditch High St, London E1 6JE, UK
places.editorial_summary: Vibrant destination serving tapas-style food & cocktails, plus late night club with DJs.

reviews.text: Fun place with amazing tacos. We went on a friday evening and it was happy hour (woot woot) cocktails were refreshing on a hot day like that.. the tacos were delicious! Music was great. Overall a good experience and would definitely bring more people with us next time.

Food was not too bad, it came and it was already cold. Tacos are cheap and small, fries too expensive for what you actually get.
We were also asked to leave a 5 star review and mention Mohit for drinks (who didn’t serve us either), we did but he never came back! Spoiler alert Mohit: you can update the review after submitting it! 😜

I stood at the host stand with 3 people chatting for a while before I was acknowledged. The bar experience was the same. The “Tommy’s Margarita” was so sweet and gut-rot worthy tbh. & the tacos were SO disappointing. Literally krafts singles  (as pictured) & tasteless.
Atmosphere & decor were lovely but otherwise so truly disappointing.
& having to pay a service charge while I’m ordering from a QR code.

Barrio Shoreditch was such a fun vibe. Great spot for tacos and cocktails with a proper party atmosphere. Music was lively, the decor was colourful, and the staff were great. Perfect place to start a night out, definitely going back.

Unfortunately a really disappointing service on a birthday night out. Went to order drinks at the bar and had to struggle to get the two free bartenders attention then finally ordered but our bartender slowly stopped and took shots with another bartender instead while we waited.
The jug was filled with ice and barely garnished which the official instagram had led us to believe was part of service.
The bar is very pretty and the drinks were okay but disappointed how customers seem to be a hindrance to staff

places.name: 34 Mayfair
places.formatted_address: 34 Grosvenor Sq, S Audley St, London W1K 2HD, UK
places.vicinity: 34 Grosvenor Sq, S Audley St, London
places.editorial_summary: British game and world meats cooked on an imported Argentinian grill in art deco-inspired brasserie.

reviews.text:
Went here on day 1 of our London trip for anniversary dinner.

Fancy interior and utensils.
Food was delicious, particularly hummus and broccoli.

Staff were friendly and kind and they also have live music.

Definitely recommend for dates/friends gathering/family dinner.

This place is amazing. We had outdoor seating which I highly recommend if the weather is nice. My wife had the lemon sole, which was the special of the day and I had the ribeye. Both were very good, but the real winner here were the desserts. We had the chocolate fondant tart and the homemade donuts. I'm not sure how both of them can rank in our top 10 desserts ever, but they do. We're in town for a week and are already planning to go back for dessert again. Highly recommended!
And a word about our server, Remus - he was fantastic. Very attentive, helpful with suggestions and quick to clear dirty plates. While we were there a lady at the table next to us (seating is very close) complained to him about a menu item that was not available. He responded apologetically but she wouldn't take no for an answer she continued on and on and made mention of how betrayed she felt and that she felt like she was lied to by the receptionist she spoke with earlier in the day. Remus maintained his composure and continued to respond kindly to her. The situation was clearly beyond Remus' control. Much respect to him for handling the situation with grace.

Today, we had lunch at the 34 Mayfair in London. The food was not that great but not bad either. However, the portion sizes were very, very small. The octopus was minuscule. Avoiding gluten was impossible no matter how carefully one orders. The matcha-based non-alcoholic drink was quite disappointing – it was overpowered with lemon and didn’t taste like it had any matcha. Additionally, the salad looked limp and the leaves didn’t seem very fresh. Also, all bread was sweet. Riffle with chicken tasted good but the coating on the chicken didn’t stick well and the croffle was too sweet to be in that dish. The sole was good. Overall, it was just an okay meal, not really a great experience.
An average fine dining. My favorite Mac & cheese. Others liked the steak but we all agreed that the burrata salad wasn’t a great choice.
One of my best dinner experience in London. Definitely coming back. My wife loved it so much. The food is top notch and the staffs are awesome.

reviews.author_name: Samira Hotel, Food, Travel& Beauty Expert
reviews.text:
Breathtaking atmosphere — a true visual spectacle.
The interior at Bacchanalia is absolutely stunning. The ceiling installations with the winged horses and the opulent garlands are nothing short of mesmerizing — it feels like dining inside a living artwork. The decor alone makes the visit unforgettable.

The only downside was the wait. Even with a reservation, we had to wait quite a while for our table, which was a bit frustrating considering how busy it was. However, the staff handled it well and offered us an aperitif, which was a classy touch and made the delay more bearable.

Once seated, everything turned around — the food was outstanding. The flavors, presentation, and quality were exactly what you’d expect from a place of this level. Service throughout the meal was warm and well-coordinated.

Bacchanalia really does feel more like an experience than just dinner. The space is dramatic — Roman statues, rich colors, and a kind of grandeur that makes you pause when you walk in. It’s bold and theatrical, but somehow still inviting.

The food was excellent across the board. Fresh seafood, perfectly made pasta, and a wine list that clearly had thought put into it. Service was attentive without being too much, which I appreciated.

The star for me, though, was dessert — the Medusa pavlova (pictured). It’s almost too beautiful to touch, a sculpted meringue surrounded by cream, berries, and coulis. But once you dig in, the flavors are as good as the presentation — light, crisp, tangy, and sweet in just the right balance.

The food here is decent but not outstanding — I’d give it about 6.5 out of 10. Service is around 6 out of 10 as well. The atmosphere, however, is excellent — a solid 10 out of 10. Overall, if you’re coming mainly for the ambiance, it’s worth visiting. But if you’re looking for really great food, this might not be the place for you.

Extremely disappointing experience. The food fell far below expectations—what was meant to be “truffle tagliatelle” ended up tasting like a fish soup. The pasta itself was overcooked and mushy, the sauce thin and watery instead of creamy, and there was no hint of truffle at all. Easily the worst truffle pasta I’ve ever had, despite trying similar dishes in top restaurants across Dubai, Doha, Marbella, Paris, and London when the waiter
Tried to make it seem as if I wouldn’t know what good truffle pasta was supposed to taste like
The restaurant’s interior is undeniably beautiful, with elegant décor that raises your expectations, but sadly the food did not match the setting. The starters were average at best, and the main course was a complete letdown. For the price charged, the quality simply isn’t justified—I left both hungry and annoyed.

Adding to the disappointment, TikTok suggested there would be entertainment—music or a show—but the atmosphere was completely flat. On a Saturday night, the place was lifeless, and we were told to leave at midnight when it closed.

Overall, a waste of money and time. I won’t be returning, and I wouldn’t recommend booking here.

This place is… something. Lavish refurbishment? Yes. Tacky and remarkable in equal measure? Also yes, though not always in a good way. We came for a friend’s birthday lunch, having booked a set menu online that included three courses, a welcome drink, and a cocktail. Sadly, what we got was a juice shot, no cocktail, and a bizarre negotiation with staff to honour what we’d already paid for. The waiter admitted the deal wasn’t running anymore but said a manager might approve it. We eventually got our drinks—after pleading—and overheard the same thing happening to the table next to us.

The food was fine, the live opera we barely caught, and the senior staff were dismissive at best. Host team and servers were lovely, but the overall experience left a bad taste.

It’s the sort of place where the decor’s louder than the service. Not awful, but wouldn’t rush back.

places.name: COYA Mayfair
places.editorial_summary: Upmarket venue with 3 open kitchens, serving Peruvian sharing plates, char-grill dishes and ceviche.

reviews.text:
Beautiful restaurant if you are looking for something special.  The service and attention was refined and not overwhelming. The sommelier was knowledgeable and eager to help find that right wine.
The food was cleverly presented and eye pleasing.
That had several dining option which was very much appreciated. Set menu pair with drinks or order a la cart
